title: Jared Goff: I love it when the vultures come out
summary: The first two weeks of the Lions' season haven't painted the picture of a team firing on all cylinders.
full_text: The first two weeks of the Lions' season haven't painted the picture of a team firing on all cylinders. Week 1 saw them give up a 21-0 lead to the Saints before rallying for a win in overtime and they fell down by 21 points during a 41-31 loss in Buffalo in Week 2. That's led to plenty of doubts about the team's ability to contend at a high level this season, but quarterback Jared Goff said that is just fine with him because he thinks it will bring the best out of the team. "I'm excited to get back home and play in front of our fans for sure, but you love when the vultures start coming out ," Goff said. "Guys' character really emerges and I know our guys in this locker room and you can see those guys stand tall and be who they are. Stand in the fire, take the shots and fight right through it. . . . We're in a great place. Excited to get back in front of our fans." A win over the Jets this Sunday would keep the vultures at bay, but a loss would probably make Goff and company a little less comfortable with how they're situated heading into October.
author: Josh Alper

title: Marvin Harrison Jr.: My process won't change whether I get 0 catches or 10 catches
summary: Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has only caught one pass through two games this season.
full_text: Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr. has only caught one pass through two games this season. But he doesn't think he needs to change anything. Asked if he's losing confidence, Harrison said he knows he's preparing the right way, and that's all that matters. "Does your confidence come from results or does your confidence come from your process?" Harrison said, via ESPN. "And I think for me it comes from my process. So, my process isn’t going to change whether I get zero catches or 10 catches. I'm going to still do the same thing week in and week out, Monday through Saturday to prepare myself for games. So, I think that's where I have a lot of my confidence comes from. And obviously you want to have more of an impact in the game, but I think confidence really has to come from preparation more than anything." Harrison said no one player is ever solely responsible for his own production. "It's definitely a combination of a lot of things," Harrison said. "For my route tree getting down the field, you need a lot of things to go right. You need the right coverage, you need protection to hold up, you need me to run a great route, you need obviously Jacoby to make the right pass and make the right read. So, I feel like it's never one person's fault for anybody's success or lack thereof, really. So, I think it's always a combination of a bunch of things and whether that's a lack of success or success in general." Harrison's comments may be true, and yet there's no denying that he has been a disappointment as the fourth overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft. His rookie year was only OK, he declined in his second season, and through two games in Year 3 he has gone into a steeper decline. Harrison's process may not change, but something has to change.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Darius Slayton: Daniel Jones and I see field similarly, expect that to work well for us
summary: Darius Slayton was watching last Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs, which meant he saw Colts wideout Alec Pierce leave the game after aggravating a heel injury.
full_text: '' Darius Slayton was watching last Sunday night's game between the Colts and Chiefs, which meant he saw Colts wideout Alec Pierce leave the game after aggravating a heel injury. Slayton said on Wednesday that he "wasn't cheering for that," but he knew that Pierce's injury might create an opportunity for him to land his first job since being released by the Giants this summer. Not only did the Colts have an immediate need for receiver help, they also have Slayton's former Giants teammate Daniel Jones as their quarterback. That history likely played a role in Slayton signing with the Colts this week and he said he expects to get right back into a groove with the quarterback. "Really enjoyed playing alongside him ," Slayton said, via the team's website. "He's a good quarterback. He's smart. He can spin it. . . . Philosophically, I think we see the field pretty similarly, and that's something that worked well for us in the past. And I expect it to work well for us going forward." Pierce averaged more than 20 yards a catch in each of the last two seasons, but Slayton has not been that kind of wideout during his time in the NFL so the Colts will have to adapt their offense to the players available as they try to find their first win of the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Mike Vrabel, Drake Maye address the balance between decisiveness and recklessness
summary: After a Week 2 win over the Steelers, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel didn't want to have his Sunday "ruined" by questions about the performance of quarterback Drake Maye.
full_text: After a Week 2 win over the Steelers, Patriots coach Mike Vrabel didn't want to have his Sunday " ruined " by questions about the performance of quarterback Drake Maye. Vrabel also didn't seem to want to have his Wednesday ruined by them, either. Asked during his midweek press conference whether the pendulum for Maye "maybe swung too far back in the other direction" from being overly aggressive in Week 1 against the Seahawks (when he had three game-killing fourth-quarter interceptions) to being too careful in Week 2 against the Steelers, Vrabel didn't seem to be thrilled with the inquiry. "Again, these are questions that I would like to answer on Monday," Vrabel said. "I think I was willing to do that. The focus has got to be on Jacksonville and our performance. Whether it’s the pendulum — it’s being decisive in everyone's play, but it’s certainly magnified with the quarterback. So being decisive, believing in what you see. Again, that’s what we ask all our players to do is prepare to try to play fast and aggressively and make great decisions. So, yeah, we could always say, 'Man, we should have let that one rip,' or 'We’ve got to make a better decision.' Ultimately, it’s his responsibility to be able to distribute the football as quickly and decisively as possible in the places that it’s supposed to go, continue not to force things and try to just create a next play on every single play." Maye's midweek press conference opened with a question regarding the importance of not overthinking and playing freely on the field. "One of the best things about getting new chances every week is having to let the other ones go," Maye said. "That's one of the best things about this sport and playing this position. You’ve got to let plays go, and you want to be attacking the next play, learning from the ones in the past and getting after the next one. So, I definitely think, this job, it's hard to play this position when you’re thinking about a lot of different things, and you are going to be regardless. It's going to be natural to think about motions, fronts, defenses, what our guys are doing, route concept and what they’re doing versus the play we have up. So, just thinking and trying to be instinctive. That's one of the best things I learned in college is to be instinctive and try to play as fast as you can back there." Maye later was asked about Vrabel's comments on the importance of decisiveness and believing what he sees. "I think that goes back to playing instinctive, seeing it, trusting what I see in practice, trusting the decisions I’m making out there on the field," Maye said. "I’ve never shied away from trusting something and letting it rip. So, just knowing what I’m seeing, seeing it in front of the guys, and at the same time, giving our guys a chance to make a play. Sometimes, when you do that, you end up forcing the football into decisions that you maybe want back by trying to give your guys a chance to go make a play. So, realizing that, and also keeping the chains moving is just as important to get those next chances to push the ball down the field." Through two games in 2026, something is off. To the extent passer rating matters, Maye's has fallen from 113.5 in 2025 to 63.1 in 2026. He had 31 touchdown passes and eight interceptions last year. This year, he has one touchdown pass and four interceptions. With upcoming games at Jacksonville and Buffalo, it's an opportunity to turn the clock back a year. If not, an ugly early-season narrative could start taking root.
author: Mike Florio

title: Kurt Warner: I played through a dislocated left elbow, Jayden Daniels can if he wants to
summary: Warner injured his left elbow in 2007 and returned the next week wearing a large brace.
full_text: Hall of Fame quarterback Kurt Warner says Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels could play through the left elbow injury he suffered on Sunday. Warner, who now appears on ESPN , described suffering the same injury in 2007 and not missing a game. “I suffered the exact same injury back in ’07, and I played the next week," Warner said. "I braced it up, obviously a couple shots along the way, I had to hand the football off with my right hand in both directions, but this to me is something, because it's the left arm, if he wants to play through that, and get back out there and help his team, I believe he can. It's not going to be one of those things that affects the throwing part of things. Does it affect his movement, does it affect his running or some of the things they want to do by design? Maybe, but I do believe this is something he can come back from. Because it's the left arm, I don't think it's something we worry about long term and go, 'Should we extend this guy, because he's had this type of injury twice?' I believe it's something he can play through." Warner said that as a player, his mentality would be to do everything he can to help his team win. "I can brace it up and go," Warner said. "I don't care about all that stuff. Let me go out there and play, I want to be out there with my guys as opposed to thinking about this a year or two down the road." Warner suffered his left elbow injury in Week 6 of 2007 when he was sacked by Panthers defensive end Julius Peppers. Warner missed the rest of that game, and when the injury was initially diagnosed he was expected to miss more time, but instead he played in Week 7, wearing a large brace on his left elbow, and started every game for the Cardinals the rest of the season. Warner played well down the stretch and was named the starter in 2008 after starting 2007 as the backup to Matt Leinart, and in 2008 Warner led the Cardinals to the Super Bowl. What's unknown is whether Warner is correct to call his injury "the exact same injury" that Daniels had. Daniels' left elbow injury may be more severe, and it may not be feasible for him to play, even with a heavy brace on his left elbow. Warner displayed incredible toughness, but that doesn't necessarily make it the right decision for Daniels.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Justin Herbert disputes perception of lack of vocal leadership
summary: Something has kept Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert from fulfilling a skillset that has had coach Jim Harbaugh proclaim that Herbert will be regarded as the best to ever play the game.
full_text: Something has kept Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert from fulfilling a skillset that has had coach Jim Harbaugh proclaim that Herbert will be regarded as the best to ever play the game. The disconnect between talent and production has become more pronounced in the early days of the 2026 season, given that the Chargers have lost a pair of home games to two of the worst teams in the league in 2025. On Wednesday, Herbert's midweek press conference included questions about a potential increase in vocal leadership. In response to the first — regarding the possible need for vocal leadership in advance of the Week 3 game at Buffalo — Herbert bristled . "I think that would imply that there's no need for vocal leadership before this week," Herbert said, via Kris Rhim of ESPN. "I think every week is a super important week for us and it's a great opportunity for us to go play football again and correct the things that we made mistakes on last week and keep pushing forward." Herbert interrupted the second question on the subject. "I don't think there's a lack of vocal leadership at all," Herbert said. "So, I'm going to stop you right there and say that it's very present. I don't think anyone is panicked or worried because that's not going to be the sentiment. It's moving on to the next play and understand that we're close, we've made mistakes, how do we fix it?" Herbert reiterated his expectation that there will be no panic, as the team stares at the possibility that 0-2 will become 0-3 and, based on the upcoming schedule (at Seahawks, Broncos, at Chiefs), possibly 0-6 at the bye. Regardless, something is missing. And it it's not an issue of Herbert's talent, it's something else. Perhaps the players around him aren't good enough. Perhaps he's not doing enough to get more out of them. Perhaps the odd-couple pairing of Harbaugh and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is a work in progress that has yet to make enough progress. A win will change everything. But the team looked flat and overmatched in two straight games the Chargers should have won. Now comes the gauntlet, and there's a chance the hole will get deeper and deeper with each passing week.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders push back on narrative they abandoned Jayden Daniels
summary: Commanders franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels was injured on the final play of the first half.
full_text: Commanders franchise quarterback Jayden Daniels was injured on the final play of the first half. As team medical personnel worked on his dislocated left elbow, Daniels' teammates were seen on the Fox broadcast walking by him toward the locker room. Commanders players pushed back against the social media narrative that they abandoned their quarterback. " It’s bullshit what people are saying," Washington left tackle Brandon Coleman said, via John Keim of ESPN. "Jay's our guy, and he's been our guy. There's no malice behind it." Many players stayed on the sideline watching Daniels being attended to, per Keim, and many returned to his side after trainers popped Daniels' elbow back in place. Coach Dan Quinn said what actually happened was the "opposite" of the narrative that grew from Fox's short clip. "When the half is over, the referees are saying, 'Man, I can't delay the half. They can't stay on the field,' The players were like, 'No, we want to stay,'" Quinn said. "So it's just the opposite of that. They were gutted. They love this guy. So halftime was hard and emotional in that space." Coleman and lineman Josh Conerly Jr. were the last players to leave for the locker room, along with Quinn and backup quarterbacks Marcus Mariota and Athan Kaliakmanis. "All that stuff is ridiculous," tight end Ben Sinnott said. "As far as the love and brotherhood we have for Jayden, it's really strong. We've seen how hard he worked to get to where he's been. "It was a weird situation. People were trying to figure out what's going on, and they wanted to give the trainers space to do it. You don't want to crowd the guy. Obviously, guys are taking a step back and giving him space, praying, and we all came back. "All that stuff is nonsense."
author: Charean Williams

title: Case Keenum ready to start for Bears if needed
summary: The Bears haven't named Case Keenum the starter for Monday night's game against the Eagles, but he could be the next man up.
full_text: The Bears haven't named Case Keenum the starter for Monday night's game against the Eagles, but he could be the next man up. Keenum was the only quarterback on the active roster to practice Wednesday, with Caleb Williams rehabbing a hamstring injury and Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol. Miller Moss, an undrafted rookie on the Bears' practice squad, took the backup reps to Keenum. Keenum has started 66 games but none since Dec. 24, 2023, against the Browns. That was also the last game he saw action. " I feel very prepared ," Keenum said, via Courtney Cronin of ESPN. "It's what I do every week. It's what I've done for a long time. I've backed up a long time in this league. If my name's called, I'm excited to be out there." Keenum, 38, has played for eight different teams since entering the NFL in 2012. He is 3-0 as a starter against Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio. Keenum has thrown for 15,175 yards and 79 touchdowns. Coach Ben Johnson, formerly the Lions' offensive coordinator, has never called plays for a backup quarterback , and both Jared Goff and Caleb Williams were No. 1 overall picks. Keenum was an undrafted free agent but with experience. "He's been a baller from the day he was born from what I can tell," Johnson said. "He's got that way about him. He's got a knack. His teammates gravitate to him. I think that's a good starting point for a quarterback. And of course he's up there in years a little bit, but that experience has really paid off for him. He sees the game the same way we do. I think he accelerates through his progressions, because he's seen so many things over the course of his time. He's been in so many different offenses. "So in a lot of ways, he might be a step slower than he was when he first entered the league, and yet his mind is going so fast it helps catch him on up. And he's playing as good of football as he probably has his entire career, is what he'd tell you."
author: Charean Williams

title: Jacoby Brissett: No one has lost confidence in Marvin Harrison Jr.
summary: Marvin Harrison Jr. hasn't been the wide receiver the Cardinals thought they were getting when they drafted him fourth overall in 2024.
full_text: Marvin Harrison Jr. hasn't been the wide receiver the Cardinals thought they were getting when they drafted him fourth overall in 2024. That's something everyone can agree. The Cardinals, though, are pushing back against the narrative surrounding Harrison's slow start to 2026. A viral video , viewed more than 18 million times, started the discussion about Harrison's effort level. Other videos have since questioned whether Harrison is giving 100 percent. Quarterback Jacoby Brissett and coach Mike LaFleur defended Harrison on Wednesday. “When you talk about his work ethic and you talk about him showing up and being engaged in the meetings and then going out on the field and giving 110 percent and being the Marv we all know he is, that hasn’t changed ,” Brissett said, via Tyler Drake of Arizona Sports. “Nobody’s lost confidence in Marv. The hard part as a young player is the noise from the outside telling you what they expect from you and the things of that nature. Does Marv want the ball? Yes. Do we understand that he wants the ball? Yes. Is it only Week 2? Yes. . . . At some point, the tide will change. When? We don’t know yet. Hopefully soon.” Harrison has seen four targets, with one catch for 33 yards this season. LaFleur was asked on Monday about Harrison jogging through routes. “I don’t see it that way. I think his running style is different from some other people’s,” LaFleur said. “If that’s people’s narrative on him, that’s fine, but I know his teammates don’t feel that way.” LaFleur doubled down Wednesday. "In between those walls, Marv is Marv,” he said. “He’s attacking it every single day like he always does, just like his teammates do. I appreciate the way he goes about his business.” As for whether Harrison’s run-blocking needs to improve, LaFleur said everyone’s “efforts need to improve.” Dan Graziano of ESPN talked to league executives who wondered whether the Cardinals will shop Harrison before the trade deadline. The Texans are among the teams that could be in the market for help at the position.
author: Charean Williams

title: Antonio Brown plans to take plea deal in attempted murder case
summary: Former NFL receiver Antonio Brown will not be going to prison for attempted murder.
full_text: Former NFL receiver Antonio Brown will not be going to prison for attempted murder. Via David Fischer of the Associated Press, Brown plans to accept a plea deal. He'll plead guilty to a lesser charge and serve no time. Per the report, attorney Mark Eiglarsh said Brown plans to plead no contest to aggravated assault on September 30. He will be sentenced to probation and the adjudication will be withheld. That prevents Brown from being regarded as a convicted felon. It means that Brown will be pleading no contest to a felony. He originally faced up to 30 years in prison for an incident that occurred at a celebrity boxing match in May 2025. Brown allegedly grabbed a handgun from a security officer and fired two shots at a man who allegedly had attacked Brown. Brown had left the country after the incident. He was eventually apprehended and returned to the U.S. to face the charges. “This was not an easy decision,” Eiglarsh said in a statement issued Wednesday. “Antonio believes in his innocence. He believes strongly in his Stand Your Ground defense, and he believes he would ultimately prevail at trial. But when prosecutors put an offer on the table that transforms a potential decades-long prison sentence into a significantly reduced charge and probation, there was simply no way he could reasonably turn it down.” Brown is eligible for enshrinement in the Hall of Fame in 2027. Off-field issues aren't supposed to be considered. It remains to be seen how the newly reconfigured Hall of Fame voting panel will handle his candidacy. A 12-year veteran, Brown earned first-team All-Pro status in four straight seasons. He qualified for the Pro Bowl seven times. Brown finished his career with 928 catches for 12,291 yards and 83 touchdowns. That puts him at 28th, 28th, and (with Travis Kelce's next touchdown catch) 28th on the all-time list. Which could make it hard to get him in, even without considering the off-field issues. Especially in light of the various disruptions he created for the Steelers, Raiders, Patriots, and Buccaneers.
author: Mike Florio

title: Graham Bensinger issues statement regarding Mike Macdonald interview
summary: Graham Bensinger's recent interview with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald made headlines not just for its content but for how the content was obtained — making Bensinger himself part of the story.
full_text: ' Graham Bensinger's recent interview with Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald made headlines not just for its content but for how the content was obtained — making Bensinger himself part of the story. As a result, Bensinger posted the following statement on Twitter: "Due to ongoing media requests for comment, I want to clarify the timeline surrounding a portion of our recent interview with Mike Macdonald that has received attention this week. "The complete Mike Macdonald interview, including the conversation now at issue, was provided to Seahawks PR last Wednesday, September 16 — five days before it was published on YouTube Monday. During that time, no concern was raised about the exchange, and we were never asked to remove it. For the last couple of years, our typical practice with long-form interview releases has been to include some of the pre-interview conversation. "Coach Macdonald reached out to me directly yesterday morning expressing concern. I immediately told him we would remove that portion, and we did. Unfortunately, it had already been clipped from our interview by online outlets and circulated elsewhere. I told Coach that, in hindsight, I regretted allowing that exchange to be included and that it was my error in judgment. "I have tremendous respect for Coach. We spent significant time together in Seattle, and I came away impressed not only by what he has accomplished in such a short period of time, but by the person he is. The last thing I want is for one exchange to overshadow that story. I also have great respect for Sean Payton, whom I had the opportunity to profile previously." It will be interesting to see whether the Seahawks agree that the full conversation, including the segment regarding the 2024 brouhaha with the Broncos, was sent to them on September 16. Also, it feels like Bensinger is opting to blame the Seahawks for not spotting an interaction that, as Macdonald has said, was never meant to be aired. Besides, why was Bensinger giving the thing to the Seahawks in advance anyway? This isn't Hard Knocks ; it's an independent interview that does not need to be reviewed or approved by the subject of the interview before publication. And while the situation has helped remind everyone that Graham Bensinger continues to operate in an increasingly crowded media space, this specific incident could complicate his efforts to attract willing participants from the NFL ecosystem for future sit-down interviews.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bills WR DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited; WR Keon Coleman (ankle) did not practice
summary: Last Thursday night, Bills receiver DJ Moore left the home opener against the Lions with a shoulder injury.
full_text: Last Thursday night, Bills receiver DJ Moore left the home opener against the Lions with a shoulder injury. On the first full day of practice in advance of the Week 3 home game against the Chargers, Moore made a move toward returning. Moore was listed as practicing on a limited basis. Given the very broad nature of the "limited" category, it's hard to know whether that means he'll be good to go in four days. Also injured from the Buffalo receiving corps is Keon Coleman. He did not practice on Wednesday, with an ankle injury. The Bills also were missing a pair of starting defensive tackles. Ed Oliver didn't practice due to the hip injury that made him a late scratch on Thursday night. Defensive tackle T.J. Sanders underwent an appendectomy on Tuesday night. In Week 1, Moore had five catches for 100 yards and a touchdown in the win over the Texans. He had no catches in his 23 snaps from Week 2. Coleman had one catch for one yard in Week 1, and six catches for 63 yards on six targets in Week 2.
author: Mike Florio

title: George Pickens is "happy" despite nine catches for 68 yards through two games
summary: In a contract season, Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens is looking for an encore to his 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns last season.
full_text: In a contract season, Cowboys wide receiver George Pickens is looking for an encore to his 93 receptions for 1,429 yards and nine touchdowns last season. He has only nine catches for 68 yards through two games, with two drops. CeeDee Lamb leads the team with 13 receptions for 197 yards and three touchdowns. "Long as we score, and as long as we're winning, me personally, if I'm blocking or if I'm setting a crack block and that engineered the 37 points, I’m happy ," Pickens said Wednesday, via Tommy Yarrish of the team website. Pickens' numbers aren't far off the start to his 2025 season when he made eight catches for 98 yards and a touchdown in the first two games. "Of course I want to get him and CeeDee the ball," Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "I think CeeDee is playing great. I think George is playing really well. Some of the catches he made [against Washington] were really big-time plays in big-time situations for us. . . . He draws a lot of attention out there. But believe me, we're looking for ways to continue to get those guys the ball. "If you look at George last year, he didn't take off until a couple games in. And the rest, as they know, is history how well he played. I have no questions about him and his readiness. He'll be ready to go this week." Pickens agrees that he is playing well despite how the numbers look. "I'd definitely say team for me. I feel like I've been doing great," Pickens said. "As far as the team, like my whole game. Some people just look at certain parts of my game. My whole game I feel like has been great."
author: Charean Williams

title: Mike Macdonald learned valuable lessons regarding his media approach
summary: Despite his immense success in a short time with one of the 32 most coveted jobs in football, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is still learning.
full_text: ' Despite his immense success in a short time with one of the 32 most coveted jobs in football, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald is still learning. As it relates to his recent sit-down with Graham Bensinger, Macdonald has learned that nothing is off the record unless both sides to the conversation agree that it is. Macdonald also has learned to assume that every mic is a hot mic, and that every camera is capturing images. He's also learning to be careful about who he trusts, and about when and where he lets himself get comfortable. More broadly, Macdonald is learning why Bill Belichick behaves the way he does. If you say as little as possible, the chances of saying something you come to regret will be minimized. Earlier this week, Macdonald was asked about his decision to submit to interviews in the aftermath of winning the Super Bowl. “If someone’s interested in talking and you feel like it’s an honest process, then why not?" Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "I don’t have a long relationship with Graham [Bensinger], but I was really impressed with how they did their business. There are other podcasts that you had prior relationships with folks, and I respect the work that they do, and we have prior relationships that you want to honor. It’s probably that simple." As the owner and operator of a media outlet, I'll never complain about coaches, players, and others from the NFL universe providing compelling content. Plenty of it comes from the press conferences to which coaches are required to submit. When they stray beyond that, they need to be careful. Careful about what they say. Careful about who they say it to. Careful about who they trust. As to Bensinger, he won the battle of capturing a compelling sound bite. He may have lost the broader war, however. By possibly operating under the premise that it's better to seek forgiveness than to request permission — and by clinging to the technicalities of invoking off-the-record protection — Macdonald surely won't be inclined to sit down with him again. And, if Macdonald does, he'll be far more guarded. Others may have similar trepidations about submitting to interviews and/or allowing themselves to be charmed into getting too comfortable. For Macdonald, he got way too comfortable. One source not connected to either the Seahawks or Broncos deemed it "reckless." Complicating matters for Macdonald is that he now reports to ownership that didn't hire him. And while winning is ultimately all that matters, early impressions matter, too. And it's one thing for outsiders to question Macdonald's judgment and discretion. If Vinod, Neeru, and/or Neal Khosla feel a little differently about Macdonald after this incident, it could come back to haunt him if/when the wins aren't as consistent or convincing.
author: Mike Florio

title: Five Texans miss practice with injuries
summary: The Texans were without six players in Wednesday's practice, five of them rehabbing injuries.
full_text: The Texans were without six players in Wednesday's practice, five of them rehabbing injuries. Offensive tackle Trent Brown (knee/wrist), defensive end Jadeveon Clowney (knee), wide receiver Nico Collins (hamstring), linebacker Jake Hummel (groin), offensive guard Ed Ingram (groin) and tight end Dalton Schultz (rest) did not practice. Collins injured his hamstring in practice last week and missed the Week 2 loss to the Bengals. Defensive end Will Anderson Jr. (rest), defensive end Logan Hall (knee) and safety M.J. Stewart (knee) were limited. Safety Reed Blankenship (thumb) and linebacker Wade Woodaz (thumb) were full participants.
author: Charean Williams

title: Travis Etienne, Chase Young limited in Saints practice
summary: Running back Travis Etienne was among the Saints players on the team's first injury report ahead of their Week 3 game against the Raiders.
full_text: Running back Travis Etienne was among the Saints players on the team's first injury report ahead of their Week 3 game against the Raiders. Etienne was a limited participant in practice due to a hamstring injury. Etienne signed with the Saints this offseason and has 17 carries and 71 yards through the first two games of the year. Defensive end Chase Young (calf) was also listed as limited. He was on the injury report last week and was listed as questionable before playing in last Sunday's win over the Ravens. Wide receiver Barion Brown (hamstring), cornerback Martin Emerson (shoulder), and defensive lineman Christen Miller (toe) did not practice on Wednesday. Safety Jonas Sanker (knee), defensive end Nathan Shepherd (hip), and linebacker Isaiah Stalbird (shoulder) were limited participants.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jonah Coleman out of Broncos practice; J.K. Dobbins, RJ Harvey limited
summary: The top three Broncos running backs are all on the injury report.
full_text: The top three Broncos running backs are all on the injury report. Jonah Coleman did not practice on Wednesday due to an ankle injury. Coleman scored his first NFL touchdown in last Sunday's win over the Jaguars and the rookie ran 10 times for 39 yards in the game. Coleman saw more playing time because J.K. Dobbins left the game with a hip injury and RJ Harvey was inactive with a hamstring injury. Both of those backs were listed as limited participants. Wide receiver Marvin Mims (foot) was also a limited participant. He missed practice all of last week and did not play against Jacksonville.
author: Josh Alper

title: Sean McVay: We'll err on the side of caution with Puka Nacua
summary: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua missed Week 2 with a groin injury and his outlook for this week's game against the Broncos remains unclear.
full_text: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua missed Week 2 with a groin injury and his outlook for this week's game against the Broncos remains unclear. Head coach Sean McVay said that Nacua would have missed Wednesday's practice — the team only held a jog-through — and they'll see what he's able to do on Thursday. McVay said Nacua is "frustrated," but that the team doesn't believe this is a long-term issue and will exercise caution to ensure it doesn't become one. “I don’t think so. I think it’s more along the lines of just seeing how that responds ," McVay said, via Nate Atkins of TheAthletic.com. "When you’re a skill player and you’re really trying to hit high-speed yards and really open up, then some of the things can be like pre-hernia is what he’s feeling. You err on the side of caution. Usually, time is the best thing that allows that thing to heal and then when you get to a certain point, I think you feel pretty good moving forward.” If that doesn't happen by Sunday, Davante Adams will remain the top wide receiving option for the Rams.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jaxson Dart could return for the postseason, if the Giants qualify
summary: John Harbaugh confirmed Jaxson Dart will need surgery to repair his knee injury, but the Giants coach couched how long the quarterback might be out.
full_text: John Harbaugh confirmed Jaxson Dart will need surgery to repair his knee injury, but the Giants coach couched how long the quarterback might be out. " Regular season at least , I would say," Harbaugh said, via video from SNY Giants. Asked a follow-up question about whether he was leaving open the possibility of Dart returning for the postseason, if the Giants qualify, Harbaugh said: "I think I said it. I said it. Regular season. Other than that, how do you know? There's no way to know. It depends on the recovery. You can't pinpoint it exactly." Dart's absence, though, decreases the Giants' chances of getting to the playoffs. Dart, who was injured in Monday night's loss to the Rams, will undergo surgery to repair damage to the MCL and the meniscus in his left knee, according to multiple reports. The Giants initially believed Dart's injury was not season-ending, but the MRI delivered the bad news, and he will undergo surgery soon. "It's a big loss for sure. It's your starting quarterback," Harbaugh said. Dart was in team meetings on Wednesday, while trying to come to terms with the fact that his third season is over after only two games. "I think he's determined," Harbaugh said. "He's bummed. It's hard. The season's not over, but it is for him. We kind of talked about that, too. That was part of it. There's a certain mourning that takes place." Jameis Winston will take over as the starter, though the Giants are in the market for a veteran quarterback to join Jake Haener behind Winston. Harbaugh said his message to the team was "it's not a one-game man." "We need to be the best Giants we can be," he said.
author: Charean Williams

title: Knee injury keeps Aaron Jones out of practice for Vikings

He’s bouncing around the building like normal , but it’s more so the knee," O'Connell said at his press conference. "Just allowing that thing to turn over. He feels pretty good. We’ll just keep getting treatment around the clock and see if we can pick up his workload as the week goes on.” Jordan Mason is on injured reserve and DeeJay Dallas was limited with a toe injury, which leaves sixth-round pick Demond Claiborne as the only healthy back on the active roster. Linebacker Jake Golday (ankle) and punter Brett Thorson (right hamstring) also missed practice. title: Brian Burns likely to miss time with low ankle sprain

full_text: Giants pass rusher Brian Burns said after Monday night's loss to the Rams that his low ankle sprain was " nothing serious ." But it is probably serious enough to keep him out at least this week. Burns is likely to miss some time, according to Adam Schefter. The 28-year-old Burns is one of the Giants’ best defensive players, losing him was a big blow, on a night when the offense suffered an even bigger blow with the loss of quarterback Jaxson Dart, who will miss the rest of the regular season with a knee injury. title: John Harbaugh: All options are open for adding a veteran QB

Can't say who at this point. We're working on that." Harbaugh, who said he prefers adding a veteran, did not rule out acquiring a quarterback via trade. title: Joe Burrow is no longer on the Bengals injury report

full_text: At a press conference before the Bengals practiced on Wednesday, head coach Zay Taylor said that he wasn't sure how much quarterback Joe Burrow would be able to do at practice. As it turns out, Taylor was either overly anxious about Burrow's health or attempting some gamesmanship. Videos from the open portion of practice showed Burrow working without any limitations and the team did not list him on the injury report at all. That suggests he's full speed ahead for this Sunday's game against the Steelers. Burrow was listed as questionable in Week 2 because of a back injury and could be heard telling teammates during the game that a hit from Texans defensive end Will Anderson popped his rib back into place. Defensive tackles Jonathan Allen (knee) and B.J. Hill (Achilles) were both out of practice. title: Sean Payton: All good with Mike Macdonald, incident helped us handle training camp videos
summary: It sounds like the 2024 kerfuffle has been put to bed once and for all.
full_text: Broncos head coach Sean Payton got his chance to address Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald's comments about a 2024 disagreement between the teams at his Wednesday press conference. Macdonald said earlier in the day that he called Payton to apologize after comments he intended to be off the record about Payton getting upset about the Seahawks' use of fan videos from training camp to prepare for a 2024 game went public. Payton said he and Macdonald are good and said he called Seahawks General Manager John Schneider "shooting before I started looking" because he didn't know how the Seahawks had obtained the videos. The videos were posted on social media and Payton said that the incident wound up in a positive way because it allowed the Broncos to address videotaping of their practices. “Talking with them, it allowed us to figure out how to handle our training camp relative to videos ," Payton said. "I don’t think anything was intentional by fans. We did some research online of what was available and that's kind of how we changed our policy.” Payton called the entire episode "eye-opening" in terms of how information from open practices can circulate and both sides will likely be sticking to official game tape to prepare for their Week 6 game.
author: Josh Alper

title: The Joey Porter Jr. situation lingers, with no end in sight
summary: With the Steelers facing the Bengals this weekend — and receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — it would be helpful to have cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on the field.
full_text: With the Steelers facing the Bengals this weekend — and receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins — it would be helpful to have cornerback Joey Porter Jr. on the field. Yet again, it appears he won't be playing. And the situation seems to be settling into a week-to-week lather/rinse/repeat of limited practice time (if any) and no game appearances. On Wednesday, coach Mike McCarthy wasn't even asked about Porter during the midweek media availability. On one hand, it's easy to justify the absence of a question by assuming that it would have promoted the same-old response about being optimistic he'll play (or whatever). On the other hand, the questions badly need to change. How frustrating is it that no progress is being made? Is injured reserve being considered? Do the Steelers believe Porter is actually injured, or do they suspect he is declining to play because he doesn't have a contract? No one wants to call this what it is. It's a hold-in that has lingered into the season. Porter is doing what former Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons was ready to do in 2025. Once the Cowboys realized it was going to go that way, they quickly traded Parsons. For the Steelers, there are only two ways out of this maze. Pay him, or trade him. Playing hardball is possibly becoming harder to accomplish each week, since the Steelers are publishing injury reports that represent to the world that Porter is injured. (Today, the stated reason was "conditioning.") If, at some point, the Steelers suddenly say "enough," they may have to answer for weeks of possibly embellished injury reports. Either way, it could get ugly if/when the Steelers decide to squeeze Porter to play. At some point, however, the situation becomes sufficiently obvious to be ridiculous. It's arguably already at that point. And, again, there are only two good ways to fix it. Pay him, or trade him.

author: Josh Alper

title: What is happening with Marvin Harrison Jr.? Former top 5 pick has disappeared from Arizona offense
summary: Coming off a down second season, Harrison has been a bust through the first two games, with just one catch
full_text:
Through the first two weeks of the 2026 season, Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr . has just one catch for 33 yards. Five different players on the Cardinals have more grabs, including both of the team's running backs. Harrison has only been targeted four times by Jacoby Brissett in those two games, a mark that ranks tied for fifth on the team with Tyler Allgeier . Ostensible No. 3 wideout Kendrick Bourne has more than twice as many targets (11) and 10 times as many catches (10) as Harrison.
The raw counting stats sound bad, but the rate stats might be even worse when you look at them in the context of the league. There are 103 wide receivers who have run 25 or more routes so far this year, according to TruMedia. Harrison ranks 100th among that group in target rate, at 6.5%. Such luminaries as Konata Mumpfield , Kevin Coleman Jr. , Bryce Lance , LaJohntay Wester and Xavier Legette have been targeted more often on a per-route basis. He ranks 92nd in yards per route run, at 0.52. Players like Jahan Dotson and Isaiah Williams and Roman Wilson have generated more yards on a per-route basis.
Ordinarily, a receiver getting off to a poor start to the season wouldn't be all that notable. It happens. The difference is that Harrison isn't just any wide receiver. He's the son of Marvin Harrison, one of the greatest receivers of all time. He's the former No. 4 overall pick in the NFL Draft . And he was widely considered one of the best wide receiver prospects in years when he came out of Ohio State. And he's already been disappointing through the first two years of his career. So this cold start is especially notable, and especially alarming. He looks like he could go down as a huge draft bust if anything remotely like this keeps up.
It's worth asking what, exactly, is going on down in Arizona.
The way Harrison is being used within the offense is, frankly, not conducive to being targeted at a high volume.
Among the aforementioned group of 103 wide receivers who have run 25 or more routes so far this year, Harrison has the farthest average route depth, according to TruMedia. The average break on his routes has come an incredible 12.83 yards down the field. That mark would have led the league last year, ahead of guys like AD Mitchell, Alec Pierce , Tyquan Thornton and more. Those guys are pure deep threats. That's how Harrison is being deployed right now.
You can see this in his route distribution. He's run 62 routes so far this year, according toTru Media, and 19 of them have been go routes. That 30.6% go-route rate is fifth-highest among those 103 receivers. His post-route rate of 12.9% is 23rd among the same group of players. Those routes combine to make up 43.5% of his total. And he's been targeted just once on those 27 combined routes; that target yielded his one 33-yard catch.
pic.twitter.com/yfqAvmdWpO
Harrison, in other words, is being used as the so-called Sacrificial X receiver. He's lining up on the line of scrimmage, out to the wide side of the field, and running his man off the line in order to create space for other players underneath the coverage. That's not a role conducive to being targeted at a high rate, and he has accordingly not seen the ball very many times so far.
Of course, you can't blame everything on his utilization. Harrison already has a drop, for example, and there are numerous times on film where you can see him running routes at less than full exertion. There was a pretty brutal cut-up from Week 1 alone that showcased his lack of speed, crispness and ability to create separation on his routes.
Marvin Harrison Jr. struggled to get ANYTHING going against the Chargers. Harrison Jr. finished the game with 3 TGTS, 1 REC, 33 total yards, and 1 registered drop. The Cardinals former 4th overall pick is NOT off to an ideal start to his third year 👀😳 pic.twitter.com/GqzNrdoU9A
Not content to put that effort forth in just the season opener, Harrison went out there and did it again in Week 2 against the division rival Seahawks . There are times here where he is barely even pretending to be part of the play or look for the ball to come his way.
I hesitate to ascribe too much to body language on a guy's tape, but... This looks like somebody who has checked out. At times before this season, it felt like MHJR was just way low on confidence. Here, he doesn't look like he ever expects the ball. pic.twitter.com/69Uw2ZcB8k
really great blocking effort too, Marv pic.twitter.com/JOdJidAvms
That's unacceptable stuff, even if the ball isn't designed to come to you. You have to run your route as if you will get the ball. (And you have to block, because the run could come your way as well.)
First of all, because there is a chance it will actually come to you, even if it's not designed to do so. ( Josh Allen said he had never thrown the route that resulted in his game-winning touchdown pass to Josh Palmer in Week 1, for example.) And second of all, if you're not putting forth the full effort to run the coverage off for your teammates, then they won't be as open as they're supposed to be, and that undermines the rest of the offense.
The biggest reason the ball isn't coming Harrison's way is that he's just very clearly not the best pass catcher -- and he may not even be the best wide receiver -- in his own offense, even if he was drafted that way.
Trey McBride is arguably the best tight end in the NFL . He leads all tight ends with 23 targets and 17 receptions this season, and his 136 receiving yards rank fourth at the position. Last year, McBride led all tight ends in targets, catches, yards and touchdowns. He is always open. Brissett trusts him, and so do the coaches running the offense, because he has earned that trust with his play. (That was true of both last year's coaching staff and this year's.)
Over the last year-plus, Michael Wilson has also looked like the better option than Harrison. He exploded when Harrison missed time last season, and he's done a better job of earning targets (seven in each of the first two games) this season. The coaching staff said before the year that it wanted to use Wilson in a Puka Nacua-style role in the offense as the Z receiver and Harrison in Davante Adams ' role as the X, and that has held true so far this year. It's not surprising that Wilson is being targeted at a much higher rate given the players' respective roles and their level of play.
author: Jared Dubin

title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson comments on Rio field ahead of international game, as conditions draw criticism
summary: The first ever Rio De Janeiro game between the Cowboys and Ravens will be broadcast on CBS this Sunday
full_text:
History will be made on Sunday when the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens face off in the league's first ever game in Rio de Janeiro and as much excitement as there is surrounding the game, there are also some concerns swirling. The field conditions are a major subject ahead of the contest, with several soccer players who call Maracaña Stadium home complaining and criticizing the conditions.
Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson , who has quite a bit at stake in the quality of the field, commented on the conditions on Wednesday.
"I believe the NFL does a great job at having their specialists go out there and look over the fields," Jackson said to the media. "I cannot worry about that. I just have to worry about getting us a dub in Brazil. [As for] the field, we have played on bad fields plenty of times, so I cannot really dwell on that."
Lamar Jackson said he’s not concerned about the condition of the field in Rio pic.twitter.com/BNJskW3AeC
This week, the stadium released pictures and have said the conditions would improve. Some reasons they state for the field issues are due to the high number of games, more matches with precipitation close to the game and high temperatures.
The NFL is reportedly "aware" of the possible challenges with the field. It appears groundskeepers are working to improve the conditions.
The NFL took is now in charge of the field prep, taking over the stadium management this week.
O perfil do Maracanã divulgou imagens do trabalho da Greenleaf para tentar mitigar os problemas do gramado e melhorar as condições para a reta final da temporada. A chuva ontem foi castigando ainda mais o campo, que apresentava falhas durante Flamengo x Corinthians. Na última… pic.twitter.com/7aBcnVcelI
This marks the NFL's third game in Brazil, with the others played in São Paulo, a field that was also criticized. The Ravens and Cowboys have never played in Brazil. The Cowboys have played in one previous international game, coming in 2014 against the Jacksonville Jaguars . The Ravens have played in two international games before this, both in London, with the most recent one against the Tennessee Titans in 2023 and the first one against the Jaguars in 2017.
Other players and coaches participating in Sunday's game also commented on the situation and the overall feeling is that the NFL will ensure the conditions are safe to play on.
"There is a lot of just, 'he said, she said,' kind of thing going on right now, so we will see," Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton said . "I know the players are the product in this league. As soon as we lose 'putting the players forward' is when we lose the league. I am sure the league knows that and they are doing their best to put us in the position to be safe. So, that is not really in the forefront of my mind right now."
Baltimore cornerback Marlon Humphrey joked that the team will play on whatever surface they're given.
"If we got to play on some concrete, we will play on some concrete," Humphrey said. "I'm hoping those reports aren't true."
Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer is looking for Dallas' second ever win against the Ravens, with Baltimore holding a 6-1 all-time series record. In preparation for the game, they're not just studying up on their opponent, but learning about different cleats.
Schottenheimer said his players were informed on what cleats to wear, citing ones with better traction as a good choice for this field.
"The biggest thing for us is we expect the field to be fine and we have backup plans in place, but right now we've educated these guys," Schottenheimer said. "At the end of the day, these guys have to wear things that make them feel comfortable, and if they're slipping, then that's going to be on them."
The game will be broadcasted on CBS, streaming on Paramount+ with kickoff at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sept. 27.
author: Shanna McCarriston

title: Five QB trades the Giants could make with Jaxson Dart out for season, including two with ties to John Harbaugh
summary: New York is turning to Jameis Winston for now, but several mobile quarterbacks and familiar faces could emerge as trade targets if the veteran struggles
full_text:
The NFL season hasn't even hit Week 3, and the New York Giants are already in trouble. Jaxson Dart is out for the season after suffering a knee injury during the first quarter of New York's 28-6 loss to the Rams in Week 2.
With Dart out, the Giants turn the offense over to Jameis Winston . The former No. 1 overall pick just signed a two-year, $13 million extension with New York, so the Giants clearly have some faith in him, but if he struggles over the next week or two, that could open the door for John Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen to start poking around for another quarterback.
One potential problem with Winston is that he has a completely different skill set than Dart, which is why it wouldn't be completely crazy for the Giants to look around for a mobile QB.
With that in mind, we're going to take a look at five trade options that could make sense. This list will consist of two types of quarterbacks: guys who are mobile and/or guys who have ties to the coaching staff, which will make it much easier to get them acclimated to New York's offense.
If the Giants do end up making a trade, adding Huntley would probably make the most sense. Huntley spent the first four seasons of his career in Baltimore playing under Harbaugh. After heading to Miami in 2024, he returned to Baltimore last season to spend one more year with Harbaugh. During his time in Baltimore, Huntley saw plenty of action: He started a total of 12 games under Harbaugh, including a wild-card playoff game in January 2023.
The former Pro Bowler has the mobility Harbaugh loves to see in his quarterbacks, and he's always done a good job of using it on the field. One other upside to adding Huntley is that Greg Roman is on the Giants' coaching staff. Roman was the Ravens ' offense coordinator during Huntlery's first three seasons, so he could quickly get him up to speed on the playbook that offensive coordinator Matt Nagy is running in New York.
Due to Lamar Jackson's injury history, the Ravens might not be willing to part ways with Huntley, but Baltimore did keep rookie Joe Fagano on the roster, so it's certainly possible that they would think about making a deal at the right price.
When the 2026 offseason started, Fields was in New York with the Jets , so a deal here would send him back to the Big Apple. The Jets ended up trading him to the Chiefs in March , which was a move that made sense at the time. When the offseason started, the Chiefs weren't sure if Patrick Mahomes was going to be ready to play in Week 1, so they added Fields as an insurance policy. With Mahomes now back on the field and looking like himself through the first two weeks, the Chiefs might be willing to ship Fields off to New York. One reason Kansas City might be open to a trade is that they already have a potential backup QB on the roster in rookie Garrett Nussmeier .
One reason Harbaugh might be interested in adding Fields is that the Giants' offensive coordinator, Matt Nagy, is already familiar with him. Nagy coached during Fields' rookie year with the Bears in 2021.
If the Giants want someone who could come in and learn the offense quickly, Trubisky would make a lot of sense. The Titans backup QB started his career in Chicago in 2017 when the Bears selected him with the second overall pick in the NFL Draft . In 2018, Trubisky led the Bears to an 11-3 record and a playoff appearance and his coach that year just happens to be the same guy who is currently serving as the offensive coordinator with the Giants: Nagy.
Nagy and Trubisky spent three seasons together in Chicago, and they went 25-13 during that span. That doesn't sound possible, but it's true. The only thing that could throw a wrench into a possible deal for Trubisky is that he plays for the Titans, who the Giants happen to be playing this week. The Titans probably wouldn't want to make a deal until after the game, which could potentially work out well, because that would give the Giants an extra week to figure out if Jameis Winston is good enough to carry the offense.
This might be the perfect time for Indianapolis to unload Richardson, who made a trade request earlier this offseason . He did win the backup job in Indianapolis this year, but if the Colts decided to trade him to New York, they'd still have Riley Leonard to take over the No. 2 spot.
By trading him away, it would allow the Colts to get something in return for Richardson, who was the No. 4 overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. If they keep him on the roster, he'll likely be leaving in free agency at the end of the year, and they'll get nothing in return.
This would almost be an ideal situation for both sides. Since the Colts didn't pick up Richardson's fifth-year option, that means his rookie deal is going to expire at the end of the 2026 season. If Richardson got dealt to New York and played well, that would put him in a position to cash in when he hits free agency after the season. As for the Giants, they wouldn't be tied to Richardson in any way, since his contract would expire at the end of the year.
If there's one guy in the NFL who can show up and be productive right away, it's definitely Flacco. Last season, he got traded to the Bengals on Oct. 7 , didn't participate in his first practice until Oct. 8, but that didn't stop him from throwing for 219 yards and two touchdowns in a 27-18 loss to the Packers on Oct. 12.
The difference between Cincinnati and New York is that Flacco wouldn't be in a totally unfamiliar situation because he would be reuniting with his former head coach, John Harbaugh. Flacco's first year in the NFL came in 2008, which just happened to be Harbaugh's first year as head coach of the Ravens. The Harbaugh-Flacco combination had a lot of success during their 11 seasons together in Baltimore, including a Super Bowl win in 2012.
Yes, that was 14 years ago, and yes, Flacco is now 41, but the Giants don't need him to be their franchise quarterback. They need him to play at high level for 15 games and that's something he might be able to pull off. In six starts with the Bengals last season, Flacco averaged 272.7 passing yards per game while also throwing 13 touchdown passes compared to just four interceptions.
Flacco ending his career with the same head coach who was there at the beginning would also be kind of a poetic way for the former Super Bowl MVP to go out. Of course, for the Giants to get Flacco, the Bengals would have to be willing to trade him and there's no guarantee that would happen. Due to Joe Burrow's injury history, the Bengals would probably prefer to hold on to Flacco unless they got absolutely blown away by an offer.
That said, the two front offices are very familiar with each other thanks to the April trade that sent Dexter Lawrence to Cincinnati, so anything is possible.
Other quarterbacks who could be available for trade: J.J. McCarthy , Mac Jones . As I mentioned above, we stuck to two types of quarterbacks on our trade list: They either had to be mobile or familiar with the current coaching staff or both. If the Giants want classic pocket passer, it would probably just make sense to stick with Winston, who's in his second season with the team.
In terms of free agency, the Giants could give Jimmy Garoppolo a call, but at this point, he might not be a huge upgrade over Jameis Winston. There's also Russell Wilson , but he seems more than happy working with us here at CBS Sports.
The Giants do have a chance to save their season here. If they can find a QB who can play at a high level -- even if that QB ends up being Winston -- they could stay afloat all season. Over the next five weeks, the 1-1 Giants will play three games against teams that are currently 0-2 (Titans, Texans , and Commanders ), along with a game against the Cardinals , so there are some winnable games that New York needs to take advantage of.
author: John Breech

title: Giants' Jaxson Dart to undergo knee surgery that will end his 2026 season
summary: Dart's ACL is intact, but his season is over
full_text:
The New York Giants ' fears have been realized. Quarterback Jaxson Dart will undergo knee surgery that will end his 2026 season, Giants coach John Harbaugh announced on Wednesday. Harbaugh left the door open for a potential postseason return. According to ESPN, Dart's ACL is intact, but the second-year signal-caller suffered damage to his MCL, PCL, and meniscus. The meniscus is reported to be the main issue.
Dart suffered the injury on the first drive of the night in New York's Monday night matchup against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2. The former first-round pick was hit by multiple defenders while in the air, and his knee bent awkwardly. Initially, it was thought Dart's injury was not as severe, with reports suggesting he sprained his MCL.
Upon further review of the injury, however, it was worse than initially diagnosed.
Starting 12 games as a rookie after being the No. 25 overall pick in the 2025 NFL Draft , Dart entered this season as the full-time starter, and New York was eyed as a potential breakout team with John Harbaugh as head coach. The club furthered that offseason hype when it defeated the Dallas Cowboys in the season opener. In that game, Dart completed 79.3% of his passes for 230 yards and three passing touchdowns. Now, the 2026 season is viewed through a much different lens.
With him on the shelf, the Giants will likely turn to Jameis Winston as their starter going forward. While coming in under duress on Monday night against the Rams, Winston completed 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and an interception.
That sharpens the stark contrast in what the play under center has looked like for New York over the last two seasons, with and without Dart.
Over the next month-plus, the Giants will host the Tennessee Titans in Week 3, and then the Arizona Cardinals in Week 4 before heading to Washington to face the Commanders (who lost their starter in Jayden Daniels) in Week 5. They'll return to MetLife Stadium for a Week 6 matchup against the Saints, then travel to Houston to face the Texans in Week 6 before their Week 7 bye.
