title: Cowboys discussion: Ravens a step up in competition for a team with lots to prove
summary: It is too early in the season to say the game against the Washington Commanders was a must-win for the Dallas Cowboys, but it certainly felt like it. A defeat would have given Dallas two losses in the division, and two losses to start the season. That would have been a big hole to climb […]
full_text: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images | Getty Images It is too early in the season to say the game against the Washington Commanders was a must-win for the Dallas Cowboys, but it certainly felt like it. A defeat would have given Dallas two losses in the division, and two losses to start the season. That would have been a big hole to climb out of. But the Cowboys posted a convincing looking win over the Commanders and now sit at 1-1. Unfortunately, the operative word in that previous sentence is “looking.” There were some pretty glaring warts. Now Dallas faces a game in Brazil against the Baltimore Ravens, who were upset by the New Orleans Saints on Sunday and are likely to come out angry. The Cowboys are the underdog. There are some good reasons, as our Sean Martin and Tom Ryle discuss. Tom – A 17-point win looks good, but there are some ugly things in the stats and at least one huge break on a touchdown that certainly looked good but was still denied by replay. Even bigger, Jayden Daniels was leading his team well and had them in position to tie things up just before the half. Then disaster struck as he dislocated his elbow. (Do not watch the replay if you are squeamish.) Marcus Mariota is a seasoned backup, but he’s a backup for a reason. The offense put up plenty of points, but did so as a one-dimensional attack as Dak Prescott’s record had to cover for another paltry rushing attack. The defense had a huge takeaway and a handful of other stops, but still looked far too vulnerable. It was especially so when Daniels used his legs. Now, they face Lamar Jackson. Oh, boy. Sean – There’s a lot to critique about the defense and we’ll do some of that, but chalk me up for the biggest area of concern coming out of this win being the run game, Tom. The trust isn’t quite there to keep going to the bellcow back, Javonte Williams. Brian Schottenheimer conceded they had a heavy passing-game plan going into the Washington game. With Williams averaging 2.5 yards a carry in this win and 3.4 in week one, that makes sense. This is an interesting thing to be talking about specific to the Ravens matchup upcoming, because they too had a lead at home in week two but inexplicably forgot about Derrick Henry and their own run game, losing that lead to the Saints. When the Cowboys got the ball back up 27-13 after a missed field goal in the third quarter, they were only able to hand the ball off on seven of their remaining 18 plays. The Ravens went up 17-9 in the third quarter and proceeded to go three and out with a negative 11 yard drive, three and out again, and threw an interception to lose the game, all while running it one measly time during this stretch. Whichever team can remember to stick with their running game, and of course find production within it, can help their quarterback the most in this Brazil game. The Cowboys will need to do everything they can to elevate Prescott in a matchup where we’re all worried about what Jackson could do to the Dallas defense in return. I don’t know how well they’ll be able to do so going up against a Jesse Minter defense they saw a year ago against the Chargers, where the Cowboys were held to 91 yards on the ground, tied for the second lowest output of the season. It still may be the defense that’s the main culprit of why fans feel a little uneasy even after a divisional win, but I think more of it than advertised is the struggles running the ball as well, not something we’re used to seeing from a Cowboys offense of late. Tom – I was thinking about things and came up with the idea that there are five elements of the game for a team. Passing offense, running offense, pass defense, run defense, and special teams. Right now, the Cowboys are good in one, passing offense, and perhaps two if you count special teams where Brandon Aubrey is again hitting everything out to 60 yards or more. But they are clearly struggling in the remaining three elements. That does not bode well when you look at the matchup this week. You’ve already covered the issues with their ground game. Dallas has been giving up big yards on the ground, and now they face Derrick Henry and Lamar Jackson. Their pass rush has been anemic and coverage spotty at best, and Jackson is no slouch throwing the ball. That puts the burden clearly on the passing game, and we already saw that wasn’t enough in the season opener. Frankly, they are almost a different team when playing from behind, one that presses and makes mistakes. We can’t expect CeeDee Lamb and Prescott to have another monster game. Hopefully George Pickens and the rest of the receiving corps can step up, but it still leaves them in a position of having to play almost perfectly just to hang with the opponent. They scored on all but one possession against Washington, and that is going to be a lot harder to do against the Minter defense. Disturbingly, you have to wonder if they would still have won Sunday if Daniels had not been injured. It almost certainly would have been much closer. The path to a win would probably involve another lights out passing game and some takeaways, which have been hard to get. Forgive me if I’m not optimistic. Sean – Sounds like I have just a bit of optimism to spare you for this matchup Tom, but not a whole lot so use it wisely. We’ll calculate the exchange rate on that between the States and Brazil some other time. The latest injury update for the Cowboys is not good at all for the defense, with P.J. Locke and Cobie Durant set to miss time. Unless this unit can finish off some sacks on Lamar Jackson, not just get close like they did to Daniels/Mariota, it almost feels like the defensive mindset has to shift to just slowing the Ravens down as opposed to really expecting many stops. The Ravens had as many first downs as the Saints while running eight less plays, faced six less third downs, and averaged 5.6 yards per play. Parker’s scheme in theory should be able to do some of this, but I worry what it means for a Cowboys offensive game plan that needs balance like we said. Then there’s this x-factor of how skill players will find their footing on a field that’s reportedly not up to snuff. Our old friend Kellen Moore may not have done us a favor at all by beating this Ravens squad in week two either. Getting them off a bad loss doesn’t feel great for the designated home team’s chances in Rio de Janeiro. Tom – Hey, I’m not going to slam Kellen for one of the biggest wins of his young career. But, no, he didn’t do his old team any favors. This is not an unwinnable game for the Cowboys. Just a very difficult challenge. They have to keep doing what they’ve been getting right without a slipup, and they have to have multiple other things gel, or at least one. I do think this team will get better over time, particularly on defense. The problem is that they can’t take too much time, and gradual improvement isn’t going to help this week. We’ll still hope for the best, but we better prepare for something short of that. Sean – A 1-2 record would be an awfully familiar place to be anyway, and I agree, if they get there while competing well and not showing any major flaws like in week one, we’ll be back here next week still finding some positives to talk about. Until then, enjoy the overseas game Tom! Okay BTB, what is your take on the issues brought up here?
author: Sean Martin

title: Cowboys Week 3: A look at the 2026 Baltimore Ravens
summary: Week 3 is here, and the matchup with the Baltimore Ravens looms in beautiful Brazil. Let’s take a look at the 2026 Ravens. What’s new in Baltimore? Baltimore looks like a team in transition. Jesse Minter is in his first season as head coach and defensive play-caller, Declan Doyle is calling the offense for the […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images | Getty Images Week 3 is here, and the matchup with the Baltimore Ravens looms in beautiful Brazil. Let’s take a look at the 2026 Ravens. What’s new in Baltimore ? Baltimore looks like a team in transition. Jesse Minter is in his first season as head coach and defensive play-caller, Declan Doyle is calling the offense for the first time, and both sides have shown the ability to produce big plays but neither has been particularly consistent. Baltimore opened with a 41-23 demolition of Indianapolis, where they gained over 500 yards of offense, then lost 24-17 to New Orleans after failing to score in the final 18 minutes of that contest. So which Ravens team is Dallas getting? Probably somewhere in between. Lamar Jackson is still Lamar Jackson Let’s get the obvious one out of the way. The Cowboys are facing a two-time MVP quarterback who can ruin a defensive game plan with either his arm or his legs, and if the first two weeks reflect this team’s defensive struggles against mobile quarterbacks, the Cowboys may be in for a long day. Jackson opened the season by throwing for 324 yards and a touchdown against Indianapolis, while adding 40 rushing yards and another score. He followed that with 235 passing yards, a touchdown and an interception against New Orleans, plus 34 rushing yards. Through two games, he’s thrown for 559 yards, two touchdowns and one interception while adding 74 yards on the ground. The Week 2 performance wasn’t nearly as explosive, but that’s part of the challenge with Jackson. The Saints sacked him three times, and Baltimore’s offense couldn’t find much of a rhythm after halftime. But Jackson can still turn a broken play into a 30-yard gain, and Dallas’ defense has already shown that containing mobile quarterbacks will be one of its biggest tests. For Christian Parker’s defense, this is less about stopping Jackson from running entirely and more about making him consistently beat them from the pocket. That’s easier said than done. Lamar Jackson 🎯 Rashod Bateman for the TD NOvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RwqbUrIoEP — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Derrick Henry isn’t slowing down either If Jackson is the knife that will cut you up, Derrick Henry is the blunt instrument, and, well, he’s still pretty good. Henry opened 2026 with 144 yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries against Indianapolis. He followed that with 68 yards and a touchdown on 16 carries against New Orleans. That’s 212 yards and four touchdowns through two games. But something interesting happened in the Saints game. Henry had just two carries in the second half, and Baltimore ultimately went away from its running game while trying to protect its lead. As mentioned earlier, the Ravens were shut out in the final 18 minutes. That’s something Dallas should remember. Baltimore’s offense is at its most dangerous when Jackson and Henry are working together. If the Cowboys can make Baltimore more one-dimensional, the Ravens have shown that their offense can become much easier to handle. The problem is obvious: making Baltimore one-dimensional means finding a way to slow down Derrick Henry. After seeing this Cowboys defense through two games, good luck with that. Derrick Henry takes it himself for SIX 👑 NOvsBAL on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/xTPWbcJhpE — NFL (@NFL) September 20, 2026 Zay Flowers will likely be back Zay Flowers was Baltimore’s biggest offensive receiving weapon in Week 1. He caught five passes for 150 yards and a touchdown, including a 54-yard score against Indianapolis. He also set a career high in receiving yards. Then he missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury. That’s one of the biggest things to watch heading into Brazil. As of Monday, Minter said he felt the Ravens had a “good shot” with several injured players returning, including Flowers, but Baltimore won’t know more until later in the week. If Flowers plays, he immediately becomes one of the biggest problems for Dallas’ secondary. If he doesn’t, Rashod Bateman becomes the top returning receiver, while Baltimore can lean more heavily on Mark Andrews and its running game. Bateman already had a big Week 2, catching seven passes for 88 yards and a touchdown. So even without Flowers, Dallas can’t ignore this receiving corps. Zay Flowers is FAST. 54-yard TD! BALvsIND on CBS/Paramount+ pic.twitter.com/IQfU8vIXhY — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Ravens have some great pieces on defense Baltimore brought in Trey Hendrickson this offseason to bolster a pass rush that needed more production. He didn’t record a sack in Week 1, but he generated eight pressures against Indianapolis. He got his first sack as a Raven against New Orleans. Behind him, the Ravens still have some familiar names. Roquan Smith, Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey and Nate Wiggins give Baltimore plenty of veteran and young talent on the back end. Smith was particularly good in Week 1, recording an interception and earning Baltimore’s highest PFF grade on defense. Wiggins also had an excellent game against Indianapolis. But the Saints exposed some cracks. New Orleans finished with 298 total yards, including 233 through the air, and second-year quarterback Tyler Shough helped the Saints rally from a seven-point deficit in the fourth quarter. So, this isn’t necessarily the same suffocating Ravens defense we’ve seen in years past. There’s talent, there’s speed, but it’s still developing, and Dallas may be able to take advantage of it with their explosive offense. Fighting History, travel and the field? There isn’t much history between these two franchises, but what history they do have has been pretty one-sided. The Cowboys are 1-6 all-time against Baltimore, with their only victory coming in 2016. The Ravens have won the last two meetings, including a 28-25 victory in Dallas in 2024. So, yeah, Baltimore has Dallas’ number. On top of that, for the first time in franchise history, the Cowboys are playing a regular-season game in Rio de Janeiro. They’ll travel Thursday, practice in Brazil Friday and then play Sunday at Maracanã Stadium. That’s a different routine for an NFL team, and the Cowboys aren’t pretending otherwise. Brian Schottenheimer called it a “unique week”, with Dallas essentially shifting its normal practice schedule before making the overnight trip to Brazil. The travel itself isn’t necessarily what decides a football game, but it does add another variable. Players are leaving their normal routines, crossing an international border and adjusting to a new time zone and environment only days before playing a physically demanding game. And then there’s the field. This has become one of the bigger storylines surrounding the game. From a prominent sports journalist in Brazil we get a look at the field. His tweet reads: The Maracanã pitch is in TERRIBLE condition And then they’ll say on Monday, the 28th, that it’s the NFL’s fault. When the stadium hasn’t even managed the pitch well for football (soccer). O gramado do Maracanã tá em PÉSSIMAS condições E ai vão falar na segunda, dia 28, que é culpa da NFL. Sendo que o estádio não fez uma administração boa pro gramado nem pro futebol. pic.twitter.com/HCpPHhViwb — Danilo Lacalle (@danlacalle) September 21, 2026 Soccer players who regularly play at Maracanã have publicly criticized the playing surface in recent days. Flamengo goalkeeper Agustín Rossi described “bumps everywhere,” while midfielder Giorgian de Arrascaeta said the field had been getting worse. The stadium has also dealt with unusually heavy rainfall over the past six weeks. That’s obviously worth watching when you’re talking about NFL players wearing cleats and moving at full speed. The NFL, however, has pushed back on the concern. Field director Nick Pappas said Monday that the league was confident the surface would be ready, noting that the NFL had already sent a crew to Rio and shipped a tarp to help protect the turf. He also pointed out that some…
author: Jorge Guajardo

title: Brian Schottenheimer report card: Cowboys offense shines in week 2
summary: It’s really hard to call a week two game in the NFL a “must win” game, but boy was it ever for the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys defense was dominated in week one, and despite some offensive highlights, the Cowboys slow start on offense, along with just two possessions in the second-half saw them fall […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images It’s really hard to call a week two game in the NFL a “must win” game, but boy was it ever for the Dallas Cowboys. The Cowboys defense was dominated in week one, and despite some offensive highlights, the Cowboys slow start on offense, along with just two possessions in the second-half saw them fall short to the New York Giants. In week two however, the Cowboys offense got back to their “GOTI” form and dominated the matchup, despite the defensive still showing their struggles. On top of the players executing, Brian Schottenheimer was “in his bag” as the kids say nowadays. Schottenheimer received some pushback in week one after deciding to throw a fade to CeeDee Lamb for their first score of the game, instead of setting the tone by feeding Javonte Williams. I could not disagree more with the pushback. The Cowboys offensive line struggled to generate push in the running game in week one, and instead of trying to establish the run against a stout Washington defensive front, Schottenheimer leaned into his offense’s strength and threw the football all over the yard. The Cowboys lack of running game is no doubt concerning, but with Tyler Smith sidelined, Cooper Beebe currently struggling, and Terence Steele’s inconsistencies still showing up on tape, Schottenheimer decided to live-or-die with his best players in week two. The Cowboys running game generated -0.24 in EPA in their week two victory, while their passing game generated 0.46. Thankfully, it seems like Schottenheimer figured out it was going to be a tough day running the football pretty quickly, because the Cowboys offense called only 18 rushing plays throughout the game, and that’s with a quarterback sneak, a fullback dive, and a KaVontae Turpin end-around mixed in. Those 18 rushes, compared to 31 pass attempts, despite leading the entire game is why the Cowboys were able to keep their foot on the gas and continue to finish drives with points instead of punts. Schottenheimer’s play-calling was very good in week two and we saw a bit more creativity and explosiveness from the passing game that was lacking in week one. With the offensive line struggling to gain much traction in the running game, Schottenheimer is going to need to lean into the passing game more, until that unit starts to generate more consistent push up front. Leaning into the passing game is something the Cowboys offense has been very familiar with over the years, and something Dak Prescott and the Cowboys’ wide receivers handle very well. That proved to be true again in week two as Prescott, Lamb, and Ferguson came up big. Prescott threw just five incompletions all game with four touchdowns, 279 passing yards, and added 26 yards on the ground as well. CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson combined for three touchdowns, with Lamb hauling in eight receptions for 153 yards. While fans may want to see more success in the running game, Schottenheimer is smart to lean into what’s working and this week it was throwing it all over the yard. Play-Calling A Fourth-Down Decisions B+ There was only one fourth down decision to really ponder in week two. A 4th and 5 from the Washington 6. Schottenheimer elected to kick the field goal, but this is a down and distance he should be a bit more aggressive beginning with the third down play-call moving forward, if the defense is still going to struggle to get off the field and limit points. Timeout Usage B- Team Preparation B+ What grade would you give to Brian Schottenheimer on Sunday?
author: Connor Livesay

title: 3 things we learned about the Cowboys after Week 2 win
summary: The Dallas Cowboys where in what could have been seen as a must-win situation in Week 2 when they took on the Washington Commanders. Not only where they looking at an 0-2 hole to start the season, but they were also in danger of starting 0-2 in the NFC East. It wasn’t always pretty, but […]
full_text: Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys where in what could have been seen as a must-win situation in Week 2 when they took on the Washington Commanders. Not only where they looking at an 0-2 hole to start the season, but they were also in danger of starting 0-2 in the NFC East. It wasn’t always pretty, but the Cowboys were able to get their first win of the year. Quarterback Dak Prescott was in the zone as he put up 279 yards passing and four touchdowns while completing 26 of his 31 psass attempts. Dallas converted seven of their 11 third down chances, and they also scored touchdowns in three of their four red zone opportunities. Defensively, they still have some things to clean up. Which that said, they only allowed 20 points for the game which is something they can build on. Before they face one of their toughest challenges in Brazil this Sunday against the Baltimore Ravens, let’s take a look at three things we learned about the Cowboys in Week 2. Lamb is still Lamb He didn’t have the best outing in the season opener versus the New York Giants with just 44 yards. Against Washington, CeeDee Lamb went nuclear as he reminded everyone why he’s one of the top wide receivers on the planet. One the very first drive of the game, Lamb caught three passes for 41 yards and ended it with a touchdown. At game’s end, Lamb had eight receptions on nine targets and accumulated 153 yards and two scores. This was the ninth time in Lamb’s career that he registered two receiving touchdowns in one game, and it was the second time he’s done it against the Commanders in the last three seasons. When Lamb and Prescott are clicking on all cylinders, you’ll be hard-pressed to find a better quarterback/receiver duo in the league. Caleb Downs is as good as advertised It’s only been two games, but Downs is already showing why the Cowboys took him with the 11th overall pick back in April. After racking up eight tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble in his NFL debut, Downs was stellar again versus the Commanders. His nine tackles were tied for first on the team and he also registered another forced fumble and a pass breakup. Downs was all over the field making plays against the run and showing his instincts in coverage, which were on full display during a pass breakup on Terry McLaurin in the first half. He’s still making mistakes here and there, but that’s expected for a rookie. However, it’s clear that he will continue to be a vital piece in Christian Parker’s defense. We talked about miscommunication a lot last week. This Caleb Downs PBU looks like effective communication — and a really nice play from the rookie. https://t.co/UZs9TV94PR pic.twitter.com/HnBVxzTVkl — Joseph Hoyt (@JoeJHoyt) September 21, 2026 Jaishawn Barham is figuring it out It was a tough debut for Barham against the Giants, which led to him showing his frustration while talking to the aforementioned Parker on the sideline. However, after getting the green dot to call plays with DeMarvion Overshown on the shelf, Barham looked excellent against the Commanders even with some of the errors he made. He ended up with seven tackles, one tackle for loss, and a huge forced fumble in the third quarter which led to a Jake Ferguson touchdowns to put the Cowboys up by 14. . @jaishawnbarham forced fumble and the @dwintersdos recovery 🫡 📺: #WASvsDAL on FOX 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/XM2vIx7C1d pic.twitter.com/PVbUXHj4SO — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) September 20, 2026 He did a good job playing downhill as well as moving sideline-to-sideline against the run. Barham looked comfortable in getting guys in their right spots with his pre-snap checks and he looked good in coverage as well. Through the first two games, Barham is the highest-graded defensive rookie per Pro Football Focus . So, he’s laying the groundwork for a productive first year in the NFL as he continues to progress.
author: Matthew Lenix

title: Cowboys playoff tracker: What the 1-1 record says about their playoff chances
summary: It’s never too early to talk about the playoffs – even if some eager beaver is already frantically searching for the Jim Mora “Playoffs? Playoffs?” gif to offer a never-before-seen and totally original rebuttal to this playoff talk. Don’t be that guy. If you read our playoff tracker from last week, you’ll know that the […]
full_text: (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s never too early to talk about the playoffs – even if some eager beaver is already frantically searching for the Jim Mora “Playoffs? Playoffs?” gif to offer a never-before-seen and totally original rebuttal to this playoff talk. Don’t be that guy. If you read our playoff tracker from last week , you’ll know that the historical playoff rate for 1-1 teams is 43%. But that’s just one way to look at the playoff picture. ESPN for example uses their Football Power Index to calculate their playoff picture, and they have the Cowboys with a 57% chance of making the playoffs . Kalshi has the Cowboys’ playoff chances slightly lower at 50% right now . NFL.com on the other hand lists the Cowboys playoff probability at a much more moderate 40% . So there you have it: playoff probabilities between 40% and 57%, which feels pretty much like where a 1-1 team should be. At this moment in time, do you believe that the Cowboys will make the playoffs or not? Let us know your answer and reasoning in the comments.

title: 2026 NFL Week 3: Dallas Cowboys vs. Baltimore Ravens
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are 1-1 through the first two games of the season and their third is set to be a doozy. This week the Cowboys will travel to Brazil for a “home” game against the Baltimore Ravens. The Cowboys are the designated home team for this one, but instead of taking place at AT&T […]
full_text: Photo by Sam Hodde/Getty Images | Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are 1-1 through the first two games of the season and their third is set to be a doozy. This week the Cowboys will travel to Brazil for a “home” game against the Baltimore Ravens. The Cowboys are the designated home team for this one, but instead of taking place at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, it will be played at Maracanā Stadium in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The NFL is all about international growth. Field concerns have been a storyline since the Cowboys finished their last game, a 37-20 victory over the division rival Washington Commanders. This game will be very different as the Ravens present one of the greatest duo challenges to a defense, Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry. Below you will find our story stream with all articles relevant to the game. Last week, Dak Prescott became the Cowboys’ all-time leader in passing touchdowns, but he is going to have to throw plenty of them for Dallas to stand a chance in this game. CeeDee Lamb and Jake Ferguson each had a pair last week, but we are still waiting for George Pickens to find the endzone for the first time in 2026. The defense will be the main story for the Cowboys. Caleb Downs has played well in his first two games, but Christian Parker is going to have to get more from the likes of Quinnen Williams, Kenny Clark, and others along the defensive front. It should be quite the matchup. title: Bo Nix and Broncos’ offense preparing to battle revamped Rams defense
summary: Good morning, Broncos Country. This Sunday night, the Denver Broncos have a huge challenge going up against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime. Each team suffered losses in Week 1 of the season, but both rebounded in a big way to defeat their Week 2 opponents. Everyone knows the Rams have a high-powered offense led […]
full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Bo Nix #10 of the Denver Broncos looks on prior to the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Justin Edmonds/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country. This Sunday night, the Denver Broncos have a huge challenge going up against the Los Angeles Rams in primetime. Each team suffered losses in Week 1 of the season, but both rebounded in a big way to defeat their Week 2 opponents. Everyone knows the Rams have a high-powered offense led by quarterback Matthew Stafford—last year’s league MVP. They also have a good run game, two of the best wide receivers in the NFL, and a handful of different tight ends that will be a huge test for Defensive Coordinator Vance Joseph and his players. However, their revamped defense will certainly be something to keep your eyes on this weekend. After falling to the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC Championship game, the Rams pushed all their chips in to bring their defense from an average unit to an elite one. Yesterday after practice, quarterback Bo Nix talked about what has stood out to him throughout the week going over film while preparing for Sunday night’s gridiron battle. “They have a veteran defense. They have a really good front. They really play through their front four, their front five, the guys that are the defensive line that are in there. They’ve done a good job of building on their back end this off season with some corner depth. They’re going to be good, they’re going to provide a challenge for us,” stated Nix. The premier move for General Manager Les Snead was swinging a huge trade that sent rising star Jared Verse and a bounty of picks to the Cleveland Browns for Myles Garrett—a future Hall of Famer. After suffering an injury in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers, Garrett won’t be on the field to face the Broncos in just a few days. Several other players they brought in are poised to make an impact against Denver. As Nix mentioned, they added to their defensive backfield which was in desperate need of an infusion of talent. The premier acquisition at cornerback was trading for two-time All-Pro cornerback Trent McDuffie. They also inked his former teammate in Kansas City, Jaylen Watson, to a multi-year contract during free agency. However, one major addition to their defensive line will come into focus under the bright lights at Empower Field at Mile High. That’s the resurgence of Aaron Donald who came out of retirement to chase one more Super Bowl title with the Rams. One of the greatest defenders in NFL history, Donald was impressive in his outing last weekend and came back like he had never left. Nix is excited to be able to go head-to-head against one of the best to ever do it. Though knows limiting his impact and game-changing ability will be an absolute must for the Broncos to earn their second win of the season. “He’s going to provide a challenge that we haven’t necessarily faced before. He’s literally one of the best at his position of all time—you don’t play those many Sundays. He’s going to be a good player; he’s going to play more and more as the season goes with rep count. He’s just getting back in the swing of things, but a dominant player for a long time. I honestly don’t expect anything different, we just have to limit the time he’s dominant.” How the Broncos go about combatting Donald’s pass rushing prowess and penchant for making plays behind the line of scrimmage will be a huge story line to watch. There’s no doubt Denver’s offensive line, especially those on the interior, are going to have to play a great game to keep the future Hall of Famer from wrecking their game plan. As always, thank you for reading. Here is today’s slate of articles for Horse Tracks .

title: Sean Payton sees all his running backs as ‘bell cow’ type backs
summary: The Denver Broncos were down to their third and fourth string running backs for a period of time during their win over the Jacksonville Jaguars with rookie Jonah Coleman taking up a lion’s share of carries late in that game. full_text: DENVER, COLORADO - SEPTEMBER 20: Jonah Coleman #20 of the Denver Broncos runs the ball during the fourth quarter of a game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Empower Field At Mile High on September 20, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Denver Broncos were down to their third and fourth string running backs for a period of time during their win over the Jacksonville Jaguars with rookie Jonah Coleman taking up a lion’s share of carries late in that game. He was the driving force behind Denver securing the game-clinching four-minute drive to run the clock out. Head Coach Sean Payton was asked about his ability to carry a heavier workload if necessary. “So yesterday, RJ [Harvey] was out, and then J.K. [Dobbins] got nicked up and wasn’t able to finish,” Payton said. “None of that today on Monday is at a place where we’re—I think all three of those players we’re discussing can be bell cow, handle a majority of the carries. Yes, I think there’s a lot ahead of us this week relative to who our runners are going to be.” By saying all three can be ‘bell cow’ type running backs all but confirms his sentiment towards Coleman in the long-term. He is that guy. That being said, in 2026 the ‘bell cow’ backs will likely continue to be J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. That is who they have ahead of Coleman on the depth chart and — barring injury — it should remain that way. Though I wouldn’t mind seeing Coleman spell Dobbins more into a 60-40 type role. We shall see. Broncos daily recap Broncos vs Rams preview: Denver aims to stack wins The Broncos host the LA Rams on SNF after getting their first win of the season. Denver looks to build on that victory. Broncos vs. Jaguars stats analysis from Week 2 The Denver Broncos bounced back from from that humiliating loss to the Kansas City Chiefs to win a come-from-behind game against a very strong Jaguars team. The Jacksonville Jaguars had won nine straight regular season games coming into Sunday’s matchup with the Broncos, although they did lose to the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs last season. The Broncos offense is unlocked with Jaylen Waddle The Denver Broncos offense took off with Jaylen Waddle. Now others will benefit from him opening up passing lanes Potent Quotables Sean Payton On Seahawks Head Coach Mike Macdonald’s comments and if they talked “We spoke. He and I are good. Lord knows I’ve been in his position where you’re talking about something… The story is three years ago. I don’t know [Seahawks Head Coach] Mike [Macdonald] at that time really, but I know ‘Schneids’ really well, [Seahawks General Manager] John [Schneider]. I’m sure my initial call to John wasn’t pleasant. But I would say this: in talking with him, it allowed us to figure out how to handle our training camp relative to just videos. I don’t think anything was intentional by fans, but at first, you’re kind of thinking, ‘How could…’ Then we did some research online of what was available, and that’s kind of how we changed our policy. So I’ve known John for 20 years, so it was an easy call to him. That’s really it.” On if his first thought was not that the training camp videos were from fans “I didn’t know what the heck. Then all of the sudden you start realizing like, ‘This is all out there.’ So it helped us to some degree. Look, when I say this, we’re pulling for them except for one game. They’re playing our division. They’re in the NFC. Like I said, the conversation last night was good. I have a ton of respect for him, and that’s it.” On how they found out about the training camp videos “Unimportant. It’s really unimportant. I don’t know what time of the year… I know it seems like years ago. It was a ways ago.” On if he thought the Seahawks may have taped training camp “I didn’t know. So obviously I called shooting before I started looking. (Laughs) I could only do that with [Seahawks General Manager] John [Schneider] because again, he’s someone I’ll have a beer with at the Combine. I consider him a good friend. It was eye-opening relative to we have to be better in this area.” On if there is anything else from the video he wants to clarify “There’s nothing to clarify. We just got it.” On if there are any common threads that have allowed the team to win nine consecutive games against NFC opponents “I don’t know. Honestly until walking here, [Chief Communications Officer] Pat [Smyth] just said. Now if you win 14 games or 15 games, you’re probably going to have some sort of, ‘in a row,’ but I wasn’t aware of the NFC-AFC thing. It’s taken me a couple of years to figure out who I’m rooting against for being however many years in the NFC. So then pretty soon you figure it out.” On if it’s more difficult to scout NFC teams due to less common opponents “I think it’s a by-product of one year winning 10, one year winning… I really do. It’s not like baseball used to be. That was like groundbreaking when the American went and played the National [League]. It’s not only a rotation—call it four years—but then it’s also the additional game. You just see these teams. I think there’s probably more about just playing well.” On what has allowed the offense to be so successful in the fourth quarter and if there is anything they can translate to earlier in the game “That’s a great question. The last part of it, in other words, we talk about finishing. One of the things especially at home is… And we talked about it at the start of the season, playing better early. I think the focus is more on the front end. I think if you’re playing with a lead, obviously you have that balance. If you’re playing within a touchdown, you still have to have that balance. Last week was a good example really. It becomes difficult if it’s one dimensional in this league.” On if he sees himself in Head Coach Sean McVay “I consider him a good friend. I would think the one thing we had in common a little bit is both of us cut our teeth under [former NFL Head Coach Jon] Gruden at some point, myself in 1997 and then [Rams Head Coach] Sean [McVay] later. He’s done a fabulous job coming to an organization that had recently just moved to L.A. Then just the year-in and year-out success. That’s really what you begin to look at with coaches. I have a ton of respect for him. He’s sharp. You watch his film, it’s good film always to watch. Of course we had joint practices three years ago or whatever. We’ve always had a good relationship. It’ll be a good challenge.” On if he has concern at running back “I think we’re good at that position. Today one was limited and the other one didn’t practice, but I think we’re going to be alright.” On why CB Jahdae Barron hasn’t seen the field as much “Well some of it is the packages you’re in. Certainly he’s starting in dime. So a lot of it depends on the defensive gameplan and the opponent, what they’re doing. This is a group that the last couple of weeks, they’re in a lot of heavy personnel. So each week, that can vary.” On the trend of NFL teams using more heavy personnel and if they are trying to get CB Jahdae Barron on the field more “I think first is game planning the heavy, and understanding what teams do from it because it’s different, then defending it. So whether that involves him or other players, a lot of it is gameplan.” On Rams DE Aaron Donald returning and how he looked on Monday night “Good. Really good. He’s one of those guys that obviously, he’s in great shape. To be able to do that and play at a position inside where that’s not easy… Certainly tracked him his whole career, and he’s something else.” On if he remembers watching the Broncos-Rams game in 2022 and if Denver was on his radar at that point “I was at the Denver-Chargers game. I don’t know why. I was invited. I think it was Sunday Night Football , overtime… Monday night. I was at that game just because I was living near L.A. I don’t really recall the game you’re referencing. I kind of do. When was that, Christmas?” On when he thought of Denver…

title: Broncos vs. Jaguars stats analysis from Week 2
summary: The Denver Broncos bounced back from from that humiliating loss to the Kansas City Chiefs to win a come-from-behind game against a very strong Jaguars team. The Jacksonville Jaguars had won nine straight regular season games coming into Sunday’s matchup with the Broncos, although they did lose to the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs last […]
full_text: The Denver Broncos bounced back from from that humiliating loss to the Kansas City Chiefs to win a come-from-behind game against a very strong Jaguars team. The Jacksonville Jaguars had won nine straight regular season games coming into Sunday’s matchup with the Broncos, although they did lose to the Buffalo Bills in the playoffs last season. The Bronco defense which was atrocious against the Chiefs in missing 24 tackles, missed only 3 tackles against the Jaguars. Both Alex Singleton and DJ Jones were tagged with four missed tackles in the loss to the Chiefs. Neither player had a missed tackle against the Jaguars. While the Bronco defense is still “leading” the NFL in missed tackles with 27, the Colts are close with 22. After missing 24 tackles in week 1, the Bronco defense missed only 3 in week 2. pic.twitter.com/ksg7lDUOtX — Joe Mahoney (@ndjomo76) September 22, 2026 What concerns me more than the missed tackles is the lack of pressure. The Broncos are only getting pressure on 20.3 percent of dropbacks. That is currently 23rd. Two defenses are getting pressure on more than 40% of opponent dropbacks, The Raiders and the Vikings. In terms of allowing pressure, the Bronco offense is currently 15th according to PFR – allowing pressure on 21.9 percent of dropbacks. The best pass blocking team right now (by pressure allowed) is the 49ers (9.38 percent). The worst pass blocking team right now is the Panthers allowing pressure on an astounding 41.5 percent of dropbacks. By most accounts the Broncos allowed a great deal of pressure on Bo Nix in game one and they were much better in game two. NFL.com shows that the Broncos allowed seven QB pressures in game 1 and only three in game two . The Jaguars got 10 pressures on the Browns the week before . The Bronco run game was mostly silent in week one partly because of the lack of run plays. Denver had 14 actual runs (kneeldowns count as runs in the NFL STILL, for some stupid reason) for 62 yards (4.43 YPC). That’s respectable, but the run game was not employed very often. The Broncos had 25 actual runs for 107 yards on Sunday against the Jaguars (4.28 YPC). The Broncos have been about average in terms of avoiding wasted run plays. Denver has five runs that gained 11 or more yards – one by Pat Bryant, two by JK Dobbins and two by Jonah Coleman – that’s 12.8 percent. So far the average NFL team gets 16.7% stuffed, 24.3 % gaining 1-2 yards, 31% gaining 3-5 yards, 18.8% gaining 6-10 yards, and 9.2% gaining 11 or more yards. Every team in the NFL has as least one long run with the exception of the Browns. The Texans have been the worst at getting 28 percent of their runs stuffed (no gain or loss). The Broncos had 48 runs in 2025 that gained 11 or more yards with JK Dobbins getting 19, Bo Nix 13, RJ Harvey 8, Jaleel McLaughlin 4, Marvin Mims 2, and Troy Franklin and Adam Prentice both had one. The run game looked much better against the Jaguars than it did against the Chiefs. The Broncos have 11 total runs that gained 6 or more yards, with eight of those coming against Jacksonville and only three coming against Kansas City. The defense did a much better job of stopping the run against the Jaguars. After giving up 223 rushing yards on 35 actual runs (6.37 YPC) the week before, the Broncos allowed 95 yards on 24 carries on Sunday (3.96 YPC). The Denver defense is still 30th in the NFL in YPC allowed, but they were 31st after week one. Not missing tackles is good for stopping the run.

title: The Broncos offense is unlocked with Jaylen Waddle
summary: Thinking back to last week’s win, I think that may have been the first time that the Broncos under Sean Payton have used the same player over and over again throughout the game offensively to dominate the opponent. Jaylen Waddle popped off with 8 catches for 138 yards. I think that is notable because this […]
full_text: Thinking back to last week’s win, I think that may have been the first time that the Broncos under Sean Payton have used the same player over and over again throughout the game offensively to dominate the opponent. Jaylen Waddle popped off with 8 catches for 138 yards. I think that is notable because this is not what the Sean Payton offense does. His offense is never that simple. Payton beats teams by scheming players into plus situations and creating plays from any player at any depth on the roster. Heck, Nate Adkins popped off from the tight end room last week (which doesn’t surprise me…he’s probably the best 2-way tight end on the team). But what’s worth noting is that Waddle showed the capability to create his own separation over and over. Bo Nix showed that he trusts and understands where to lead Waddle with that blazing speed. We’ll see more of this as the season wears on, but one thing to watch is not what Waddle does in the next few weeks. No, look out for who else gets big plays off the pressure Waddle is now going to create as teams start doubling him and running coverage games to remove his deep crossers. We’ll likely see some big games from Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, and RJ Harvey in the near future that you will be able to point to Waddle’s clearing route opening up holes in the defense that Payton and protegee Davis Webb are going to attack. The Broncos needed a talent infusion on offense just for this reason. The offense is going to be able to really start humming as you give one of the league’s best offensive minds more ways to scheme guys open. title: Lions, Jets injury report: 2 starting OL return to practice, another safety down
summary: As the Detroit Lions (1-1) enter Week 3 of the 2026 season, they will finally get back to a “normal” in-season workweek. Coming off a Thursday night game, the Lions got a couple of extra days of rest before practices this week, spending most of that time in the film room correcting mistakes, but now […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 13: Offensive tackle Blake Miller (76) of the Detroit Lions holds back defensive end Carl Granderson (96) of the New Orleans Saints during the an NFL football game between the New Orleans Saints and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 13, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images As the Detroit Lions (1-1) enter Week 3 of the 2026 season, they will finally get back to a “normal” in-season workweek. Coming off a Thursday night game, the Lions got a couple of extra days of rest before practices this week, spending most of that time in the film room correcting mistakes, but now that Wednesday has arrived, they’re back on the practice field as they prepare to host the New York Jets on Sunday afternoon. Let’s take a look at Wednesday’s injury report and get you up to date with what we know. Note: Any changes from the most recent injury report will be bolded . Injured list updates RB Isiah Pacheco (MCL/Back) — injured reserve, expected to be out until December C Cade Mays (Wrist) — injured reserve OL Giovanni Manu (Undisclosed) — NFI S Brian Branch (Achilles) — PUP S Kerby Joseph (Knee) — PUP S Avonte Maddox (foot) — injured reserve, expected to be out for the season A new NFL rule allows any player on PUP to open their return-to-play practice window after just two weeks into the regular season, but unfortunately, neither Branch nor Joseph is healthy enough to begin that process this week . “I think Branch has a chance to be back sooner than Kerby, but it won’t be this week,” coach Dan Campbell told the media on Monday. While Branch is consistently making progress, every update on Joseph gets bleaker by the report . On Tuesday, Campbell told 97.1 The Ticket that Joseph continues to work to strengthen his knee, and despite being in this stage of recovery for roughly a year, he’s still not ready, with no clear sign of when that will happen. “It’s going to come as it comes, and he’s not ready,” Campbell explained. “We’re trying to get him there as fast as we can, and we’re trying to be as smart about it as we can. And if he’s ready, when he’s ready, of course we want to play him and get him on the field.” Things got even tougher at safety, as Maddox injured his foot in Week 2 and will miss the remainder of the season after requiring surgery . N o practice G Ben Bartch (foot) — New injury DT Alim McNeill (personal) — New addition S Thomas Harper (ankle) — New injury Batch did not appear to suffer an injury against the Bills last Thursday, but it’s possible his injury showed up after the fact, as we saw with Blake Miller in Week 2. We won’t get an official update on his status until coach Dan Campbell speaks with the media again on Friday, but he’ll be a name to watch when the Thursday injury report is released. McNeill’s absence was expected, as Campbell notified the media ahead of practice and suggested that it was a non-issue: “Mac won’t be out there. There’s nothing to it. He’ll be back ready. I mean, he’ll be back here probably just when practice ends, so no big deal and be ready to roll.” Harper, like Bartch, didn’t appear to suffer an injury in Week 2, but with Maddox landing on injured reserve and neither Branch nor Joseph ready to return, this situation is potentially very concerning. While it’s not 100% certain that he is next in line to step into the starting lineup, if he can’t go, the Lions secondary would be limited to just Chuck Clark and Christian Izien as capable starters. Though this week the Lions added safeties Jalen Mills (practice squad) and Bishop Fitzgerald (53-man roster). Harper had a boot on in the locker room today, which he described as precautionary. "Just trying to stay off of it." He said the ankle injury "shouldn't be long term," and he'd "know a little bit later in the week" about his status for Sunday vs. the Jets. https://t.co/5jZEAGJVWn — Richard Silva (@rich_silva18) September 23, 2026 Limited practice LG Christian Mahogany (hip) — returned to practice after missing last game RT Blake Miller (knee) — returned to practice after missing last game RG Tate Ratledge (elbow) — New injury EDGE Ahmed Hassanein (illness) — New injury Campbell had previously noted that Mahogany was expected to practice this week, and he did indeed get some reps in. title: 6 Lions vs. Jets thoughts after watching New York’s loss to Packers
summary: In order to prepare for Week 3’s game between the New York Jets and Detroit Lions, I watched the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers to get a better sense of how Aaron Glenn’s team is playing amidst their 1-1 start. Here are six things I learned. The Jets offensive line looks […]
full_text: New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn signals during a game between the New York Jets and the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, Sep 20, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co In order to prepare for Week 3’s game between the New York Jets and Detroit Lions, I watched the Jets’ Week 2 loss to the Green Bay Packers to get a better sense of how Aaron Glenn’s team is playing amidst their 1-1 start. Here are six things I learned. The Jets offensive line looks improved Now, this could very well be the result of an extremely questionable Packers pass rush without Micah Parsons, but Geno Smith had all day to pass against the Packers defense. The Jets’ offensive line averaged 2.71 second to pressure, the seventh-highest mark of Week 2 (they ranked 10th in Week 1). New York currently has PFF’s highest pass blocking grade (77.4) and seventh-highest run blocking grade (70.0). Where they’re particularly strong is on the left side, where third-year left tackle Olu Fashanu is having a great start and veteran left guard Dylan Parham (PFF’s #1 graded guard) has been outstanding. It’s no surprise the Jets’ most successful runs are to the offense’s left. EPA/Rush by run gap through week 2 pic.twitter.com/Eb1nfWHHeF — Ray Carpenter (@csv_enjoyer) September 22, 2026 While Aidan Hutchinson moves around quite a bit, DJ Wonnum spends the majority of the time opposite the left tackle, so it’s a big game for him. Run game has had mixed results The Jets ran for 152 yards and 3.9 yards per carry in Week 1 vs. the Titans, but they managed just 67 rushing yards and 2.5 yards per carry against the Packers. There were far too many negative plays for New York running the football, with 29.6% of their rushes gaining zero or fewer yards—the third-highest mark of Week 2. Even in Week 1, they managed just 0.82 yards before contact (25th), so there should be plenty of opportunities for the Lions defense to get the Jets behind the sticks. The Packers were able to be disruptive by being aggressive with their linebacking corps. I got the sense the Jets were being a little predictable in the run game. Through two weeks, the Jets have the second-highest early-down run rate in the NFL. Tough to beat in passing game in perimeters, but inside may be available On defense, I was impressed by the Jets’ ability to defend the perimeter in the passing game. That meant slowing down the Packers’ wide receiver screens, but also erasing the sidelines on deeper throws. As you can see, most of Jordan Love’s work came over the middle of the field. Love completed a lot of passes near the line of scrimmage, but those plays were largely ineffective. It was the intermediate stuff over the middle that finally got Green Bay’s offense going. Of course, that could play into Detroit’s strengths. Guys like Sam LaPorta and Amon-Ra St. Brown thrive over the middle of the field. But I would stay away from No. 1 cornerback Azareye’h Thomas. The second-year corner was excellent against the Packers, and PFF credited him with a 75.9 coverage grade this season, and he was also outstanding against the run vs. Green Bay. Run defense has some hidden leaks On the surface, it looks like the Jets have an awesome run defense. They rank: Second in rushing yards allowed (66.5 YPG) 18th in YPC (4.1) Third in rush EPA (-0.378) Ninth in rush success rate (32.3%) But when the Packers were at their best against the Jets, they were able to get the run game going pretty well, particularly in the first half. Green Bay rushed eight times for 35 yards (4.4 YPC)—all of which came on their first touchdown drive. If Green Bay could’ve stuck with the running game and not gotten behind the sticks with 15 penalties, I believe the game would have worked out differently. Through two weeks, the Jets have produced just a 9.4% stuffed rate (27th), and have given up 3.30 yards after contact per attempt (23rd). In short, I think some of their early run defense success may be a result of playing a Packers team down several offensive linemen and a Titans team that spent the entire second half down two scores. They’ve faced an NFL-low 32 rushing attempts, so they’ve yet to be really tested, but the cracks in the foundation are there. But one thing to keep an eye on: fumbles. The Jets forced five (!) fumbles against the Packers, but only recovered one. Coaching decisions, conservative play could be a big issue The Jets should have beaten the Packers. They were the better team for approximately 55 minutes of that game and on a success rate basis, they were dominant . However, there were several very questionable coaching decisions that Aaron Glenn is rightfully under fire for. At the end of the first half, the Jets got the ball back with four minutes left and no timeouts (another coaching issue). New York seemed more concerned about ensuring the Packers didn’t get the ball back, and they essentially erased all four minutes without getting in field goal range (to be fair, the drive did start at their own 9-yard line). Still, that level of conservative play likely cost them at least a field goal attempt. The fourth quarter was far worse. First, the Jets faced a fourth-and-1 from the Packers’ 9-yard line up a touchdown. Rather than go for the kill, they kicked a field goal to go up 10. Then, they had an opportunity to get one more possession before overtime. When Green Bay failed to convert a third-and-10 from midfield, the Jets could’ve called a timeout with over a minute left. Instead, Glenn said he was worried about being backed up in his own zone and wanted to play for overtime. Then, in overtime, Glenn made the controversial decision to take the ball first. Typically teams want to go second in overtime, to know what sense of urgency they need on offense (i.e. do they need a FG? A TD?) plus it gives the second-team’s chance to go for a two-point conversion for the win. Glenn believed they could run a bunch of overtime clock and put the pressure on Green Bay’s offense. Instead, they went three-and-out and lost. The Jets did get aggressive on one occasion against the Packers. With 1:20 left in a tie game, New York faced a fourth-and-1 at midfield. The Jets went for it, but a predictable run up the middle was stuffed. In a close game, Detroit’s more aggressive mindset could give them the edge. Special teams were a disaster Here are all the of the mistakes I saw the Jets make on special teams in one game: (Former Lions) punt returner Isaiah Williams muffed two punts, but the Jets recovered each Allowed a 43-yard kick return to the Packers’ own 46-yard line Allowed a 63-yard punt return that set up Packers’ game-tying field goal Four penalties on the return teams Overall, the Jets rank 26th in special teams DVOA, 23rd in punt return average, 22nd in kick return average, 31st in punt return average allowed, and 13th in kick return average allowed. If the issues continue, this is the kind of thing that could swing the result of a close game on Sunday.

title: Detroit Lions mailbag: What shakeups are coming on defense?
summary: Changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense. After giving up the second-most points through two weeks and having an extended weekend to diagnose their problems, Lions coach Dan Campbell promised changes were coming. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said Monday. “We’re going […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NY - SEPTEMBER 17: Christian Izien #5 of the Detroit Lions lines up before the snap during an NFL game against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium on September 17, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Changes are coming for the Detroit Lions defense. After giving up the second-most points through two weeks and having an extended weekend to diagnose their problems, Lions coach Dan Campbell promised changes were coming. “We’re going to do a couple of things defensively. We’re going to move some guys around,” Campbell said Monday. “We’re going to give some guys some more opportunities to play here and shake it up a little bit. And because they’ve earned that, we’ve got some guys in here that have earned some play time that they deserve a chance to do more for us.” On top of that, the Lions have to make some adjustments in the secondary after losing starting safety Avonte Maddox for the season to a foot injury. They started by signing Jalen Mills to the practice squad and poaching rookie safety Bishop Fitzgerald, but more mixing and matching is certainly on the way. On this week’s Midweek Mailbag podcast, Erik Schlitt and I offer ideas and depth chart shakeups the Lions may consider moving forward. Our discussion starts at safety, where the Lions have some choices to make. Will the Lions roll with Chuck Clark and Thomas Harper as starters, or will Christian Izien take over one of those roles? Schlitt suggests the Lions may have a three-person rotation at safety moving forward. But if the Lions pull Izien from the nickel position, how will that impact the cornerback room? Will Roger McCreary become the full-time starter, or will rookie Keith Abney see more opportunities? If it’s McCreary, then the domino effect continues at outside cornerback. Who is CB3? Is this where Ennis Rakestraw or Nick Whiteside get the call-up to the game-day roster? And is Rock Ya-Sin’s starting job in jeopardy? That conversation kicks off this week’s podcast, but there are plenty of topics we cover this week, including: Is it practical to simplify the defense right now? Why does the defense keep looking good in training camp, but fail to carry it over to the regular season? Are safeties more important than cornerbacks in this defense? Is Brad Holmes to blame for early extensions that have backfired because of injury (Kerby Joseph, Alim McNeill)? Does Kelvin Sheppard need a senior defensive assistant? What’s more likely: Campbell fires Sheppard midseason, the Lions hire a defensive assistant, or Detroit rides out the season and reassesses in 2027? Why does Dan Campbell have such a short leash on offensive coordinators, but leeway for Aaron Glenn and Sheppard? When, if ever, will the Lions get offensive weapon reserves (Jacob Saylors, Tay Martin, Tom Kennedy) involved in the offense? You can hear our answers to the questions by searching “Pride of Detroit” on any of your favorite podcasting platforms, or just use the Spotify embed below: If you’d like the watch the podcast, which has a ton of extra content in between segments that is not included on the audio version, you can catch replays over on our YouTube page and Twitch channel .

title: Free agent RB Jamaal Williams contacted Detroit Lions about a reunion
summary: Jamaal Williams was one of the most beloved players for the Detroit Lions during his two-year stint with the team from 2021-22. His energy was palpable, he showed leadership in times of strife, and he was also pretty dang good, rushing for 17 touchdowns in 2022—a franchise high at the time. He left Detroit after […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - JANUARY 01: Jamaal Williams #30 of the Detroit Lions reacts after the Lions defeated the Chicago Bears, 41-10, at Ford Field on January 01, 2023 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jamaal Williams was one of the most beloved players for the Detroit Lions during his two-year stint with the team from 2021-22. His energy was palpable, he showed leadership in times of strife, and he was also pretty dang good, rushing for 17 touchdowns in 2022—a franchise high at the time. He left Detroit after a free agency contract dispute, and his career fizzled away after two unsuccessful years with the New Orleans Saints. Williams has been out of football since the end of the 2024 season, but he wants back, and he’s been keeping in shape to do so. Apparently he is very much interested in a reunion in Detroit, despite a slightly messy divorce in 2023 . Williams told the Detroit Free Press this past weekend that he called Lions coach Dan Campbell about a possible return to Detroit. Campbell responded that they’d keep the door open, but his services were not needed at this time. “He reached out to Lions coach Dan Campbell last weekend to let Campbell know he was on the comeback trail,” Dave Birkett wrote. “And while Campbell said the Lions are holding tight at running back for now but would keep him in mind if things change, Williams is hopeful he’ll land a job soon and ready to contribute when he does.” As for the way things ended in Detroit, Williams doesn’t take it personally. “I didn’t want to go nowhere. I wanted to be there,” Williams told Birkett. “That’s where I wanted to be, but at the same time it’s just like, ‘We just got done having this crazy season, what am I doing that you don’t think I deserve?’ And they had their right, they have their things and it’s cool. And then at the time, it was just the Saints who offered what I wanted. They gave it to me and I ended up there. And that’s pretty much it. There’s no personal feelings, no hard feelings.” The Lions are down their RB2 with Isiah Pacheco sidelined indefinitely after going through back surgery recently . Reports suggest Pacheco won’t be back until December at the earliest, potentially leaving a power back role for someone like Williams. However, the Lions have increased the workload of Jahmyr Gibbs, which has severely lessened the role of backup running back in Detroit. Through two weeks, Gibbs’ is currently tied with Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker for the most touches in the NFL (56). Beyond that, the Lions have shown a lot of faith in 2024 fourth-round pick Sione Vaki to pick up the slack. Though he only has three rushes and two catches, Vaki has played 33 offensive snaps, providing Gibbs with some rest and the Lions offense with a decent pass protector. Detroit also has Jacob Saylors, a strong special teamer who proved he has some rushing skills when he led the NFL in rushing yards this preseason. As Campbell told Williams, their situation could certainly change. But, for now, it looks like any hope for a reunion between the Lions and Williams is not in the cards.

title: Detroit Lions scouting report: Jets are improved, but by how much?
summary: With an embarrassing performance on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions turn the page and shift their attention to the New York Jets. Lions head coach Dan Campbell has faced his former offensive coordinator in Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, winning both games, and now he’s facing off against former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: The defensive team of the New York Jets celebrate after recovering a fumble during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images With an embarrassing performance on “Thursday Night Football,” the Detroit Lions turn the page and shift their attention to the New York Jets. Lions head coach Dan Campbell has faced his former offensive coordinator in Chicago Bears head coach Ben Johnson, winning both games, and now he’s facing off against former defensive coordinator Aaron Glenn. Glenn’s looking to improve after an awful 2025 in his head-coaching debut season and keep his head above water. Detroit enters the contest 1-1, and after a tough loss on national television, they’ll be hungry to get back on the field and right the wrongs of last week. New York is also 1-1 and coming off an overtime loss to the Green Bay Packers at home. The Lions need this win badly to wash the bad taste out of their mouths early in the season. The Jets will want to bounce back from the win they fumbled and regain momentum. Let’s take a deep look at the Jets and how much they’ve changed ahead of Week 3. New York Jets 2025 season 3-14 record (4th in AFC East) 29th in points for, 31st in points allowed Overall DVOA: 32nd (30th on offense, 31st on defense) 2025 was not a fun introduction to being a head coach for Glenn. The defense was a laughing stock in the NFL, and the offense had a revolving door at quarterback. Injuries also didn’t help the team’s chances of putting something together. After having successful seasons in Detroit, Glenn got another taste of what it’s like to be at the bottom again. At quarterback, the Jets had Justin Fields, Tyrod Taylor, and Brady Cook all start last season. Together, the trio threw for 2,385 yards, 15 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions. Fields was the best of the three, throwing for seven touchdowns and only one interception, but he was benched by Glenn after starting 2-7. Taylor and Cook could manage only one win between them, and neither threw more touchdowns than interceptions. The Jets leaned on the ground game, with running back Breece Hall rushing for 1,065 yards, averaging 4.4 yards per carry, and tying with Fields for the most rushing touchdowns with four. While they didn’t find the end zone often, the unit was their most consistent. Star receiver Garrett Wilson only played in seven games and still finished as the team’s top receiver with 395 yards and four touchdowns on 36 catches. Rookie tight end Mason Taylor impressed with 44 catches, 369 yards, and a touchdown. The defense is where this team fell apart the most, as they had the fewest takeaways in the NFL with four, all fumbles. The Jets became the first team in NFL history to go a full season without recording a single interception. The best player on defense was EDGE Will McDonald IV, who led the team with eight sacks. With the defense struggling, the Jets traded both DT Quinnen Williams and CB Sauce Gardner to help kick-start a full rebuild. Overall, it was a disaster of a season for the Jets. The biggest problem was the defense, which allowed the second-most points in the league at 29.6. Glenn didn’t impress and fired multiple assistant coaches after the season, bringing an overhaul to the coaching staff. 2026 offseason Key additions: EDGE Joseph Ossai, LB Demario Davis, DL David Onyemata, EDGE Kingsley Enagbare, K Jason Sanders, DT T’Vondre Sweat (trade), S Minkah Fitzpatrick (trade), QB Geno Smith (trade) Key losses: G Alijah Vera-Tucker, G John Simpson, LB Quincy Williams, EDGE Michael Clemons, K Nick Folk, EDGE Jermaine Johnson II (trade) 2026 NFL Draft picks Round 1: EDGE David Bailey Round 1: TE Kenyon Sadiq Round 1: WR Omar Cooper Jr. Round 2: CB D’Angelo Ponds Round 4: DT Darrell Jackson Jr. Round 4: QB Cade Klubnik Round 6: G Anez Cooper Round 7: S VJ Payne Jets general manager Darren Mougey made some big moves via trade to give the team new life, trading for safety Minkah Fitzpatrick and defensive tackle T’Vondre Sweat. That wasn’t the only move on defense: he signed more EDGE rushers in Joseph Ossai and Kingsley Enagbare, while also adding interior help with defensive lineman David Onyemata and linebacker Demario Davis. On offense, more people left than arrived, as the team traded for quarterback Geno Smith to be their starter but lost both starting guards, John Simpson and Alijah Vera-Tucker. The defense also lost EDGE Jermaine Johnson in the trade for Sweat, along with linebacker Quincy Williams and EDGE Michael Clemons in free agency. Even special teams saw kicker Nick Folk move on before getting replaced by Jason Sanders. Once the draft started, the Jets got help in multiple spots, first on defense, drafting EDGE David Bailey to add firepower to that defensive line. The offense got two good weapons in tight end Kenyon Sadiq and wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr., relieving pressure on Wilson to do all the heavy lifting. New York shifted focus back to defense, selecting cornerback D’Angelo Ponds in the second round and defensive tackle Darrell Jackson Jr. in the fourth. To round things out, they drafted project quarterback Cade Klubnik, who they hope could be their future starter, and added depth on the offensive line and in the secondary. In the end, this team went hard to address its defensive issues from 2025, revamping its entire defensive line, improving its linebacker room and secondary. The offense could use more attention, but with a coach like Glenn, he’ll believe the defense can do the heavy lifting. After what happened in 2025, if the defense can even be a fraction better, this team can win more games in 2026. 2026 season thus far (1-1) Week 1: Defeated Tennessee Titans 23-10 Week 2: Lost to Green Bay Packers 20-17 (OT) Stats: 20th in points scored, 6th in points allowed Overall DVOA: 8th (14th on offense, 3rd on defense, 26th on special teams) The Jets have had a tale of two games so far this season. The Week 1 win against the Tennessee Titans was a strong defensive showing, holding the Titans to 195 total yards, getting three sacks, and recovering a fumble. The offense was average, with the running game as the heavy hitter, and it scored twice. It was a step in the right direction for the team that only captured a victory three times in 2025. Week 2 against the Green Bay Packers was similar, but also vastly different in a way. First, the defense played well again, holding the Packers to 199 total yards, getting three sacks, and recovering a fumble. That part is familiar, but the offense and coaching took a step back. After rushing for over 150 yards against Tennessee, New York only mustered 67 yards and found the end zone once. The Jets defense again did all it could to win the game, but the offense could only give them a 10-point lead in the fourth quarter before it all went south. New York allowed Green Bay to come back in the fourth quarter and force overtime. The coaching issues came in the fourth quarter, toward the end of regulation. Green Bay completed a 5-yard pass to make it fourth-and-5 at the Jets’ 45, and instead of calling a timeout with about a minute left, Glenn allowed the Packers to drain essentially all of the clock, giving Green Bay an opportunity at a game-winning hail mary with no risk. Then, once overtime started, the Jets made the controversial decision to take the ball first. It immediately backfired when Smith was sacked twice in a quick three-and-out. The defense would allow Green Bay to move down the field and kick the game-winning field goal. It was a massive failure by the team and completely erased all the good they had from the previous week. So far this season, the defense has carried the team, and the offense can’t seem to get things going through the air with Smith. He’s been accurate with a 70.8 completion percentage, but he has only one touchdown…

title: Do the Falcons Have the Worst QB Room?
summary: There is an old saying about quarterbacking: if you have two quarterbacks, you have no quarterbacks. The Atlanta Falcons have four quarterbacks, which means they have negative two quarterbacks? And before you tell me that my math is stupid, please note that so far Cooper Rush leads the NFL with four interceptions, which is a […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images There is an old saying about quarterbacking: if you have two quarterbacks, you have no quarterbacks. The Atlanta Falcons have four quarterbacks, which means they have negative two quarterbacks? And before you tell me that my math is stupid, please note that so far Cooper Rush leads the NFL with four interceptions, which is a pretty big negative, while Jack Strand is 6-4 and 243 pounds, which also makes him a literal big negative. The Falcons also have Tua Tagovailoa, who has an oblique injury, and let’s be honest, probably a concussion, along with a likely ego hit at not being the starter. And then there’s Michael Penix, who suffered a season-ending injury in five of his last eight seasons of football, including a torn ACL in November, but has recovered and will be starting on Thursday. It’s a complete conceptual disaster. If I wanted a quarterback room to fail, this is the kind of thing I’d put together. Jack Strand doesn’t really matter because he’s just a longshot developmental prospect, but Tua is too established to be a backup, and excels at the short passing game due to a pop-gun arm and quick release. Rush, while terrible so far, is a good enough backup to garner the support of talk radio rubes everywhere. And Penix is an elite athlete when healthy, having posted a 9.75 RAS, and he excels as a deep passer, but he’s never healthy, and the Falcons aren’t really built for deep passing. Drake London is a great player, but he excels at short and intermediate routes, while every other Atlanta receiver of note is one of the teeniest, tiniest cute little guys in the league. Jahan Dotson is a WR prospect in the 2022 draft class. He scored a 6.02 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 1040 out of 2613 WR from 1987 to 2022. https://t.co/Q1kosRb3ZK #RAS pic.twitter.com/EzbhimmPGJ — RAS.football (@MathBomb) March 23, 2022 Zachariah Branch was drafted in round 3 with pick 79 in the 2026 draft class. He scored a 9.12 RAS out of a possible 10.00. This ranked 370 out of 4196 WR from 1987 to 2026. https://t.co/AJibOVFRpG pic.twitter.com/P5TPFt3xTI — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 25, 2026 Olamide Zaccheaus went undrafted in the 2019 draft class. Olamide Zaccheaus posted a Good #RAS with V.Poor size, Good speed, Good explosiveness, Good agility at the WR position. #Falcons pic.twitter.com/pGv3Ink6Hv — RAS.football (@MathBomb) April 30, 2019 Olamide Zaccheaus too! It’s not a crime to be small, but Penix was at his best in college throwing to larger vertical threats like Rome Odunze and Ja’Lynn Polk, and that is not what we have here. The Falcons do have Kyle Pitts, and maybe he’s the real wide receiver two on this team. To his credit, he had a nice rebound season last year after being a perpetual disappointment, but he only averaged 10.5 yards per catch. Bijan Robinson is of course the best player on the offense, and he can help out any quarterback, but at some point, you need to pass. I think Tua is objectively the best choice if you can get him on the field and keep him on the field, but he’s also objectively not the future as a 28-year-old who is one concussion away from never playing again. And Penix cost the team draft capital, so they have every incentive to make him work, although he is every bit as injury-prone as Tua, hence the need to keep Rush around. More than anything, you will probably get a different Atlanta team every time you play them based on who is behind center, which isn’t that different from last year. In 2025, this team beat the Bills and Rams (and almost the Pats) but also lost to the Jets and Dolphins. So far, with Rush at the helm, the Falcons have not run a single offensive play in the red zone over their first two games. And while Penix is kind of a weird fit (phrasing, I know), they probably won’t be quite as atrocious on Thursday, especially as Thursday produces weird results generally, and the Packers aren’t exactly the picture of health. Green Bay should win this game, but I don’t think I’ve ever seen a beginning to a season that is less predictive in terms of what is about to happen, and the weird, bizarre, dysfunctional Falcons QB room makes predicting them a nightmare. The Packers and their terrible guards played against the 80% blitz Vikings, and in terrible weather in New York. The Falcons haven’t had a healthy starting quarterback to run their new offense with their new head coach (Kevin Stefanski replacing Raheem Morris). But I suppose with Penix, who is the intended starter, this game should be a relatively “normal” (other than taking place on Thursday). And other than Za’Darius Smith almost definitely getting a revenge sack , Let’s see how the Packers react to “normal.”
