title: What a Packers game-day roster could look like: Week 3
summary: This week’s edition of playing out the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster decisions will be much simpler than past ones, since there are fewer moving parts. The Packers have already ruled out four players for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons, and they’re at positions where they were already “oversigned,” so their roster can […]
full_text: (Photo by Ross Harried/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images This week’s edition of playing out the Green Bay Packers’ game-day roster decisions will be much simpler than past ones, since there are fewer moving parts. The Packers have already ruled out four players for Thursday Night Football against the Atlanta Falcons , and they’re at positions where they were already “oversigned,” so their roster can withstand the numbers there. The only question is how the team will use their final inactive spot, or if both of their questionable players (DL Anthony Campbell and Javon Hargrave) will both miss the game. If that happens, the Packers will probably need to call up Eric Johnson II from the practice squad, despite him just arriving in Green Bay last week . That’s really it! Below is what the Packers’ roster will likely look like, unless they throw a curveball at us. Quarterback In: Jordan Love and Tyrod Taylor Out: None Running Back In: Chris Brooks, Kaleb Johnson and MarShawn Lloyd Out: None Receiver In: Christian Watson (Z), Matthew Golden (X), Skyy Moore (slot), Bo Melton (X) and J. Michael Sturdivant (Z) Out: Jayden Reed (injury) The Packers’ receiver room has been very rigid dating back to the preseason, with players firmly locked into Z, X and slot positions. With Jayden Reed out, Skyy Moore is the backup slot on the team and is expected to fill in the snaps that Reed played. With that being said, though, now that push has come to shove, I wouldn’t be surprised to see Bo Melton, who is usually Matthew Golden’s direct backup at the X position, splitting some time with Moore and taking over some slot reps. Tight End In: Tucker Kraft, Mark Redman, Jonnu Smith and Josh Whyle Out: None Offensive Line In: Jorgan Morgan (LT), Donovan Jennings (LG), Sean Rhyan (C), Jacob Monk (RG), Anthony Belton (RT), Jager Burton (G/C), John Williams (T/G/C) and Travis Glover (T/G) Out: Zach Bako-Bewele (injury) and Aaron Banks (injury) This will likely be Travis Glover’s first active game of the 2026 season. John Williams was active in Week 1, when Aaron Banks was ruled out, but was a healthy scratch in Week 2 (along with Glover), as Banks was able to suit up for the game before eventually going down with a toe injury. Defensive Line In: Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Jonathan Ford and Chris McClellan Out: Warren Brinson (injury) One of three will play: Javon Hargrave (injury), Anthony Campbell (injury) or Eric Johnson II (practice squad) The only real decision this week is who the 48th man will be, and that player will almost certainly come down to a defensive lineman, as there are only four certain “goes” on the 53-man roster — leaving the Packers with just one sub at the position when they play base defense. Edge Defender In: Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Brenton Cox Jr. and Dani Dennis-Sutton Out: None Off-Ball Linebacker In: Zaire Franklin, Edgerrin Cooper, Isaiah McDuffie, Ty’Ron Hopper and Nick Niemann Out: None Cornerback In: Keisean Nixon, Brandon Cisse, Carrington Valentine, Benjamin St-Juste and Kamal Hadden Out: None Safety In: Xavier McKinney, Evan Williams, Javon Bullard and Kitan Oladapo Out: None Specialists In: K Trey Smack, P Daniel Whelan and LS Matt Orzech Out: None — Maybe the only benefit to the Packers’ injuries this year is that it’s made it easy to predict their Week 3 48-man game-day roster. It just comes down to who the fifth defensive lineman will be.

full_text: (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Green Bay Packers have officially ruled out five players for action on Thursday: receiver Jayden Reed (neck), right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele (knee), left guard Aaron Banks (knee/toe) and defensive lineman Warren Brinson (calf). Reed and Bako-Bewele suffered major injuries, but have yet to be placed on the injured reserve, while Brinson has yet to play in a game since injuring himself in warmups before the team’s Week 2 preseason game. The big surprise here is that Banks has already been ruled out, as head coach Matt LaFleur said just yesterday that he would give the offensive lineman until 90 minutes before kickoff to make a ruling on his status. Questionable players going into the game are defensive linemen Anthony Campbell (ankle) and Javon Hargrave (knee/concussion). Both were limited participants for the Packers’ two walkthrough practices this week. Green Bay desperately needs to have five bodies at the position, as they run a 3-4 defense, but with three injuries on the line, they could be down to just Devonte Wyatt, Karl Brooks, Jonathan Ford and rookie Chris McClellan against Atlanta. Their practice squad call-up option is Eric Johnson II, who was signed just a week ago . The good news on the injury report was that the following players were cleared to play on Thursday: receiver Bo Melton (neck), Anthony Belton (elbow), Donovan Jennings (hand), linebacker Edgerrin Cooper (shoulder), cornerback Brandon Cisse (teeth) and cornerback Benjamin St-Juste (hamstring). Belton and Jennings will most likely replace Bako-Bewele and Banks at right tackle and left guard, respectively. Meanwhile, the Falcons are relatively healthy, as only edge defender Samson Ebukam (hamstring) has been ruled out for tomorrow. Billy Bowman, the team’s slot defender who was a full participant in practices all week, was listed as questionable. Aaron Banks is OUT for tomorrow’s game. title: Packers Film Room: Week 2 blitz of the week
summary: The Green Bay Packers defense is showcasing a variety of unconventional blitz packages, and in Week 2, Jonathan Gannon called a specific blitz package at least five times, one for an incompletion and a few that the Jets were able to gain minimal yards on. But in large part, these blitz packages helped keep the […]
full_text: (Photo by Rich Graessle/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Green Bay Packers defense is showcasing a variety of unconventional blitz packages, and in Week 2, Jonathan Gannon called a specific blitz package at least five times, one for an incompletion and a few that the Jets were able to gain minimal yards on. But in large part, these blitz packages helped keep the Jets offense mostly stale and allowed the offense to eventually seize the lead late and win. The Overload Blitz Concept The blitz called is commonly known as an overload blitz. It is a pressure scheme built around creating a numbers advantage on one side of the pass protection. Rather than rushing evenly across the formation, the defense sends four rushers to the same side, overloading it against whatever blockers are responsible for that side — typically the tackle, guard, and running back in man protection, or a zone-slide combination. Because so many rushers commit to one side, the defense will often drop the rusher who would normally attack the opposite edge into coverage instead, playing zone behind the pressure rather than sending four true edge threats. A common variation has an interior lineman, such as a nose tackle, take over as the contain rusher on the backside — replacing what would normally be a traditional edge rush with a slower-developing but still disciplined rush lane. Here, the blitz sends five rushers by bringing four from the weak side against the pass protection and one that slants away from the call. There’s two rushers through the A-gap to break the running back in protection. Zaire Franklin and Brenton Cox are the low zone droppers off the line of scrimmage with Evan Williams adding to the rush as the safety walking down. The concept works because it attacks protection rules directly. Most pass protections are built to handle a standard four-man rush distributed evenly across the line, so overloading one side breaks those assignments, puts the running back in conflict, and forces hurried, often incorrect decisions from blockers and forces errant throws from the quarterback. It also forces the offensive line and running back into a protection slide, shifting blockers toward the overloaded side, which can leave the opposite side thin or create confusion over who picks up the extra rusher. Defenses can disguise which side will actually be overloaded until very late, showing pressure to one side before the snap and then bringing the extra rusher from the other side entirely. Week 2 overload pressure cut-up This approach is especially effective on passing downs, since it pairs well with tight man or zone coverage behind it — the defense can sell out on stopping the pass, bait certain throwing lanes by showing favorable-looking coverage, and then rally to the football once the quarterback is forced into a rushed decision. Because the exact rush lane and coverage rotation can vary from snap to snap, even well-prepared offensive lines have trouble consistently identifying where the free rusher will come from. At its core, the concept is about manufacturing a 4-over-3 numbers mismatch, either to the man-protection side or the zone-protection side, using scheme, disguise, and coaching rather than raw talent alone to generate free rushers.

title: Tramon Williams’ pick-6 among great Packers performances against Falcons
summary: The Packers and Falcons will meet for the 37th time in the regular season tomorrow night. While not exactly a storied rivalry, these two teams have certainly had a few interesting matchups, and they’ve produced a few great performances for the Packers as well. Here are the highlights, including one game from all the way […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GA - JANUARY 15: Tramon Williams ##8 of the Green Bay Packers returns an interception 70-yards for a touchdown in the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons during their 2011 NFC divisional playoff game at Georgia Dome on January 15, 2011 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers and Falcons will meet for the 37th time in the regular season tomorrow night. While not exactly a storied rivalry, these two teams have certainly had a few interesting matchups, and they’ve produced a few great performances for the Packers as well. Here are the highlights, including one game from all the way back in 1970. Passing yards – 396 ( Aaron Rodgers, 2011 ) En route to his first MVP, Aaron Rodgers sliced and diced the Atlanta Falcons’ secondary in 2011, following up his one-man destruction of the Georgia Dome in the playoffs the previous year. His 396 yards included 140 just to James Jones, who went 70 yards for a touchdown in the third quarter to give the Packers’ the lead for the first time in what would become a 25-14 win. Rushing yards – 155 ( Ahman Green, 2002 ) In some grim foreshadowing, the Packers had trouble with Michael Vick at Lambeau Field to open up the 2002 season . The Falcons, however, had even more trouble with Ahman Green, who carried 27 times for 155 yards to help the Packers to a 37-34 overtime victory. Green also added 42 yards on six catches. Samkon Gado gets an honorable mention here, too. He rushed for 103 yards and two touchdowns in Atlanta in 2005 , but we’ll have more from him later on. A second honorable mention goes to Donny Anderson, the only player in Packers history to surpass the 100-yard mark against the Falcons twice: once in 1968 and once in 1969 . Receiving yards – 186 ( Carroll Dale, 1970 ) I’d have guessed the top yardage game would have come from either James Jones in the aforementioned 2011 game or from Jordy Nelson circa 2014, but Carroll Dale had both of them beat before Jones or Nelson was even born. In 1970, Dale caught four passes for 186 yards and two touchdowns, including an 89-yard strike from Don Horn that put the Packers ahead for good. Horn’s pass traveled an impressive 56 yards in the air, which would have been the longest completion by air yards in the NFL in 2025. Points – 18 (Two tied) I told you we’d mention Samkon Gado again. Well, here we are. Dr. Gado is one of two Packers to score three touchdowns in a game against the Falcons, doing so in the aforementioned 2005 game. In that game, he rushed for two touchdowns and added a third through the air to cap off a four catch, five yard, one touchdown receiving performance. The other Packers player to hit a touchdown triumvirate against the Falcons is Robert Tonyan. Big Bob put three across against the Falcons in 2020 as a part of a dominant Packers win . Sacks – 4 ( Tim Harris, 1989 ) Squaring off against the Falcons at Milwaukee County Stadium, the Packers got a serious boost from Tim Harris via his four sacks. One came on the Falcons’ final drive , which helped preserve the Packers’ 23-21 victory. Also noteworthy, Za’Darius Smith recorded three sacks against the Falcons in the Packers’ 2020 win at Lambeau Field. Now a member of the Falcons, you have to think Smith has a pretty good shot at hitting that number again, especially if he’s working against Anthony Belton. Tackles – 11 ( Blake Martinez, 2018 ) A week after firing Mike McCarthy, the Packers got their first of two wins in the short-lived Joe Philbin era with a 34-20 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Blake Martinez led the defensive effort, recording 11 solo tackles as the Packers shut down the Falcons. Interceptions – 2 (Three players tied) Counting playoff games, three different players have recorded two interceptions in a game against the Falcons. Herb Adderley did it first, picking off the Falcons twice in 1968 . Mark Murphy (no, not that one) did it next, also grabbing two interceptions during a 1988 shutout loss in Atlanta. And finally, Tramon Williams did it best. His leaping interception late in the second quarter of the Packers’ 2010 Divisional Round victory over the Falcons set up what would become the go-ahead drive for the Packers. The Packers scored so quickly that they left time on the clock for the Falcons to try to rally. They tried…and they got burned .
author: Jon Meerdink

title: Week 3 matchup with Packers is a homecoming of sorts for Falcons’ Za’Darius Smith
summary: The 2019 offseason was a busy one for Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In his second offseason at the helm of the franchise’s personnel department, Gutekunst headed into the start of free agency with a plan: spend money to bolster a few position groups in desperate need of help, most significantly the edge […]
full_text: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - SEPTEMBER 20: Za'darius Smith #55 of the Atlanta Falcons waves to fans during an NFL football game against the Carolina Panthers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Kara Durrette/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2019 offseason was a busy one for Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst. In his second offseason at the helm of the franchise’s personnel department, Gutekunst headed into the start of free agency with a plan: spend money to bolster a few position groups in desperate need of help, most significantly the edge defenders. Gutekunst did just that, first agreeing to a 4-year deal with former Washington Commander Preston Smith before landing one of the biggest fish in the pond: Za’Darius Smith, who had spent his first four NFL seasons with the Baltimore Ravens. The Smith Brothers proved to be a formidable tandem for the next two seasons. Za’Darius recorded back-to-back Pro Bowl campaigns in 2019 and 2020, as he posted 13.5 and 12.5 sacks in the two seasons, respectively. Preston also had a double-digit sack season in the players’ first year in Green Bay with 12, though he tapered back a bit with just four in 2020. The 2021 season brought an abrupt end to the experiment, however. A back injury and controversy about not being voted a team captain led to Za’Darius playing in just one game, the season opener, before being shut down on injured reserve. Green Bay released him in the offseason before the last year of his 4-year contract, and he signed with the Minnesota Vikings, where he posted another ten-sack Pro Bowl season. Since then, Smith has bounced around to various teams, spending time with the Browns, Lions, and Eagles before landing in Atlanta this offseason. With a limited workload through two games with the Falcons, Smith has flashed some of the power rushing ability that made him a Pro Bowler in Green Bay and elsewhere earlier in his career. He has 2.5 sacks in just 44 defensive snaps so far this season, making him the only player on the Falcons’ roster with more than a half-sack so far this season despite being third among the team’s defensive ends in snaps. Two of those sacks came against his old teammate Aaron Rodgers in Week 1; meanwhile, Pro Football Reference has him down for a total of six QB pressures, certainly a solid rate to start the season. Thursday night’s game will be Smith’s fourth time matching up with the Packers since his split with the team after the 2021 season, though only one of the previous three games took place at Lambeau Field. That came right away in 2022 with the Vikings, though Smith had little impact with just three tackles in a 41-17 Packers victory late in the season. Smith’s other two games also both came as a divisional opponent — the Vikings defeated the Packers in Minnesota in week 1 of that 2022 season, and Smith was a member of the Detroit Lions in 2024 when they beat Green Bay 34-31 at Ford Field on Thursday Night Football. Both of those two games saw Smith record a sack. With starting end Samson Ebukam limited on the Falcons’ injury report this week, Smith might well be in line for a heavier workload. His snap count increased from 16 against the Steelers in Week 1 to 28 last Sunday against the Panthers. If Ebukam is significantly limited or inactive on Thursday, Smith will almost certainly be on the field for more than 30 snaps, and the Packers will need to find a way to cobble together a pass rush plan to minimize his impact on the game. Looking in the other direction, Smith’s one game against the Falcons while playing in a Packers uniform was a star performance. In week 4 of the 2020 season, Smith recorded three sacks, five QB hits, and 8 total tackles in a 30-16 Packers victory at Lambeau Field. (Credit to our Jon Meerdink for pointing this out.) That game also featured three touchdown receptions from Robert Tonyan, who led the Packers in receiving with Davante Adams and Allen Lazard both out due to injury. Smith also recorded one sack in his only other career game against the Falcons, which came in 2018 as a member of the Ravens.

full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NJ - SEPTEMBER 20: Lukas van Ness #90 of the Green Bay Packers defends during the second quarter of the game against the New York Jets on September 20, 2026 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey. I don’t expect the Falcons’ pitiable offense will be the combo breaker here. The Packers will have a chance to do even more cool things on defense this week. title: Houston Texans NFL Power Rankings: Week 3
summary: Two weeks into the season, and the Houston Texans are already entering a death spiral on nearly everyone’s power rankings. It’s been a surprisingly difficult onset to the season for Houston, who now has to metaphorically look in the mirror and ask: How much change will be enough to stop this? How many cracks at […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Quarterback C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans readies to pass the ball during the NFL football game between the Houston Texans and Cincinnati Bengals on September 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Two weeks into the season, and the Houston Texans are already entering a death spiral on nearly everyone’s power rankings. It’s been a surprisingly difficult onset to the season for Houston, who now has to metaphorically look in the mirror and ask: How much change will be enough to stop this? How many cracks at solving the offensive line does the Texans front office and coaching staff need until it is clearly better than before? Last week, with last year’s trade acquisition RG Ed Ingram sidelined due to a groin injury (which may cause him to miss next week’s game), Houston showcased this year’s collection of first-year Texans at the interior o-line: Rookie LG Keylan Rutledge, C Evan Brown, and RG Wyatt Teller. The result of another new offensive line combination was another front-row seat to Texans QB CJ Stroud getting pressured nearly every snap, rolling to his left or right constantly, frantically scanning the field as he looked for somewhere to go with this goofy football that has ordained him with a lifetime of torment. When will this be over? When will all of these changes be enough to grant Houston a reprieve at the offensive line position? As we keep pining for the line to turn the corner, and as the world keeps waiting for Houston to finally look the part of a Super Bowl contender, they continue to drop down the rankings as pundits lose their patience. Once a top ten team on virtually everyone’s boards, Houston has destroyed all of that goodwill in just two weeks, and are now facing the reality of being on the bubble of the playoff teams until they have undeniably improved, like last season. In fact, many power rankings author’s thoughts on the Texans down below are eerily similar to their criticisms in September of last year, and we all know how the Texans improved down the stretch during that season. Is it possible that we’re in store for another midseason surge? Considering how many players are currently on Houston’s Injury report that are expected to return sometime this season, I’d say a midseason win streak is very possible, IF they can halt this rash of injuries that has only grown in intensity since August. Unlike last year, I believe Houston has experienced starters at every position group that can be relied on, so as long as they stay healthy, their floor should be much higher than 2025. Most dropbacks under pressure this season C.J. Stroud 41 Jordan Love 34 Bryce Young 34 Tyler Shough 34 Caleb Williams 33 pic.twitter.com/LjfpoAgCEm — PFF (@PFF) September 21, 2026 But that’s just what I think, and I’m often blinded by optimism in these dark moments of the season (worked out for me last year). So, let’s come back down to reality and check out where the Houston Texans are ranked entering Week 3 of the 2026 NFL Season: NFL.COM : 11. Houston Texans (0-2) (Last Week: 12) I know the history and likelihood of a team starting 0-2 and reaching the playoffs. For those needing a reminder, just 12.8% of clubs beginning a campaign with that record have made the postseason since 1990. I also think the Texans may have landed the worst draw of any NFL team in the first two weeks. Houston competed with both Buffalo and Cincinnati , and C.J. Stroud looks more like the quarterback we’ve hoped to see. That said, you can’t score six points and expect to win. – Nick Shook ESPN: 15. Houston Texans (0-2) Week 2 result: Lost to the Bengals 20-6 Week 2 ranking: 11 One thing we know about the QB1: C.J. Stroud just needs a healthy supporting cast. Stroud has thrown for 627 passing yards in the first two games, third most in the NFL, but that has led to only two touchdowns. The Texans didn’t find the end zone at all in Week 2, as No. 1 option Nico Collins missed the game because of a hamstring injury . Stroud’s play style isn’t necessarily one that can consistently create explosive results when plays break down. He needs the players around him to be healthy so he can produce in structure – DJ Bien-Aime SPORTS ILLUSTRATED: 13. Houston Texans (0–2) Last week’s ranking: No. 8 Last week’s result: lost to Bengals, 20–6 This week: at Colts The Texans remind me a little of the Chargers. It looks bad right now, but it’s not irreparably broken. Houston is struggling to find the sweet spot in an offense where the tackles are vulnerable in pass protection and not as effective as they need to be in the run game. This is going to take a masterclass from Nick Caley in dressing up his offense while, at the same time, making it easier to grasp for those running it. – Conor Orr BLEACHER REPORT: 16. Houston Texans (0-2) Last Week: 11 Week 2 Results: Lost vs. Cincinnati 20-6 It’s still too early for the Houston Texans to panic. However, an 0-2 start is obviously not ideal, and there are some legitimate reasons for concern. Houston’s defense hasn’t looked much like the league-best unit we saw in 2025. Wide receiver depth is still a serious issue, and C.J. Stroud continues to look more like an average starter than a true franchise quarterback. However, it may be wise to give the Texans a few more weeks before writing them off as AFC contenders. The Buffalo Bills have looked like the best team in the conference through two weeks, and Houston was a dropped interception away from beating them in Week 1. Star wideout Nico Collins missed Week 2 with a hamstring injury, and his absence changed the complexion of the offense dramatically. With three divisional matchups in their next four games, the Texans can quickly climb back into the AFC South race. – Kris Knox CBS SPORTS: 24. Texans (0-2) (Last Week: 12) At 0-2, they are off to a tough start. And both losses are at home. They face an almost must-win at Indianapolis this week. – Pete Prisco USA TODAY: 18. Houston Texans (11): What, we worry? They’ve now dropped their first two games in three of QB C.J. Stroud’s four seasons … and recovered to reach postseason in the first two instances. – Nate Davis YAHOO! SPORTS: 19. Houston Texans (0-2, LW: 13) The Texans ‘ run game was dreadful Sunday when it had to carry the offense with receiver Nico Collins out. The Texans had a putrid 6.7% success rate on runs against the Bengals. Only one team has a mark under 20% in a game this season, and that was the Raiders at 18.5% in Week 2. It’s stunning that the Texans have not fixed their offensive line issues over multiple offseasons despite it being an obvious liability. “For us just collectively as a team, the one key to this victory was controlling the front and from an offensive perspective and we did not control their front,” Houston head coach DeMeco Ryans said, via Texans Wire. “We got outplayed up front. We couldn’t run the ball well. That forced us into a lot of passing situations.” The Texans bounced back from an 0-3 start to make the playoffs last season, but they’re in a big hole after losing two home games to begin this season. – Frank Schwab THE ATHLETIC: 17. Houston Texans (0-2) Last week : 9 Sunday : Lost to Bengals 20-6 Rookie spotlight : Keylan Rutledge The Texans took Rutledge in the first round in their seemingly constant attempt to fix the offensive line. It went OK in Week 1, but Rutledge and the rest of the Texans struggled against Dexter Lawrence on Sunday. Overall, things aren’t great in Houston, where C.J. Stroud is being pressured on 40.2 percent of his dropbacks, which ranks 24th in the league. Up next : at Colts, Sunday, 1 p.m. ET – Chad Graff & Josh Kendall PRO FOOTBALL TALK: 10. Texans (No. 4; 0-2): The offense is letting down the defense. – Mike Florio Average Ranking: 15.89 (Last Week: 10.11) Yeah…woof. Don’t let these rankings discourage you too much, though, because if last year taught us…

title: Are the Colts already in a must-win situation?
summary: After failing to get off on the right foot, the Indianapolis Colts find themselves in territory that is more familiar than it should be. With over a decade of losing Week 1 contests, they know what it’s like to be behind the eight ball. 2026 is no different as the Colts find themselves in an […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - NOVEMBER 30: Josh Downs #2 of the Indianapolis Colts runs with the ball while being chased by Calen Bullock #2 of the Houston Texans in the third quarter at Lucas Oil Stadium on November 30, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Dylan Buell/Getty Images) | Getty Images After failing to get off on the right foot, the Indianapolis Colts find themselves in territory that is more familiar than it should be. With over a decade of losing Week 1 contests, they know what it’s like to be behind the eight ball. 2026 is no different as the Colts find themselves in an 0-2 hole. It’s only Week 3, but is it already a must-win scenario? Technically, the answer is no. Teams that start 0-3 have about a 2.5% chance at a postseason berth. So, yes, I’m saying they’d still have a chance. I wouldn’t place large sums of money on that chance, however. The Colts have a good opportunity to dig their way out. They get the reeling Texans at home. As another 0-2 team, the Colts won’t find themselves facing the cream of the crop and have a chance to decimate the Texans’ chance at the postseason in the process. Looking forward, Jayden Daniels’ status for the game in London is up in the air. That could make that game much more manageable. With a road contest against Pittsburgh, the Colts could leave the murderer’s row that is the first five weeks at 2-3. Not perfect, but they will take it. That only happens if they win on Sunday. If this season is destined to be anything more than a dumpster fire, they have to find a way. This may be the best and last shot to truly get things on track. One benefit working in the Colts’ favor is that the rest of the division might be just as bad. They have to capitalize on the Texans’ misfortune and bury them now with the understanding they can turn it on quickly. Sunday could be a two for one. Then again, it could be the beginning of the end.

title: Colts’ Week 2 QB Analysis: Much Better
summary: Thanks to the nflFastR project, Pro Football Focus for the timely sources of data. For those of you new to this, I will publish key QB stats each week judging how well the Colts’ QB performed. Yes, O-Line, receivers, and play-calling impact these numbers but they are primarily QB measures. I will probably modify the charts throughout the season. […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MISSOURI - SEPTEMBER 20: Daniel Jones #17 of the Indianapolis Colts looks on prior to an NFL football game against the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Kansas City, Missouri. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Thanks to the nflFastR project, Pro Football Focus for the timely sources of data. For those of you new to this, I will publish key QB stats each week judging how well the Colts’ QB performed. Yes, O-Line, receivers, and play-calling impact these numbers but they are primarily QB measures. I will probably modify the charts throughout the season. Commentary will be brief but feel free to let me know in the comments that stats aren’t everything. (click charts for larger view) It’s always tough to analyze a loss, but Daniel Jones had a much better performance against the Chiefs than he did in the season opener. I feel much better about the outlook for the season than I did a week ago. Let’s break it down by the numbers. HOW WELL? mouseover definitions: median EPA gain in similar game situation (down, distance, etc.)”> arsr , 3 yards to gain in game-neutral situations”> edp , sg% , oz% , pr% , tip , ttt , adot , ay/c , yac , yacoe , yd/c , ac% , cpoe , aypa , drp , scr% , ta% , sck% , aa% , ny/d , ny/p , 1st% , td% , to% , 0″> qbsr epa/p , adj/p The Colts supported Jones with a strong running game and leaned toward the run on early downs (5th ARSR; 25th EDP) . Jones wasn’t pressured much and got the ball out at a fairly normal pace suggesting the O-Line did their job. ( 28th PR%; 16th TIP & TTT) The passing game was relatively conservative in depth, with Jones doing most of his work in the shorter and intermediate areas rather than pushing the ball downfield. ( 24th ADOT; 18th AY/C) . The receivers provided fairly ordinary production after the catch and actually came in a little below what was expected from their opportunities. ( 18th YAC; 19th YACOE & YD/C) Jones 75% adjusted completion rate helped his efficiency greatly, although relative to shorter passing depth that was expected ( 13th AC%; 21st CPOE) Very little of the passing game was lost to abandoned plays. There were no drops, Jones took no sacks, had only a couple of scrambles and rarely had to throw the ball away. ( 28th DRP%; 13th SCR%; 22nd TA%; 30th SCK%; 30th AA%) That ability to preserve his dropbacks helped turn fairly ordinary YPA into one of the better overall yardage performances of the week when counting all dropbacks. ( 18th AYPA: 10th NY/D; 9th NY/P) Jones consistently kept the offense moving, generating first downs at one of the better rates in the league. ( 8th 1st%) However, despite first down success, the scoring production from the pass game was modest, and the interception was the primary blemish on an otherwise efficient game. ( 21st TD%; 13th TO%) Overall, Jones combined good play-to-play consistency with strong total value, finishing comfortably in the upper half of QBs in success rate and total efficiency. ( 11th QBSR; 12th EPA/P) mouseover definitions: ay< , dp% , ay/c , yac , yd/c , ac% , aypa , drp% , aypa , ta% , ypa , sck% , ny/a , scr% , ny/d , car% , ny/p , 1st% , any/p , td% , any/p , to% , any/p , epa/p , opd , adj/p adj/p Jones’ efficiency was built less through explosive downfield passing than through consistant positive play. His modest completed air yards and YAC left his YPA near the middle of the pack ( 19th YD/C ), but a 75% adjusted completion rate and the absence of sacks produced a large jump in efficiency ( 7th NY/A ). A below average TD rate and the interception dragged him down but he still finished 12th EPA/P overall for the week . The play by play view shows why Jones’ final efficiency remained strong despite one enormous negative. His first-quarter interception cost -4.69 EPA , easily his worst play of the game, but there were enough consistant productive plays throughout the rest of the game including his most valuable play, the 48-yard overtime fumble completion to Laquon Treadwell. Overall, this was a game with one damaging mistake surrounded by a lot of positive production. This shows the strong rebound after a poor Week 1. Jones’ QBSR and first-down rate both jumped sharply , showing a major improvement in play-to-play consistency, while EPA per play and net yards per play made similarly large gains , showing that the successful plays also generated substantial value. HOW FAR? The 2 deep pass interference calls certainly helped, but he repeatedly picked up first downs with short and intermediate completions. The 48-yard completion to Treadwell was by far the deepest attempt. Jones continued to play a relatively conservative passing game in Week 2, with most of his production coming on shorter throws rather than consistently attacking downfield. That approach was considerably less aggressive than much of his passing profile last season, but he was effective within it — unlike week 1. For the 2 games combined. You can see that the Colts are passing short relative to the league. TO WHO? Downs led the way in targets, receptions and total yards. Same story for the 2 games combined (Okay, Downs is tied with Warren for most receptions). At least Pierce and Downs are in the good quadrant. The bulk of the targets added higher than average value. Keenan Allen was the clear negative outlier, driven heavily by the interception thrown in his direction. That is a big spread. Warren’s targets are not as valuable as I was hoping this year, but its good to see the main receivers above league average value. HOW ACCURATE? Jones completion rate was high but realtive to his short depth of target it was just about average. HOW FAST? Jones has generally gotten the ball out quickly through the first two weeks, which fits with the relatively short passing game Indianapolis has been using. His Week 2 timing was close to what would be expected for the depth of his throws, so he is neither holding the ball long nor relying on especially quick-releases. TO WHERE? Jones did most of his damage over the middle in Week 2, particularly on intermediate and deeper throws. The left side was much less productive and included his interception. Adding in week 1 makes the season totals look pretty meh, which makes sense: poor week 1 + good week 2 = OK season so far.

title: Should Colts bring ‘maybe now available’ Cardinals WR Marvin Harrison Jr. ‘home’?
summary: According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, NFL execs are now wondering whether unexpectedly struggling Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. could be available ahead of the league’s November 10th trade deadline—which begs the question of whether the increasingly wide receiver needy Indianapolis Colts could be interested? Once considered a “can’t miss” generational wideout prospect as the […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - OCTOBER 12: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals runs the ball after a catch against the Indianapolis Colts during the NFL 2025 game between Arizona Cardinals and Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images According to ESPN’s Dan Graziano, NFL execs are now wondering whether unexpectedly struggling Arizona Cardinals wideout Marvin Harrison Jr. could be available ahead of the league’s November 10th trade deadline—which begs the question of whether the increasingly wide receiver needy Indianapolis Colts could be interested? Execs around the league are wondering whether the Arizona Cardinals could explore trading WR Marvin Harrison Jr. ahead of the NFL trade deadline, per @DanGrazianoESPN . Harrison Jr. was the No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft, but has only caught one pass this season. pic.twitter.com/0K1H1seZd4 — Yahoo Sports (@YahooSports) September 23, 2026 Once considered a “can’t miss” generational wideout prospect as the former 4th overall pick of the 2024 NFL Draft, the 24-year-old is off to yet another underwhelming season production-wise in the desert, after becoming increasingly an afterthought in new Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur’s new offense . We know that ahead of the 2024 NFL Draft, the Colts, like many other NFL teams, clearly coveted Harrison Jr., who of course, is the son of Colts legendary wideout, Super Bowl Champion, and Pro Football Hall of Famer Marvin Harrison Sr.—who’s the best wide receiver in their franchise’s all-time history and holds nearly every major all-time receiving record for Indianapolis. With the 15th overall pick ahead of the 2024 NFL Draft, Colts general manager Chris Ballard publicly called Harrison Jr. “a very talented prospect,” but it also being “fantasy-land,” that Indianapolis would surrender the king’s ransom draft capital required to trade up all the way from #15 to within the Top 4 picks , where the former Ohio State 2x All-American wideout was ultimately selected. For what it’s worth, there was some league buzz that the Colts did try to realistically trade up within the Top 10 later in that draft class for now Chicago Bears wideout Rome Odunze, who went 9th overall, just a few picks later. Instead, Indianapolis ended up with UCLA edge Laiatu Latu at 15th overall as the first defensive player chosen. Limited to just 1 reception for 33 total receiving yards on 4 targets, and just targeted on 7% of his routes in 2 starts during 2026 for Arizona, it’s a question of whether Harrison Jr.‘s been properly utilized and featured right now by the Cardinals freshly installed LaFleur offense: Marvin Harrison Jr. is a hot topic right now after two disappointing weeks. Let’s take a look at what may be going on. When MHJ came out of OSU, his speed was his key attribute. He also was a tremendous 50/50 ball guy with good body control and hands. He was at his best when… — Jeremy (@Popes_FF) September 22, 2026 I have no positive news to report for Marvin Harrison Jr.'s owners He's in the most Sacrificial X role of all time, and it's quite disgusting and disheartening He currently has the 2nd-highest aDOT (23.0 yards) and Go Route Rate (33.3%) in the league (per @FantasyPtsData )… — Kyle (@KyleM_FF) September 22, 2026 Furthermore, he’s tied for the fewest catchable targets (2) among all league wideouts with 60+ receiving snaps so far this season. Some of that can be attributed to Harrison Jr. just not consistently getting open nearly enough in his newfound role, but some of it also can be chalked up to his limited starting quarterback play. No disrespect to current Cardinals starting quarterback Jacoby Brissett, but we’ve seen firsthand how he can limit his wide receivers’ production out there by being relatively risk adverse and not taking many calculated shots downfield. Their leading wideout isn’t even presumed WR1 Michael Wilson right now, it’s Kendrick Bourne with 10 receptions for 86 total receiving yards through two games in 2026. Even dating back to 2019 when Brissett was a full-time starter for the Colts due to former franchise quarterback Andrew Luck’s abrupt offseason retirement, Pro Bowler T.Y. Hilton went from having 76 receptions, 1,270 receiving yards, and 6 touchdown receptions in 14 starts catching passes from Luck in 2018 to 45 receptions for 501 receiving yards and 5 touchdown receptions in 10 starts from Brissett a year later respectively. He was only 30-years-old too in that season when paired with Brissett, so it’s not like he was simply too long in the tooth. Even with the Colts signing former New York Giants veteran wideout Darius Slayton earlier this week as an interim replacement for Pierce, the Colts could still use an upgrade with lead wideout Alec Pierce presumably out of action, with a reoccurring heel/ankle injury, to at least around misdseason. That’s around at least six weeks, if not more, depending on how Pierce reinjured ankle recovers and heals without planned surgery. Why not take advantage of a potential ‘buy low’ opportunity on a still very talented young player, who’s a legacy with the franchise, and may just need a change of scenery to better find his footing? His upside is still immense. Maybe not a first round pick anymore! But for a second round pick? Sign me up. Yes, having now been miscast in the Cardinals offense to-date, Harrison Jr. is struggling with a lack of focus and effort to go along with his surprisingly quiet receiving production so far, but to me, that’s just an initial maturity issue and is coachable for a young wideout. Harrison Jr.‘s work ethic at Ohio State was actually lauded among his even more senior teammates, presumably the same one that he mirrored from his Hall of Fame father who kept himself in pristine physical shape and conditioning ( even as a habitual junk food eater ), was a machine at pristine route-running, while playing 13 prolific seasons in the NFL. Recent commentary on the “Speakeasy Talkshow” podcast from former Cincinnati Bengals Pro Bowl wideout T.J. Houshmanzadeh on Harrison Jr were pretty telling. Houshmanzadeh believes Arizona’s struggling young wideout, who he personally knows off-the-field, is “checked out” from having not been properly deployed and utilized within the Cardinals offense, but still needs to play through it and “just ball out”: . @Housh84 gives some real advice to Marvin Harrison Jr. Listen to this! 💯 pic.twitter.com/vXDzwE6LQu — Speakeasy (@speakeasytlkshw) September 22, 2026 There may not be a better possible assistant coaching mentor in the NFL than Colts Ring of Honor wideout and future Hall of Famer Reggie Wayne, who currently serves as the Colts wide receivers coach, and was the other half of the “1-2” receiving punch that was paired with Harrison Sr. on those juggernaut Indianapolis offenses, when they won a Super Bowl back in 2006 together, catching passes from franchise GOAT Peyton Manning. Wayne has credited playing alongside Harrison Sr. for his early career development and growth by just copying Harrison Sr.’s off-the-field work ethic and football maturity. Perhaps, Wayne, who’s already been instrumental in helping to develop last year’s breakout wideout Alec Pierce, can pass along some of that football knowledge and “tough love” to the “chip off the old block of his pops,” Harrison Jr.. Why not take the chance?

title: Per Steichen, Colts set to make roster maneuver regarding injured WR Alec Pierce
summary: According to their head coach Shane Steichen on Wednesday, the Indianapolis Colts will place injured wideout Alec Pierce on injured reserve shortly, meaning he’ll miss at least the team’s next four games: Given that earlier reports suggested that the Colts were hopeful for a “midseason return,” his eventual activation off of injured reserve could be […]
full_text: KANSAS CITY, MO - SEPTEMBER 20: Alec Pierce #14 of the Indianapolis Colts runs onto the field before an NFL game between the Indianapolis Colts and Kansas City Chiefs on Sep 20, 2026 at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, MO. (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to their head coach Shane Steichen on Wednesday, the Indianapolis Colts will place injured wideout Alec Pierce on injured reserve shortly, meaning he’ll miss at least the team’s next four games: Colts HC Shane Steichen told reporters that WR Alec Pierce is being placed on injured reserve due to his heel injury. Pierce now will miss a minimum of four games. pic.twitter.com/uQ22NgnE0n — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) September 23, 2026 Given that earlier reports suggested that the Colts were hopeful for a “midseason return,” his eventual activation off of injured reserve could be realistically closer to Week 8 or 9, so at least six weeks or so. However, we’ll just have to see how his reoccurring injury heals and responds, having elected to not undergo surgery at this time. Pierce’s loss is certainly immense, but not unexpected, after he was unable to put his body weight on his reinjured left ankle/heel after a non-contact injury, which the lingering injury already cost him all of training camp and the preseason. He subsequently had to be carted off the field with trainers and was later seen walking around the players concourse in crutches and a medical boot post-game. The Colts returning lead wideout from last season had only 5 receptions for 72 total receiving yards through two games, as he worked himself back from a conditioning and training standpoint from the prior ankle/heel injury. Regarding Pierce, given that he only had his first full practice with the Colts five days prior to last Sunday night’s game , and it’s a fair question of whether he should’ve just begun the season on PUP instead and missed the team’s first four games, two of which they’ve lost anyways with him active headed in. Hindsight is 20/20, but it now looks like he’s at greater risk of missing more games, had he just been placed on PUP to start. With the AFC South rival Houston Texans coming to town—and looking to avoid an 0-3 start, the Colts will assuredly miss their elite deep threat and one of their offense’s top receiving playmakers collectively. That being said, Indianapolis did recently sign former New York Giants veteran wideout Darius Slayton, who already has familiarity with starting quarterback Daniel Jones, as an interim downfield threat replacement to help fill Pierce’s void for the next handful or more of missed weeks. Otherwise, on Tuesday, the Colts placed backup defensive end Michael Clemons (toe) on injured reserve, who didn’t record a defensive stat through his first two games with the club. Indianapolis also released running back Anderson Castle from their practice squad and re-signed wideout Eli Pancol to their taxi-man team—presumably as additional Pierce insurance at wideout, should they need it.

title: How does Chris Ballard continue to keep his job?
summary: I don’t know how I continue to write these articles. We’re going on Year 4 of me calling for Chris Ballard’s firing, and somehow he continues to survive. If there is a nuclear war in my lifetime, I would love to live with Chris Ballard because I know I will survive. In 2022, I was […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - SEPTEMBER 13: Indianapolis Colts General Manager Chris Ballard walks the sideline prior to the start of a NFL game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Indianapolis Colts on September 13, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images I don’t know how I continue to write these articles. We’re going on Year 4 of me calling for Chris Ballard’s firing, and somehow he continues to survive. If there is a nuclear war in my lifetime, I would love to live with Chris Ballard because I know I will survive. In 2022, I was saying his team building approach needed to change and in 2024 I was calling for his firing . I finished that 2024 article saying “I have to go with what I see and what I see is an incompetent front office and staff that are guiding this team to nowhere.” Unfortunately two years later, it is the same old crap. At some point, you run out of excuses. You can blame Andrew Luck’s retirement, injuries, coaching, bad luck, bad quarterback play or whatever else people have used over the years, but eventually the person responsible for building the roster has to answer for the results. Ballard is now in Year 10, and the Colts are still having the same conversations they were having five, six and seven years ago. Who is the long-term quarterback? Where is the pass rush coming from? Why is the roster always one injury away from scrambling for help? Why is this team constantly hovering around .500 without ever actually going anywhere? That is what makes this different from another article reacting to one bad loss or one bad season. This is about a decade of the same patterns repeating themselves. Ballard has made some good picks, found some good players and built a few teams that looked promising for stretches, and he deserves credit for those things. The problem is that none of it has translated into sustained success. The Colts are always close, always one move away, always one year away, and somehow still in the same place. After ten years, “close” is not progress anymore; it is the result. The definition of mediocre If there is one word that perfectly describes the Chris Ballard era, it is mediocre. Not terrible. Not historically bad. Not completely dysfunctional. Just mediocre enough to keep convincing people that something better might be around the corner. Before this season, Ballard’s record as Colts general manager was 70-78-1. In nine seasons, Indianapolis made the playoffs twice, won one playoff game and never won the AFC South. Since Philip Rivers retired after the 2020 season, the Colts have not made the playoffs at all. Their best record over that stretch was 9-8, which they accomplished twice. Nine wins has essentially become the ceiling. The zero division titles might be the craziest part of the entire résumé. The AFC South has not exactly been some impossible gauntlet over the last decade. Houston has torn itself down and rebuilt. Jacksonville has gone through multiple coaches, general managers and quarterbacks. Tennessee reached an AFC Championship Game, won the division twice and has already gone through another two resets since then. All three franchises have had seasons with more postseason success than anything the Colts have produced under Ballard, and all three have still been willing to start over when things stopped working. Indianapolis just keeps hovering in the middle. That is almost worse than being terrible. Bad teams eventually get premium draft picks, clear out the building and start again. The Colts have spent most of Ballard’s tenure picking somewhere in the middle because they are usually good enough to win seven, eight or nine games but rarely good enough to accomplish anything meaningful. They never fully bottom out, but they never take the next step either. The one recent season where they actually did bottom out gave them the fourth overall pick in 2023. They used it on Anthony Richardson. That is the trap Ballard has built. His teams are usually competent enough to avoid the top of the draft and flawed enough to stay away from January football. Every offseason begins with some version of the same argument: the Colts are close. A couple additions here, better health there, another year of development and maybe they finally break through. Being close for one or two years is understandable. Being close for most of a decade is just another way of saying you never got there. Andrew Luck masked plenty of issues early in Ballard’s tenure because great quarterbacks do that. The 2018 team won 10 games and a playoff game, and Luck covered up weaknesses because he was one of the best quarterbacks in football. Rivers then gave Indianapolis another legitimate season in 2020, when the Colts went 11-5 and looked like a team that might finally have some stability again. Rivers retired, the quarterback carousel restarted, and the Colts went right back to the middle. This is what Ballard has become exceptionally good at building: average football teams. Teams that are rarely hopeless, occasionally interesting and almost never good enough when the season actually matters. After ten years, there is no “bad luck”. That is the résumé. Too many early-round misses Ballard has built a reputation as a good drafter, and there is some truth to that. He has found quality players throughout the draft and deserves credit for it. Quenton Nelson became one of the best guards in football. Darius Leonard was an All-Pro and Defensive Player of the Year. Jonathan Taylor became one of the league’s best running backs. Michael Pittman Jr. developed into a legitimate starting receiver. Alec Pierce turned into a 1,000-yard player. Tyler Warren looks like another major hit. Braden Smith gave the Colts years of good starting tackle play. The problem is what surrounds those hits. Go through the first and second rounds of Ballard’s drafts and there are far too many picks that either failed completely or never came close to providing the return expected from premium draft capital. It started immediately in 2017 with Malik Hooker in the first round and Quincy Wilson in the second. Hooker had some good moments, but he never became the difference-making safety the Colts expected when they drafted him 15th overall. Wilson was gone after three seasons. A year later, Nelson and Leonard were home runs, but Kemoko Turay never became the pass rusher Indianapolis hoped it was getting in the second round. The 2019 class was worse. Rock Ya-Sin was selected early in the second round, Ben Banogu followed some picks later and neither became a long-term answer. Banogu in particular was a massive miss at a premium position, finishing his Colts career with just 2.5 sacks. The pattern continued. Kwity Paye and Dayo Odeyingbo were the first two picks in 2021. Both became NFL players, but neither became the high-end pass rusher the Colts desperately needed. Paye was useful, but a useful edge defender is not what you are hoping to get with the 21st overall pick when the position has been a problem for years. Both were gone within 5 seasons of their draft year. Then there is 2022, when the Colts did not even have a first-round pick because Ballard had traded it away for Carson Wentz. That pick became No. 16 overall. Wentz lasted one season in Indianapolis. You can call that a trade failure instead of a draft failure if you want, but the result is the same: another premium asset produced almost nothing for the Colts. Jelani Woods was taken in the third round that year and never developed into the player Indianapolis envisioned. In 2023, Ballard finally had another top-five selection and used it on Anthony Richardson. Julius Brents came next in the second round. Richardson is now the backup quarterback, while Brents never established himself as a dependable starter. The one time the Colts were bad enough to draft near the very top, they missed on the most important…

title: Chiefs-Dolphins Week 3 Wednesday injury report: FAU pops up with quad

title: Patrick Mahomes can see defenses respecting the Chiefs’ run game
summary: Through two weeks of the regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs have made a statement to the rest of the NFL: you’ll need to respect our run game this season. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes could see the Indianapolis Colts had already gotten the message after the team’s 220 rushing yards against the Denver Broncos in the […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Through two weeks of the regular season, the Kansas City Chiefs have made a statement to the rest of the NFL: you’ll need to respect our run game this season. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes could see the Indianapolis Colts had already gotten the message after the team’s 220 rushing yards against the Denver Bronco s in the season opener. During his press conference on Wednesday, Mahomes talked through the Colts’ defensive attention on limiting the ground attack and running back Kenneth Walker. “You could even see the differences between Weeks 1 and 2,” Mahomes said at the podium. “The Colts saw how committed we were to the run game and how well it worked. You could tell they were putting assets into stopping the run, so whenever you’re doing the play fakes and linebackers are in the line of scrimmage, it opens up guys over the top of them.” Andy Reid today on Patrick Mahomes' Week 2 performance: "I thought he did a good job of getting the ball out on time." First 3 completions of the game are good examples. Quick, decisive throws; 2 of them set up well with under-center play-action pic.twitter.com/ZXvo0F8Fii — Ron Kopp Jr (@RonOnChiefs) September 21, 2026 Mahomes noticed it early: two of his first three completions of the game came on plays that called for play-action from an under-center formation. Both times, the Chiefs’ quarterback fired to an open target quickly because of the gravity of a potential handoff to Walker. “It’s got to be a great balance that we have to have of being able to run it, run it, run it, then play-action at the right time,” Mahomes explained. “I thought Coach Bieniemy and Coach Reid did a great job of calling the perfect play action, the perfect movement plays at the perfect time, so that I had guys open for me to throw. We’ll continue to get better and better at that and continue to run the football as well.” On Sunday night, 35% of Kansas City’s pass plays were play action. That would have been the third-highest rate among all of the team’s games last year. In the two games in which the Chiefs ran play action more than 35% of the time in 2025, Kansas City won convincingly: against the Detroit Lions , 30-17, and the New York Giants , 22-9. “It just puts the defenses in a predicament,” Mahomes elaborated. “Just knowing they have to kind of choose if they want to come up and stop the run or if they want to try and stop the explosive plays from happening. That’s what you want: you want defenses guessing; you want defenses having to make decisions they don’t want to make.” It all stems from the willingness to simply hand off to Walker, the league’s leading rusher in yards and attempts, through two games. “As an offense, I think we’ve done a great job of that these first few weeks,” Mahomes said. “If they’re going to stay back, run the football; if they’re going to come up, then play action, throw it over the top of them. I think if you can continue to do that and keep defenses guessing, you can continue to have success.” “You want defenses having this tough decision,” Mahomes remarked. “Then you just kind of figure it out on the fly on which one you’re doing that day.” Whether it’s Walker or the pass game producing the explosive plays, they’re happening, and the team will keep tweaking how to balance that attack week to week moving forward.
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: The Chiefs are chasing a significant mark of 3-0 to start this season
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs are one of eight NFL teams to start this season 2-0, one of four AFC teams and joined by only the Las Vegas Raiders in the AFC West as undefeated teams still remaining. Each of the league’s 2-0 teams has a chance to advance their record to 3-0 in Week 3 […]
full_text: Tammy Ljungblad/The Kansas City Star/Tribune News Service via Getty Images) The Kansas City Chiefs are one of eight NFL teams to start this season 2-0, one of four AFC teams and joined by only the Las Vegas Raiders in the AFC West as undefeated teams still remaining. Each of the league’s 2-0 teams has a chance to advance their record to 3-0 in Week 3 with a victory; none of the teams match up with each other. According to FanDuel Sportsbook , the Chiefs are the most likely team; Kansas City is currently a 10.5-point favorite against the Miami Dolphins on the road. Of course it’s important to win every week during the 17-game NFL regular season, but there is a significant impact on playoff probability when starting the year 3-0. RotoWire.com has a 10-year study (since 2016) of NFL teams starting 3-0 ; 73% of teams make the postseason and one in five reach the Super Bowl. The 45-team sample of 3-0 starts also shows that 38% of such teams reach the Divisional Round and 31% play in that year’s conference championship game. There are many hot starts to log in head coach Andy Reid’s history in Kansas City with quarterback Patrick Mahomes. Here are the seasons the team has started 3-0 in this era and how the year finished out. 2024: Super Bowl appearance 2020: Super Bowl appearance 2019: Super Bowl LIV champions 2018: AFC Championship appearance It’s not about how you start, it’s about how you finish — but there’s no reason to doubt this team’s ability to close crucial games when it is do or die. A strong performance in September can make life easier on the way to success in January (and February).

title: The Good and the Bad from the Chiefs’ Week 2 win
summary: The Kansas City Chiefs won an exciting overtime game against the Indianapolis Colts, 33-30. The Chiefs’ pass offense looked crisp, the run game continued to make a difference, and Kansas City got enough stops without cornerback Mansoor Delane to win. After every win, I like to look at two things that went well for the […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs won an exciting overtime game against the Indianapolis Colts , 33-30. The Chiefs’ pass offense looked crisp, the run game continued to make a difference, and Kansas City got enough stops without cornerback Mansoor Delane to win. After every win, I like to look at two things that went well for the Chiefs and one thing that didn’t. Let’s start by talking about the impact of nose tackle Khyiris Tonga: The Good Khyiris Tonga brings a different element to the Chiefs’ defense For years, the Chiefs scraped by at nose tackle with cheap veterans, primarily Derrick Nnadi and Mike Pennel since 2019. Both could eat blocks and occupy space, but neither consistently impacted the run game. This offseason, Kansas City finally upgraded, signing Tonga to a three-year, $21 million contract. After bouncing around early in his career, Tonga broke out with New England by stabilizing its run defense. The early returns have been promising. Khyiris Tonga pt 1 pic.twitter.com/BCkco29Zie — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 Khyiris Tonga pt 2 pic.twitter.com/4F6zvX7o1c — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 Khyiris Tonga pt 3 pic.twitter.com/VyrNw9wbhr — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 Khyiris Tonga pt 4 pic.twitter.com/lZEDdzbzpj — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 The most underrated part of Tonga’s game is his initial burst. He fires off the ball and beats blockers to the spot, especially on zone runs. On the backside, guards have to get around his hips to seal him, which is difficult because Tonga explodes off the ball and chases plays down. He combines that burst with the strength to control blocks and eat space. Tonga even got the better of left guard Quenton Nelson in the first clip, directing him toward the running back and closing the hole. That combination of explosiveness and power gives the Chiefs a disruptive presence against the run. Tonga could be especially important when Kansas City faces the Bills. The Chiefs incorporating play action into their passing game I’ve written about this before, but I’ve believed the Chiefs needed to run more play action with the skill-position personnel they have. Kansas City’s weapons struggle to get off press coverage and create their own separation. Running play action can help mitigate this, as you can create natural rubs with the run fake and condense the formation, forcing cornerbacks to play off receivers. The issue is that with the Chiefs’ lack of run game for years, it was hard to get any team to buy the run fake Kansas City would present. Defenders would drop into coverage, so the fake did nothing. Now that the Chiefs have running back Kenneth Walker, teams have to respect the run threat much more, which has opened up Kansas City’s play-action passing concepts. Mahomes went 14/17 on play-action passes for 137 yards and two touchdowns against the Colts. Patrick Mahomes completed 32 of 47 passes for 382 yards and 3 touchdowns in the Chiefs' Week 2 win, recording a career-high 14 completions on play-action passes. He totaled 137 yards and 2 touchdowns on 17 play-action attempts. #INDvsKC | #ChiefsKingdom pic.twitter.com/DiYyyXrqV3 — Next Gen Stats (@NextGenStats) September 21, 2026 Mahomes play action to Worthy pic.twitter.com/0TEXEs7Byq — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 23, 2026 One of the first plays of the game showed the impact of the Chiefs’ improved run game on play action. The Colts are in Cover 2, but the WILL linebacker bites on the play fake and gets completely out of position. With the field corner occupied by Kelce in the flat, the MIKE linebacker must choose between tight end Noah Gray’s sail route and receiver Xavier Worthy’s backside dig. He covers Gray, leaving Worthy wide open. Mahomes play action pt 2 pic.twitter.com/q4TGrCbZoz — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 23, 2026 This is a good example of how condensed formations can help wide receivers get free releases. Wideout Rashee Rice motions inside to an F position off the line of scrimmage. This makes it look like he’s going to run block. When it’s a pass, Rice gets a free release. The Colts are playing Cover 1, but the motion gives Rice a leverage advantage on cornerback Sauce Gardner, who has no chance at recovering to Rice on the over route. Mahomes PA flat to Walker pt 1 pic.twitter.com/9GO3rj6lS0 — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 23, 2026 Mahomes to Walker PA flat pt 2 pic.twitter.com/pX2fUahqQI — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 23, 2026 The Chiefs ran this exact formation and play twice, including on a critical third down in overtime. Worthy motions across the formation, then Kansas City runs a quick boot to the flat for Walker. The first time, Indianapolis linebackers bump with the motion, giving Walker easy leverage. The second time, Gardner travels with Worthy, vacating the flat. It’s a quick-hitting concept that attacks linebackers who can’t match Walker in space. The pass offense can’t build entirely around play action, but using it more will make the offense smoother. It creates cleaner receiver releases, slows linebackers against the run, reduces the burden on the offensive line, and simplifies Mahomes’ reads by giving him one or two primary options plus a checkdown. Overall, it’s something the coaching staff should keep refining; it gives them a new and important lever to pull in big games. The Bad The Chiefs setting the edge against pin-pull runs The Chiefs defense wasn’t as dominant as Week 1, but the Colts deserve credit. They ran effectively, added bodies in protection, and consistently used hot routes to neutralize the blitz. Cornerback L’Jarius Sneed struggled in space against slot receiver Josh Downs, but cornerback Nohl Williams and safety Jaden Hicks played well. Without Delane, the Chiefs will be more vulnerable in coverage, but they did enough to win. My biggest concern was edge-setting. On both Jonathan Taylor touchdowns, Indianapolis used pin-pull concepts to create a wide edge, and the Chiefs struggled to set it. Jonathan Taylor pin-pull TD part 1 pic.twitter.com/WkUHUVd0xJ — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 Downs motions across the play, and Sneed travels with him, eliminating him from the run fit. The center and right tackle pull around the edge, with the tackle easily widening Tranquill. The center doesn’t have to block anyone because Hicks takes a poor angle and gets caught inside. But the play is really lost on tight end Tyler Warren’s block against rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas. Warren gets enough torque to seal Thomas inside and drive him three or four yards off the line. Thomas can’t lose his outside shoulder here. pic.twitter.com/Kt4kP9Oa4z — Chiefs Clips (@ChiefsClip58569) September 22, 2026 On this touchdown, the Chiefs don’t travel the corner with motion, keeping Kristian Fulton in the run fit. Unfortunately, Fulton has to take on Quentin Nelson with a full head of steam and gets pancaked. Hicks can’t beat the center to the hole, Drue Tranquill gets caught in the trash, and Nick Bolton has too much ground to cover. Defensive end George Karlaftis doesn’t get pinned like Thomas, but he still can’t shed the tight end to make the tackle. You could argue he was held, but it wasn’t called, and he needs to get off that block. These are only two plays, but they’re on tape now. Teams will keep running at Thomas and Felix Anudike-Uzomah because they’re light, so the Chiefs need to improve their edge setting.

Harlan and Green are fan favorites among Chiefs fans as they both have past ties to the organization and the city of Kansas City. Harlan graduated from the University of Kansas in 1982. Harlan also called basketball and football games for the University of Missouri from 1986-1989. Chiefs fans mainly remember Harlan as the team’s play-by-play radio announcer from 1985-1993. The biggest problem on the road against an opposing crowd was that the Chiefs went silent. There were multiple times when he was slow off the snap because of the silent count. For second time in three seasons, Nebraska will play at Arrowhead Stadium in KC | The Kansas City Star The Huskers will open their 2027 season against Miami (Ohio) on Aug. 27, a Friday. In 2025, Nebraska opened the season against Cincinnati at Arrowhead, defeating the Bearcats 20-17. The Cornhuskers’ leading rusher that game was Emmett Johnson, who became a Chiefs fifth-round draft pick this year. The game will mark the fourth appearance at Arrowhead by Nebraska. The Cornhuskers played the first game between FBS opponents at Arrowhead in 1998, when they defeated Oklahoma State. Andy Reid Gets Kansas City Chiefs-Inspired Nike Caitlin 1 Sea of Red | Sole Retriever In a social media post from the Kansas City Chiefs, coach Reid is seen holding a pair of the Nike Caitlin 1 Sea of Red that was given to him personally by Caitlin Clark. After shouting out Caitlin for the gift, Andy gives his praise to WNBA players, and of course, the sneakers, which fit the Chiefs primary color scheme. It’s also a perfect color palette for the Indiana Fever, but way back when Caitlin appeared on Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce’s podcast, she mentioned that her debut sneaker would get a KC colorway. Chiefs All-Pro Creed Humphrey serves pizza to Kansas City-area military families | KSHB 41 Dozens of service members from Whiteman Air Force Base were among those who spent the afternoon playing tailgate games and eating pizza outside Arrowhead Stadium as part of a partnership between Humphrey and Little Caesars’ Love Kitchen. “They’re the real heroes,” Humphrey, now in his sixth season with Kansas City, said. “So, any chance we had to be able to give back and help out, it’s an awesome opportunity.” Around the NFL Sources: Giants QB Jaxson Dart out for extended period | ESPN But sources told Rapoport and Garafolo that the second-year star will miss an extended period of time and is facing the possibility of season-ending surgery. Harbaugh said Tuesday that evaluations on Dart’s knee were still ongoing and declined to comment further on his timeline to return. “It’s an ongoing conversation about the health of a player, of a person,” Harbaugh said on a video call with reporters. “We’ve got to prepare for the range of possibilities.” Broncos’ Sean Payton accused Seahawks of cheating, sparking ‘Cold War,’ Mike Macdonald says | The Athletic According to Macdonald, the Seahawks scouted video of roughly 100 plays posted by fans on social media from Broncos training camp practices and used them to prepare for Payton’s team ahead of the 2024 season opener. “It’s like public knowledge. So we took like 100 plays from their training camp,” Macdonald said with a laugh. The Seahawks won the game, Macdonald’s first as head coach, 26-20. Bears QB Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol; Case Keenum could start Week 3 | NFL.com This always made a lot of sense, even before Goedert was sidelined. The team placed rookie TE Eli Stowers on IR at the start of the season, and Grant Calcaterra was put on IR at the end of training camp. With just Johnny Mundt and E.J. Jenkins left, the TE room gets an immediate boost by adding Ertz. The former Eagles draft pick has spent his time away from Philly with the Cardinals and Commanders, and has been a consistent factor in the redzone — regardless of the overall effectiveness of those offenses. Ertz is also just 11 receptions away from breaking Harold Carmichael’s franchise record (589) in Philadelphia to become the team’s leader all-time in catches. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Chiefs Film Review: Patrick Mahomes has monster game in Week 2 Mahomes was outstanding on Sunday, through a combination of making layups, working the pocket, and connecting on big plays down the field. The Chiefs offense has been firing the first two weeks of the season, but seeing Mahomes turn in a big performance on Sunday should be a sign to the rest of the NFL that he is well on his way back to prime form. full_text: The LA Rams have signed UDFA safety Maximus Pulley to the 53-man roster from the Eagles’ practice squad. To make room, the Rams placed Ronnie Rivers on IR after he was injured in Monday night’s game against the Giants. Pulley played for Wofford College in the NCAA Division I Football Championship Subdivision (FCS). In 34 career games, his statistics include: 185 total tackles, 100 solo, 7 TFLs, 7 INTs, 3 defensive TDs, 16 PBUs, 1 forced fumble, 5 fumble recoveries, and 1 blocked kick. According to SI’s Scouting Report: Maximus Pulley is a safety prospect who profiles best as a nickel defender, with good size and below-average length. He shows a quick trigger, high-end burst, and strong downhill closing ability. He excels as an underneath zone defender when roaming the intermediate areas of the field. He has a good feel for spacing, working to his depth, and shows quality range in the shallow areas. His most effective near the line of scrimmage, thriving in shallow zones and when playing the robber role. He has shown the ability to trigger on intermediate routes, take the ball away, and generate turnovers. He offers strong special teams value and projects as a nickel defender in a zone-heavy scheme and a fringe NFL rotational prospect. The same scouting report includes shallow zone awareness, instincts, and special teams value as some of Pulley’s strengths. Pulley can make an immediate impact on special teams and pass coverage in underneath zones. The fact that the Rams must now keep Pulley on the roster indicates they like what they see in the young man. The only remaining question is whether the Rams move someone off the roster to make room for a third running back.
