title: The two DBs who actually showed up in Weeks 1 & 2
summary: The jury is still out on the 2026 Los Angeles Rams. LA came out flat in Week 1 to lose an all-important game to their NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers. They bounced back in Week 2 to keep a bad New York Giants team in the losing column. But there is one huge positive […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Trent McDuffie #22 of the Los Angeles Rams runs on the field during the third quarter of the game against the New York Giants at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The jury is still out on the 2026 Los Angeles Rams. LA came out flat in Week 1 to lose an all-important game to their NFC West rival San Francisco 49ers. They bounced back in Week 2 to keep a bad New York Giants team in the losing column. But there is one huge positive for the Rams: Trent McDuffie and Quentin Lake are performing at superstar levels. LA sent a haul of draft picks to the Kansas City Chiefs in order to acquire McDuffie, and then they signed the corner to one of the richest contracts at the position. The team also committed to Lake long-term before the conclusion of last season. Both moves are paying dividends into 2026. McDuffie and Lake are on pace for All-Pro seasons. This is expected for McDuffie. It would be a first for Lake. All data from Pro Football Focus (PFF). Trent McDuffie, CB PFF coverage grade: 93.2 (1st among all corners) The Rams are paying McDuffie to be one of the best corners in all of football. He’s currently the best corner in the NFL. Opposing quarterbacks have thrown the ball his direction eight times through two games. He’s allowed one reception for 13 yards while also forcing an interception and three pass breakups. That’s good for a passer rating of 0.0. It quite literally does not get any better than that. And the even better news is that the Rams have faced potent threats at receiver. Mike Evans caught six passes in Week 1 but only totaled 49 yards and a goal line score. Malik Nabers hauled in just one of his four targets on Monday night for one yard. That’s pretty good. McDuffie’s best work has perhaps been in the screen game, which is important to consider since that was the majority of the 49ers’ offense in Week 1. He has been aggressive to step up to the line of scrimmage and make a tackle. It’s impressive to watch for a player who is generally seen as undersized. McDuffie brings a needed tenacity to the defense. Jameis Winston intercepted by Trent McDuffie! @NYGvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/LPX9L8tcnG — NFL (@NFL) September 22, 2026 Quentin Lake, DB PFF coverage grade: 92.2 (1st among all safeties) Before the 49ers game got away from the Rams, Lake intercepted a Brock Purdy deep ball for one of his teams few defensive stops in Australia. With Kamren Kinchens out due to injury in Week 2, Lake held his assigned receiver to just three catches on six targets for a measly 10 yards. The three incompletions were all pass breakups. Lake has five PBU’s on the season already. While Lake cannot claim a 0.0 passer rating like McDuffie, he’s still doing just fine at 44.8. For comparison, you’d get a passer rating of 39.6 just by spiking the ball over and over. Passer ratings only go lower because of interceptions. Opposing offenses are targeting Lake often. 16 passes have been thrown his direction already. The good news is he’s punishing them for it, as he’s allowed just 10 catches for 64 yards. 30 of those yards came after the catch point. That isn’t efficient pass game production. Quentin Lake with the PBU 🙌 @NYGvsLAR on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/Hd0kz2hyRP — NFL (@NFL) September 22, 2026

title: Is this first-round WR on his way out of NFC West?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison, Jr. fourth overall during the 2024 NFL Draft. Through two games he’s caught just a single pass for 33 yards. Across three seasons he has put together a level of production that you’d expect in a single year for a superstar receiver: 104 receptions for 1,526 yards and 12 […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - SEPTEMBER 20: Marvin Harrison Jr. #18 of the Arizona Cardinals walks off the field after his teams 7-31 loss against the Seattle Seahawks at State Farm Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals drafted Marvin Harrison, Jr. fourth overall during the 2024 NFL Draft. Through two games he’s caught just a single pass for 33 yards. Across three seasons he has put together a level of production that you’d expect in a single year for a superstar receiver: 104 receptions for 1,526 yards and 12 touchdowns. It’s clear that Harrison hasn’t been the player the Cardinals expected. He’s an afterthought in the 2026 offense under Mike LaFleur. The Cardinals just signed their best receiver, Michael Wilson, to a three-year, $75M deal . Would Arizona seriously consider cutting their losses and trade away Harrison ? The Cardinals will be one of the top contenders for a quarterback in the 2027 draft class but may be too good to land the first overall pick. Equipping yourself with extra ammunition is never a bad idea if you need to move up a few slots to get your guy. If the Cardinals decide to move on, these are the most logical landing spots for the former fourth overall pick: Los Angeles Rams It’s clear the Rams have a third receiver problem. Heck, with Puka Nacua’s uncertain injury status, they might actually have a starting receiver problem. Davante Adams is unlikely to be on the roster in 2027. Nacua’s contract is set to expire at the end of the year. In addition to an immediate need, the Rams also must consider their long-term succession plan at receiver. Sean McVay is the right person to take a struggling receiver from another team and then maximize his superpowers in Los Angeles. LA is missing draft capital from their acquisition of Myles Garrett, but we know they are aggressive and are looking to maximize a Super Bowl window. Las Vegas Raiders To everyone’s surprise, the Raiders have started the season 2-0. They also accomplished this feat without their top receiving threat in Brock Bowers. But even with Bowers, Vegas lacks quality and depth at receiver. They already have their quarterback of the future in Fernando Mendoza. If you’re tracking to achieve better outcomes than expected, why not acquire Mendoza’s go-to receiver of the future? New England Patriots The Patriots already made a splash move at receiver by acquiring AJ Brown from the Eagles. Other teams, like the Rams, were scared off of Brown’s injury history and late-career trajectory. This line of thought proved wise as Brown is currently set to miss the next month after suffering an injury in the season opener. New England was being proactive and attempting to surround Drake Maye with more dangerous weaponry. It was the right idea. The execution doesn’t seem to be there. Could they try again? Indianapolis Colts This fit makes sense until you realize the amount of draft capital the Colts are already missing because of the Sauce Gardner trade. Indianapolis traded away Michael Pittman to the Steelers and chose to keep Alec Pierce on a long-term contract. Pierce is now out for at least the next four games. The Colts’ moves are telling us they need to win now. Trotting out the ghost of Keenan Allen, Laquon Treadwell, and a lackluster receiving corps says otherwise. While Indy may not have sufficient draft capital to make this move, their depth chart is screaming “help!” Kansas City Chiefs I don’t understand the Chiefs’ reluctance to surround Patrick Mahomes with a competent receiver group. Harrison would be an immediate upgrade over any of their other options. KC has serious salary cap challenges short-term. Fortunately, Harrison is on a rookie deal and that should be manageable enough.

title: How Davante Got His Groove Back: Rams Film Room
summary: The Los Angeles Rams needed Davante Adams to have a strong performance in Week 2, but what the veteran receiver did against the New York Giants blew past even the loftiest expectations. Like many Rams, Adams struggled mightily in the Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, something that he’d have […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams needed Davante Adams to have a strong performance in Week 2, but what the veteran receiver did against the New York Giants blew past even the loftiest expectations. Like many Rams, Adams struggled mightily in the Week 1 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia, something that he’d have to overcome quickly to help this franchise reach the heights it plans to reach in 2026. Even more immediately, with Puka Nacua out against the Giants, the Rams needed him to pick up even more slack in the passing game. Adams answered the call and assembled one of the best single-game performances of his potentially Hall of Fame-caliber career , posting eight receptions for 195 yards and two touchdowns, setting a new personal best during his Rams tenure and coming just 11 yards shy of a career high overall. His production was more than just absorbing manufactured, forced touches. Adams put together a vintage effort, showing off the skill set that has set him apart from most of his wide receiver counterparts for a decade while reestablishing his chemistry with quarterback Matthew Stafford. On his first touchdown grab of the day, Adams does a great job navigating space, making an adjustment to the ball and finishing the run after catch. It’s an in-breaking route for Adams, who releases cleanly but then has to bounce off of safety Tyler Nubin (27). Adams does so without getting forced too far off the route and still gets to his spot. The throw is a bit high, but the receiver adjusts with a full extension to snatch it out of the air and cruises to the end zone for six points. Credit to Xavier Smith for helping clear the path near the end zone with a late block as well. The end zone view is useful for this play too to emphasize the point about the chemistry between receiver and quarterback made above. Stafford has always been a trick-shot artist of a quarterback, that’s not new information. This is a fun one, as he slides left, drops his arm angle low and throws back against the grain. The high throw forces Adams to adjust but it also completely neutralizes the linebacker (Zaire Barnes, 46) beyond any potential usefulness. There’s a lot of trust on display here, with the quarterback getting the ball exactly where it needs to be while trusting his receiver will go up and get it. The Rams couldn’t cash in at the end of the first half when Harrison Mevis missed a long field goal as time expired. But Adams is the reason they got in position to even try a kick before the break. Adams has always been among the best receivers in the NFL when it comes to releases (it’s an easy argument to call him the very best, in fact), and those traits are on display here. That slight hop is his signature move, a crossover inspired by his love for basketball . It helps him get away from cornerback Greg Newsome II (20) here and he can get his head around faster than the defender at the top of the route. Adams is thus the only one who can make a play on this ball. And boy, does he make a play on it. He (cleanly) fights back to the ball, boxes out the corner and hangs on for the explosive gain. This is just a stellar individual effort from a player who has run a ton of routes and fought for a lot of contested balls in his career. There’s a small number of receivers who can make that type of play, one that requires the right mix of finesse and physicality from beginning to end. Finally, let’s look at this second touchdown grab of the game, one in which he cooks another defensive back on a great end zone fade. Cornerback Colton Hood (12) had a lot of fans in the draft process this offseason, and he ended up going in the second round when plenty of analysts and pundits pegged him as a first-round talent. But no matter how gifted you are, a rookie is going to have a long day at the office when they’re battling Davante Adams in the red zone. The veteran has more than enough space to hit that crossover release, create more separation and float to the boundary in the end zone. Stafford places this ball perfectly and it’s as well-executed of a fade as you’re going to find. It’s picture-perfect stuff. Adams isn’t the same receiver he was when he earned three consecutive first-team All-Pro honors from ages 28-30, but he can still be a useful and vital weapon for the Rams this season. Even if he’s not posting nearly 200 yards and two scores every week, it was great to see his skill set is (predictably) still aging gracefully and that he still has the full route tree at his disposal.

summary: Brandin Cooks was drafted in 2014 by the New Orleans Saints and at this point, Cooks is a veteran journeyman of the NFL. full_text: OXNARD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 8: Wide receivers Brandin Cooks #3 of the Dallas Cowboys and Cooper Kupp #10 of the Los Angeles Rams talk on the field following a joint practice at Cowboys training camp on August 8, 2024 in Oxnard, California. (Photo by Kevork Djansezian/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brandin Cooks was drafted in 2014 by the New Orleans Saints and at this point, Cooks is a veteran journeyman of the NFL. He’s played for the Saints, the New England Patriots, the Los Angeles Rams, the Houston Texans, the Dallas Cowboys, the Buffalo Bills (any teams I missed?), and he’s now signing to the San Francisco 49ers practice squad. For Cooks and the Rams, it was a fairly successful stint. Heck, had he and the Rams won the Super Bowl in the 2018 season , Cooks may have been the MVP with over 100 receiving yards. Had Jared Goff and Cooks connected on a touchdown, who knows? Maybe Cooks spends more time with the Rams than he did. Maybe Goff does too. But the past can’t be changed, and instead, the Rams didn’t win that Super Bowl, Cooks seemed to get hurt often, and though Cooks was a solid Ram, he’s not likely to go down as an all-time great Ram. That being said. Cooks has put together a solid if not great NFL career in terms of production, longevity and as far I am aware he’s a drama free type player. There’s a lot to like about Cooks, and the 49ers are giving him a chance to compete in 2026. With the way the 49ers are looking right now who’s to say? Maybe Cooks finds himself in another Super Bowl. We’ll see. Source: Niners signing veteran receiver Cooks to practice squad (espn.com) “Free agent wide receiver Brandin Cooks is signing with the San Francisco 49ers ‘ practice squad, initially to get up to speed for games, a source told ESPN’s Adam Schefter on Tuesday. Cooks, 32, joins a Niners team that has lost wideouts Ricky Pearsall , De’Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson to injury this season. Meanwhile, veteran wide receiver Mike Evans will need to be managed this week with a hip injury. Cooks was the 20th pick in the 2014 draft by the Saints out of Oregon State , and he spent the first three years of his career with New Orleans. He returned to the Saints in 2025 but was waived in November after he requested his release. Cooks then joined the Buffalo Bills for the remainder of the campaign” No QB has more games with 4-plus TD passes than Matthew Stafford since 2021 (ramswire) “On Monday night, the NFL’s reigning MVP, Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, was simply sensational, getting back to basics in his four-touchdown performance. Slicing and dicing the New York Giants ‘ defense, Stafford found Terrance Ferguson, Kyren Williams, and Davante Adams twice for his passing scores that led to a 28-6 win. According to Pro Football Focus, Stafford’s performance was his 10th game with at least four passing touchdowns since 2021, which is tied with Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott for the most within that timeframe. Of course, 2021 was his first year with the Rams.“ Rams WR Davante Adams Raises Fascinating Matthew Stafford-Sean McVay What-if (sports.yahoo) “During an appearance Tuesday on The Pat McAfee Show, future Pro Football Hall of Famer Adams wondered what it could have been like if Stafford and McVay had been together much longer on the same team. “If Matthew Stafford was here with Sean McVay for his whole career, they would be saying, ‘ Is this guy literally the best QB that’s ever played,” Adams said.“ Poona Ford and Aaron Donald are Rams’ perfect pairing up front (ramblinfan) “With Donald back in the rotation, Ford’s value to the defense has skyrocketed along with that of Kobie Turner and even Braden Fiske. While Donald commands offensive lines’ attention, LA finally has defenders who can make them pay for leaving them one-on-one. Ford is among them. Double teams smothered LA’s short nose tackle was smothered in the season opener. Conversely, when Ford lined up alongside Donald in Week 2, he was the one doing the smothering. While his 5-foot-11 frame may look like a liability, it affords him tremendous power and an unnaturally strong center of gravity. That was all on display against the Giants on Monday Night Football. “ Rams vs. Broncos Prediction, Odds, Spread, Injuries, Trends for NFL Week 3 (si.com) “The Broncos and Nix rallied from an early deficit to defeat the Jacksonville Jaguars at home, and Stafford and Co. looked elite on offense in a win over the New York Giants on Monday night. L.A. didn’t have Puka Nacua (hip) or Myles Garret (knee) in that game, and Garrett remains on injured reserve and will miss this primetime matchup. Los Angeles is the favorite to win the Super Bowl this season, and both of these teams were in their respective conference championship games in the 2025 campaign. So, this should be a good litmus test for both franchises as they look to see how they stack up against the best teams in the NFL.“ Here’s how much Rams-Broncos Sunday Night Football tickets are going for (9news) “The L.A. Rams, led by quarterback Matthew Stafford, are coming to the Mile High to take on Bo Nix and the Broncos Sunday night. Tickets for the game are kind of affordable. On SeatGeek , the cheapest pair was going for $410, and on StubHub the lowest pair of seats is at $392.“ Rams PFF grades: Best and worst performers in win vs. Giants (ramswire) “ The Rams made their 28-6 win over the Giants look easy, dominating on each side of the ball throughout the night. New York only had 182 total yards on offense, which is 13 fewer than Davante Adams had himself. Jameis Winston completed just 11 of his 27 passes after replacing the injured Jaxson Dart, largely because the Rams were in the pockets of New York’s receivers all night. Pro Football Focus handed out grades for every Rams player who took the field, and we sorted them by the best and worst performers (min. 10 snaps).“ “The monster has returned,” Stephen A. Smith marvels at Rams’ bounce-back (sports.yahoo) “ “We witnessed the Los Angeles Rams,” Smith said on ‘The Stephen A. title: Raiders defense is ready for Saints offense
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are heading into the Superdome in New Orleans to take on a red-hot Saints team. Every week in the NFL, teams must prove themselves and show what they are about. Winning the first two games against the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers is fine and dandy, but taking on […]
full_text: (Robert Gauthier/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) The Las Vegas Raiders are heading into the Superdome in New Orleans to take on a red-hot Saints team. Every week in the NFL, teams must prove themselves and show what they are about. Winning the first two games against the Miami Dolphins and the Los Angeles Chargers is fine and dandy, but taking on the New Orleans Saints is a different story. Saints head coach and offensive play caller/designer Kellen Moore has proven to be a second-half team on offense in the first two games. Against the Detroit Lions, the Saints didn’t score a point in the first half and scored 30 in the second half and overtime. In Week 2, the Saints only scored six points in the first half and 18 in the second half. Despite slow starts, they have produced 54 points, the 9th-highest in the league and are averaging 27 points per game. Through the air Quarterback Tyler Shough, is completing 68.9% of his passes and has thrown four touchdown passes, adding one touchdown run from the goal line. Shough has also been sacked eight times and thrown two interceptions on the season. Possessing a live arm, good accuracy and decision-making, Shough is distributing the ball to his primary pass catchers frequently. Chris Olave and Devaughn Vele are the Saints top-2 receiving options; being targeted a combined 39 times and completing 30. Accounting for nearly half of Shough’s 62 total completions while averaging 10+ yards per reception between them. Olave is arguably the best wide receiver challenge the Raiders’ young defensive backfield has seen thus far and Vele is an ascending player. Tight end Juwan Johnson is not quite sneaky good, but a break-the-glass safety player who can get things moving in a pinch. Catching seven of his 11 targets for a respectable 120 yards and a touchdown in the young season. More of a chain mover than a game-breaker he will be a piece best utilized to clear underneath coverage for easier throws to the wideouts. Ground but no pound Running the football has been an issue for the Saints. In two games, they have rushed the ball 52 times for 156 yards and two touchdowns. Averaging 3.0 yards per carry, it remains a work in progress. None of their featured backs are over 100 yards for the season. Collectively, they have six broken tackles. Travis Etienne and Alvin Kamara are getting a combined 45.5 yards per game. With left tackle Kelvin Banks suffering a severe high-ankle sprain requiring surgery, those run game numbers may sink even lower. The blind-side pass protection is going to take a hit too and for a defense that has forced eight fumbles and eight sacks, they should be licking their chops.

title: Raiders film room: The Cody White game-sealing touchdown
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders pulled off a road win, their first at SoFi Stadium. The team was touchdown underdogs, went into Los Angeles, and beat the Chargers 26-14. After Nakobe Dean caused a fumble, the Raiders were in position to close out the football game. After two run plays in a row, Klint Kubiak faced […]
full_text: (Photo by Jeff Antenore/MediaNews Group/Orange County Register via Getty Images) | MediaNews Group via Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders pulled off a road win, their first at SoFi Stadium. The team was touchdown underdogs, went into Los Angeles, and beat the Chargers 26-14. After Nakobe Dean caused a fumble, the Raiders were in position to close out the football game. After two run plays in a row, Klint Kubiak faced a third-and-five. He went for the gut and threw a game-sealing touchdown pass to Cody White from 11 yards out. The setup for this play came in Week 1 vs. the Miami Dolphins. On a third-and-three, the Raiders got a seven-yard run from Ashton Jeanty out of the same look. Michael Mayer goes in motion, and after the snap, Ian Thomas pulls to lead-block for Jeanty. Fast forward to Sunday against the Chargers, and the Raiders are back in the red zone, and it’s third down once again. They line up in the same formation that they did against the Dolphins. This time, though, Mayer goes out to the flat, and Cody White runs a corner route. Final TD for the Raiders was a great design my Kubiak. Raiders have ran this same run look since preseason but this time it’s a PA corner route Cody White sells the block before breaking to the corner. Once again easy money pic.twitter.com/U2pro2G7fP — Marcus Johnson (@TheMarcJohnNFL) September 21, 2026 White sets up the play perfectly, using the same blocking motion he used in Week 1 against the Dolphins. However, he cuts upfield, and nobody on the opposing defense follows him. This leads to a wide-open touchdown and the Raiders going up 24-14.

title: Raiders-Saints Week 3: Kicking battle will be watched closely
summary: It would be fitting if Sunday’s game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the host New Orleans Saints play Sunday comes down to a kicker. The kicking mathcup is one of the bigger storylines in this game. In March, the Raiders signed veteran Matt Gay ending the Daniel Carlson era in Las Vegas. He signed […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images It would be fitting if Sunday’s game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the host New Orleans Saints play Sunday comes down to a kicker. The kicking mathcup is one of the bigger storylines in this game. In March, the Raiders signed veteran Matt Gay ending the Daniel Carlson era in Las Vegas. He signed with the Raiders in 2019. Carlson, after surprisingly sitting available all offseason as a free agent, signed with the Saints in August. Carlson, 31, has made four of five field-goal attempts as a Saint. His one miss was a 62-yarder at the end of regulation in Week 1. Gay, 32, has made all three of his field-goal attempts with the Raiders, including a 59-yarder at the end of the first half Sunday in the win at the Chargers. Gay has been kicking in the NFL for eight years, originally breaking in with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2019. He spent one year in Tampa Bay before three seasons with the Los Angeles Rams, making the Pro Bowl in 2021, then two campaigns with the Indianapolis Colts before spending this past fall with the Washington Commanders (10 games) and San Francisco 49ers (two games). Going into this season, Gay had a career field goal percentage of 84.3 percent (73.9 percent in 2025) with a long of 58 yards (56 yards in 2025) and has made 96.7 percent of his extra points (100 percent in ‘25). Carlson entered this season with an 86.9 career field goal percentage (81.5 percent), a long of 60 yards (which was set this past season) and 95.7 extra point rate (95.5 percent). Now, they go head-to-head Sunday with both players wanting to send a message to the Raiders. Raider Nation, take the conversation everywhere! summary: The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Tampa Bay Buccaneers Injury Report Terms and Glossary Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Jones Sr. #33 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball during the third quarter of the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings and Tampa Bay Buccaneers released their first injury reports in advance of their Sunday afternoon matchup in Tampa. Here they are. Minnesota Vikings Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Jordan Mason* RB Thumb DNP IR-OUT Jake Golday LB Ankle DNP Aaron Jones* RB Knee DNP Brett Thorson* P Hamstring DNP DeeJay Dallas RB Toe LP Ty Ingram-Dawkins* DL Oblique LP Brian O’Neill* RT Knee LP Jalen Redmond DT Elbow LP Nick Samac C Knee LP Tampa Bay Buccaneers Player Name Position Injury Wednesday Thursday Friday Injury Designation Rueban Bain Jr.* OLB Groin DNP Baker Mayfield* QB Illness FP Jalen McMillan WR Knee FP Anthony Nelson LB Shin DNP Jacob Parrish CB Back FP Josiah Trotter* LB Shoulder DNP Injury Report Terms and Glossary FP = Full participant in practice. LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. NIR = Not injury related. PUP = Physically unable to participate list. IR = Injured reserve. Note: only starters on IR are listed. Player Name* = Starter. Injury designation definitions: Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and play on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically, only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and play on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day, and league rules prohibit them from playing. Notes on Injured Players For the Vikings, the running back room has been hit pretty hard. Jordan Mason is on IR, Aaron Jones did not practice with a knee injury he suffered against the Bears, and DeeJay Dallas was limited with a toe injury. It sounds like the Vikings and Jones are doing everything they can to try to get him in shape to play on Sunday afternoon, but we’ll have to wait and see on progress. Kevin O’Connell expressed confidence in Demond Claiborne, the only halfback not on the injury list, to play as necessary, but he’s only had a handful of snaps in two games. Brett Thorson is also worth monitoring. Hamstring injuries for punters can be tricky to recover from at that position. Other than that, nothing terribly concerning among the other injuries at this point. For the Bucs, a couple of key injuries to starters Rueban Bain Jr. and Josiah Trotter defensively. Bain is a rookie first-round draft pick who has gotten off to a slow start with only one tackle in two games and just a 2.6% pass rush win rate. Bucs head coach Todd Bowles said he’s probably not completely healthy when asked about his performance, so we’ll see if he is active on Sunday against the Vikings. It wouldn’t be terribly surprising if he is dealing with something that is slowing him down- like a groin injury can- if they rested him on Sunday. Linebacker Josiah Trotter also did not practice with a shoulder injury. He is also a rookie and second-round pick that has graded well after two games. Apparently, he has been wearing a shoulder brace and harness for soreness all year so far. Unclear if that condition has worsened- he did leave the game briefly last week with a shoulder injury- but injury reports tomorrow and Friday should provide more insight. Stay tuned. title: Isaiah Rodgers Named NFC Special Teams Player of the Week
summary: The defense was the story for the Minnesota Vikings in their 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears this past Sunday, but one of their players was recognized on Wendesday for their contributions on special teams. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers was named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week on Wednesday. He’s the first member of […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Isaiah Rodgers #2 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates against the Chicago Bears during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defense was the story for the Minnesota Vikings in their 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears this past Sunday, but one of their players was recognized on Wendesday for their contributions on special teams. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers was named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week on Wednesday. He’s the first member of the team to receive weekly award recognition this season. Rodgers made, arguably, the biggest play of the Vikings’ win at Soldier Field, as his block of Cairo Santos’ 23-yard field goal attempt that would have tied the game with six minutes left in the fourth quarter helped to preserve what was then a 6-3 Minnesota lead. The block was the first for the Vikings since Week 9 of 2025, when Levi Drake Rodriguez blocked a field goal attempt against Detroit (with Rodgers recovering the loose ball). Rodriguez also won NFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors for his performance. This is the second weekly award that Rodgers has won since joining the Vikings. He was named the NFC’s Defensive Player of the Week in Week 3 of last season when he returned both an interception and a fumble for a touchdown in the same quarter in a blowout victory over the Cincinnati Bengals. Rodgers is also now the only player in the league with at least one blocked kick in each of the last three seasons. Congratulations to Isaiah Rodgers on being named the NFC’s Special Teams Player of the Week for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL season!

full_text: CHICAGO, IL - SEPTEMBER 2026: Minnesota Vikings linebacker Andrew van Ginkel (43) celebrates Minnesota Vikings cornerback Isaiah Rodgers' (2) fumble recovery in the third quarter against the Chicago Bears on Sunday Sept. 20, 2026 at Soldier Field in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) The Minnesota Vikings won a hard-fought but ugly 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears on a wet, messy Soldier Field Sunday to move to 2-0 in the young 2026 season. They’ve now won seven straight on the road against the Bears; better yet, that puts them 2-0 in the NFC North (and NFC) in the early race for a division crown and for advantageous playoff seeding. The staff at the DN did their usual stellar job recapping the highlights from the satisfying win here , here , and here . No need for me to be redundant. Instead, here are some underlying narratives on my mind heading into our Week 3 trip to Tampa Bay to play the inconsistent and baffling Buccaneers. Appreciate this defense (it won’t last forever). Listen, I can’t say anything about Brian Flores that hasn’t already been said. I’ve sung the guy’s praises from Day One. What we’re seeing now is the equivalent of the Vikings’ offense from 1998-2000. While it felt like that would last forever (or at least more than three seasons), it didn’t. This won’t either. Flores will get another head-coaching opportunity. And just as Cris Carter got older and Robert Smith retired abruptly after a 1,500-yard (and best) season, things happen (often unexpectedly). I’ve never been more impressed by a defensive coordinator in all my decades of following this team, and we’ve had some great ones. Sunday’s performance against the Bears was another masterpiece. Before leaving the game with an injury Caleb Williams struggled against the Vikings defense. 🏈 Blitzed on 24 of his 31 dropbacks (77%) going 12-21 passes with an INT and sack. 🏈 Pressured on 14 of 31 dropbacks (45%) going 3-10 with an INT and 2 sacks 🏈 1-7 with an INT on… pic.twitter.com/7RIgMRtI8x — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) September 20, 2026 It's so fascinating to re-watch the Vikings' defensive performance on tape. Just advantages everywhere. Chicago keeps six in protect, only five men rush, and there's still an unblocked pressure. "Blitzing" oversimplifies the Vikings' strategy. It's just advantage creation. — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) September 21, 2026 Offensive line promise. An issue that’s plagued this team for years; hopefully, the offensive line concerns have finally dissipated. It’s only two games, so I don’t want to get too excited yet. But the narrative that Chris Kuper was the villain in recent years could have some legs. Ed Ingram signed a 3-year, $37.5 million contract extension with the Texans in March. Garrett Bradbury posted a decent 63.1 PFF pass-blocking grade for the AFC champion Patriots last season; the Bears saw enough to hand him the starting job this year. New o-line coordinator Keith Carter has done a solid job so far, despite some early-game hiccups in Week 1, which were not unexpected. The line held up relatively well amid wet, generally horrible conditions in Chicago on Sunday. Carson Wentz had time in the pocket, and the unit clearly executed the game plan to eat clock and pound the Bears in the run game, with Aaron Jones carrying 23 times for 105 yards (4.6 avg.). The left side of the line has been particularly impressive. Christian Darrisaw and Donovan Jackson have yet to allow a pressure through 2 weeks for the Minnesota Vikings, per @SumerSports — Shawn Syed (@SyedSchemes) September 20, 2026 On that note… Giving KAM some credit. The lack of draft success and playoff wins cost former Vikings general manager Kwesi Adofo-Mensah his job after last season. The J.J. McCarthy decision may have ultimately been the deciding factor. Not all positions are created equal. When you select a quarterback in the Top 10 (and trade up to do it), the pressure to hit that pick is enormous, given the quarterback’s importance in the modern NFL. You can recover from a miss here or there at cornerback or in the trenches; heck, even at wide receiver. But a QB selection that high? It’s a whole other level of responsibility. That said, let’s give KAM his due. Addison is Addison. Donovan Jackson appears to have taken important steps in his development after a solid rookie season. Over the first two games of the season, Dallas Turner looks like Lawrence Taylor. Per Next Gen Stats, Turner has a ridiculous 20 QB pressures to go with his three sacks. We must also note the important, under-the-radar free agents like Jalen Redmond and Isaiah Rodgers, who are paying huge dividends. If the Vikings achieve something special this season, KAM’s influence will be significant. KOC’s leadership. After a sluggish start against the Packers on opening day, KOC has the Vikings playing smart, clean football over the past two weeks. We have the fewest penalties in the NFL so far and have only one turnover. Wentz has been fortunate on a few possible INTs, it must be said. Pro Football Focus also ranks the Vikings 1st in special teams so far this young season. All of these are critical elements to realizing a successful 2026 campaign. KOC also appears to be evolving as a play caller. As Alec Lewis of The Athletic noted, since December 1st of last season, the Vikings’ 53.8% run rate is second in the NFL behind the Baltimore Ravens. That can certainly be attributed to the QBs he’s started in those games, but Lewis also noted that the team has a 51.2% run rate while trailing over that period, which is the highest in the league. The clear commitment to win Sunday’s game on the back of Aaron Jones was also encouraging. Even if this commitment to the run game continues, the passing game still needs to improve. Yes, I know the weather in Chicago was abysmal, but our 129.5 passing yards per game ranks 31st in the NFL and is just six yards more than the Cooper Rush-led Atlanta Falcons. Jordan Addison, one of the premier WR2s in the NFL, has just two receptions for 21 yards. That is just wrong on so many levels, but the fact that it’s hurting my fantasy team is near the top of the list. Now I’m simply chalking this up to the perfect storm of Kyler Murray’s injury and awful weather, but if he doesn’t add a lot more to this offensive production over the next few weeks, we can dust off the panic button for possible use. All we need is something close to 2024 Murray, paired with this defense, to have another Case Keenum-Sam Darnold magic-carpet-ride season on our hands. Minus, of course, the unfortunate playoff implosions. CONCLUSION The Vikings are 2-0, but we’ve gotten some breaks. A dominant 4th-quarter defensive effort and timely offensive plays were aided by the Packers’ explosion of costly, high-leverage penalties in Week 1. And if Caleb Williams hadn’t suffered the hamstring injury memed around the world on Sunday, do we win that game? Maybe. Maybe not. But it doesn’t matter. Wins are wins, and you are what your record says you are. The name of the game is to play well every week and put yourself in a position to win games in the 4th quarter. There are no gimmes in the NFL. Just ask the team we play next week. At 2-0 with two wins in the division, the Vikings have a solid early cushion to build on over the next month, before the schedule gets tougher in the middle of the season. Let’s hope they can capitalize on it. Stay tuned.

full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings will once again be relegated to the late afternoon window in Week 3, and because of that the area where you’ll be able to view them live on over-the-air television is a bit more limited than it has been over the first couple of weeks of the season. The folks from 506 Sports have released the coverage maps for this week’s NFL games. Here is the map for the late window games on FOX, with the Vikings’ game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers represented by the blue area. As you can see, the blue area is not terribly large. It encompasses a decent chunk of the midwest as well as most of Florida, as well as the Houston metro area, a portion of the New England states, the Pittsburgh area, and the Indianapolis/Cincinnati areas. This seems like as good a time as any to review the NFL’s doubleheader rules, since they’ll be affecting the Vikings here. Both CBS and FOX are allowed to air doubleheaders in Week 1 and Week 18, but after that they alternate weeks as to who can show a doubleheader in a single market. This week, CBS has the doubleheader. So, if you live in the blue area, there will NOT be an early game on your local FOX affiliate before the Vikings’ game kicks off at 3:05 PM Central. There will be an early and a late game on your local CBS affiliate, but not on FOX. The other FOX game in the late window is represented by the orange area on the map above, which is the Arizona Cardinals at the San Francisco 49ers. The rest of the map above is colored for the early games on FOX. Red: Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills Green: New York Jets at Detroit Lions Yellow: Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders Aqua: Carolina Panthers at Cleveland Browns The doubleheader rules also mean that if you live outside of the blue area, you will have to find the game on YouTube TV NFL Sunday Ticket. Or find an alternative location to watch the game from or something. So, if you want to watch the Vikings live this weekend, it might be a bit more difficult than it’s been over the first two weeks of the season. Hopefully, as many Vikings fans as possible will be able to find a way to watch this one.

title: Vikings Add Johnny Hekker, Jaret Patterson to Practice Squad
summary: On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings made a couple of practice squad moves, at least one of which points to a potential issue with the club’s special teams unit. The team has announced that they have added punter Johnny Hekker and running back Jaret Patterson to the practice squad. To make room, the team has waived […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Johnny Hekker #5 of the Minnesota Vikings punts the ball against the Baltimore Ravens during the third quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Tuesday, the Minnesota Vikings made a couple of practice squad moves, at least one of which points to a potential issue with the club’s special teams unit. The team has announced that they have added punter Johnny Hekker and running back Jaret Patterson to the practice squad. To make room, the team has waived cornerback Bryce Phillips and wide receiver Trayvon Rudolph. The Vikings have also waived defensive lineman Taki Taimani from injured reserve. Hekker, who spent the preseason with the Vikings and ultimately lost the team’s punting battle to rookie Brett Thorson, is back with the team because Thorson is now dealing with a hamstring injury that he suffered at some point during the team’s 9-3 victory over the Chicago Bears on Sunday. The team is still evaluating Thorson’s condition, and it isn’t known at this time whether or not he will miss any time. If he does, the long-time veteran will be prepared to take over Thorson’s duties as both punter and holder for Will Reichard. Patterson has been in the league for a few seasons, as he signed with the Washington Football Team as an undrafted free agent in 2021. He spent his first two seasons with Washington, rushing for 266 yards and two touchdowns on 68 carries in his first season before appearing in only three games in his second season and getting just 17 carries. He spent part of the 2023 season on the Los Angeles Chargers’ practice squad and then landed back with Washington’s practice squad after being let go by the Chargers in December. Patterson has spent the last two seasons with the Chargers. He appeared in just one game in 2024 and in six games in 2025, carrying the ball 41 times for 159 yards and a touchdown. It’s possible that Patterson was brought in because DeeJay Dallas could be dealing with an injury now as well. Dallas went out of Sunday’s game in Chicago after suffering what appeared to be some sort of leg injury in the fourth quarter. The Vikings also have veteran running back Jerome Ford on the practice squad, having signed him in the week leading up to the Bears game.

title: Drake Maye, Patriots offense looking to find rhythm after slow start
summary: It’s been a slow start to the season for Drake Maye and the New England Patriots offense. Through two games, the unit is averaging just 11.5 points per game while ranking 23rd in EPA/play. For Maye, it’s a familiar position. The Patriots started 1-2 last season after turning the ball over five times in a […]
full_text: It’s been a slow start to the season for Drake Maye and the New England Patriots offense. Through two games, the unit is averaging just 11.5 points per game while ranking 23rd in EPA/play. For Maye, it’s a familiar position. The Patriots started 1-2 last season after turning the ball over five times in a Week 3 loss. They responded by scoring 42 points against the Carolina Panthers, kick-starting an 11-game winning streak. Now, Maye and the Patriots offense are working to try to spark another turnaround. “I think we’re finding ourselves,” Maye said about the offense. “Every time you get into a new season with new guys and new players and you’re battling injuries, you know, every team in the league is trying to really to improve. And really for us, it’s really about finding ourselves. “This time last year, I remember we were 1-2 and going into the Panthers and we were kind of figuring ourselves out and just things that, you know, guys and find rhythm on offense getting down in the run game and doing little things and really just find ourselves and kind of find a rhythm.” Part of New England’s struggles can be traced back to the quarterback. After an overly aggressive fourth quarter in Seattle leading to three interceptions and a loss, Maye seemed to swing the pendulum too far back in the other direction against the Steelers. There were multiple instances where Maye passed up opportunities to attack downfield, such as on the Patriots’ first possession where rookie tight end Eli Raridon broke free uncovered up the seam as the No. 1 read in the progression, only for Maye to check it down to Rhamondre Stevenson. “It’s being decisive in everyone’s play, but it’s certainly magnified with the quarterback,” head coach Mike Vrabel said Wednesday. “So being decisive, believing in what you see. Again, that’s what we ask all our players to do is prepare to try to play fast and aggressively and make great decisions. “So, yeah, we could always say, “Man, we should have let that one rip,” or “We’ve got to make a better decision.” Ultimately, it’s his responsibility to be able to distribute the football as quickly and decisively as possible in the places that it’s supposed to go, continue not to force things and try to just create a next play on every single play.” For Maye, that decisiveness ties back to instincts. “I think that goes back to playing instinctive and seeing it,” Maye said. “Trusting what I see in practice and trusting the decisions I’m making out there on the field. I’ve never been shied away from trusting something and letting it rip. So just knowing that and knowing what I’m seeing in front of the guys, and same time giving our guys a chance to make a play.” As the Patriots hope to avoid a 1-2 start again this year, Maye and his coach is stressing a fast start down in Jacksonville this Sunday. That means finding completions early and still stretching the defense when those opportunities provide themselves. And while some have become concerned in Maye’s ability to find that balance, his teammates are not part of that group. “I don’t know what they’re concerned about. Is he sick or something?,” wide receiver Mack Hollins said. “My faith in Drake ain’t changed. He’s a gunslinger.”

title: Patriots vs. Jaguars series history ahead of Week 3 game
summary: The New England Patriots are back on the road in Week 3, taking on the Jaguars in Jacksonville. The two teams have played in some memorable games over the years, but in total will meet for only the 16th time between the regular season and playoffs. Let’s take a look back at the first 15 […]
full_text: The New England Patriots are back on the road in Week 3, taking on the Jaguars in Jacksonville. The two teams have played in some memorable games over the years, but in total will meet for only the 16th time between the regular season and playoffs. Let’s take a look back at the first 15 of those games now. Patriots vs. Jaguars series history Overall history: The Jaguars entered the NFL in 1995, and as noted above have faced off against the Patriots on 15 occasions so far. Of those, five have come in the playoffs, including a pair of AFC Championship Games: the first in 1996 was won by the Patriots 20-6, as was the second, a 24-20 victory in 2017. New England also won a divisional game in 2007 (31-20) and a wild card game in 2005 (28-3). Jacksonville’s lone playoff victory came in the 1998 wild card round (25-10). In the regular season, the Patriots hold an 8-2 advantage. All three of their losses in the series so far have come in Jacksonville, where the teams are an even 3-3. First game: The Patriots hosted the Jaguars at Foxboro Stadium in Week 4 of the 1996 season. Three Adam Vinatieri field goals as well as touchdowns scored by Ben Coates and Curtis Martin allowed head coach Bill Parcells’ team to take a 22-0 lead in the first half, but the Jaguars fought back and scored on a Hail Mary just before halftime. Momentum shifted drastically from that point on, with the visitors erasing their deficit and nearly stealing a win. However, a Drew Bledsoe pick-six off a bobbled pass was called back by penalty and another Jaguars Hail Mary was caught inside the 1-yard line as time expired. In overtime, Bledsoe led his team down the field and the rookie Vinatieri kicked the game-winner from 40 yards out to secure a 28-25 win. | Highlights Most memorable game: Coming off a 35-point outing in the 2017 divisional round, the Patriots offense struggled against arguably the NFL’s best defense in the ensuing AFC title game. It did not help that Tom Brady had injured his hand in practice leading up to the game, nor that Rob Gronkowski exited in the first half with a concussion, but Jacksonville gave New England all sorts of fits early. Ultimately, however, a 20-10 lead was not enough for the visitors to punch their Super Bowl ticket. Brady and Danny Amendola took over in the fourth quarter, after all, combining for two touchdowns. The Jaguars’ last-gasp effort to come back ended with Stephon Gilmore making an acrobatic pass breakup on 4th-and-14. | Highlights Most recent game: Drake Maye’s second career start back in 2024 saw him take on the Jaguars at London’s Wembley Stadium. Even though the Patriots jumped to an early 10-0 lead, the game quickly went south for the team from that point on: Jacksonville joined 25 consecutive points between the second and third quarters, including a 96-yard punt return touchdown. A fourth quarter TD from Maye to K.J. Osborn did little to change the eventual outcome, and New England losing the game with a final score of 32-16. | Highlights The Patriots will take on the Jaguars at Jacksonville’s EverBank Stadium on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET. Both teams own identical 1-1 records entering the contest.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: What Dell Pettus, Jose Ramirez, Brenden Schooler moves mean for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots started the on-field preparation for their upcoming game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Wednesday, but before even taking the practice field were already busy. As head coach Mike Vrabel announced during a press conference leading up to the session, his team moved safety Dell Pettus to injured reserve and promoted outside […]
full_text: The New England Patriots started the on-field preparation for their upcoming game against the Jacksonville Jaguars on Wednesday, but before even taking the practice field were already busy. As head coach Mike Vrabel announced during a press conference leading up to the session, his team moved safety Dell Pettus to injured reserve and promoted outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 53-man roster. Later, core special teamer Brenden Schooler made his practice comeback after starting the season on the non-football injury list. Let’s assess what all of it means for the Patriots. Safety depth in the spotlight The Patriots lost two safeties to injury during Sunday’s win over the Steelers, with neither Pettus nor Craig Woodson finishing the game. Even though he did not practice on Wednesday due to his shoulder injury, Woodson remains on the active roster for now alongside Kevin Byard and Jaylen Reed. Pettus, on the other had, is now off to IR. The third-year man will miss at least the next four games as a result, meaning New England’s depth at the position will be tested in the near future — at least until Schooler’s theoretical activation from NFI. For the time being, however, the group looks like this: 53-man roster (3): Kevin Byard (31), Craig Woodson (4), Jaylen Reed (23) Practice squad (2): Mike Brown (33), Elliott Davison (27) NFI (1): Brenden Schooler (41) IR (1): Dell Pettus (24) Head coach Mike Vrabel already mentioned earlier this week that he would expect the Patriots’ practice squad safeties to play an increased role this week. It seems that that does not include moving up to the 53-man team at this point, though; both Mike Brown and Elliott Davison have their three standard elevations left, so New England could go this route to bolster their game day depth. Next man up Jaylen Reed Now on IR, Pettus will be out at least against the Jaguars, Bills, Raiders and Jets, with his earliest permissible return date to game action being Oct. 22 versus the Bears. Until then, late-August trade acquisition Jaylen Reed is projected to serve as New England’s third or possibly even second safety, depending on Craig Woodson’s outlook. “I think Jaylen has done a nice job,” said Mike Vrabel earlier this week. “He’s worked hard. He got put in there – we have to be ready to go. He had some plays that were good. He’s helped us in the kicking game. He would go in there at [punt protector], that’s not an easy thing to do. So, I’m glad that he was prepared and ready to go.” Injury response The Patriots could have opted to promote one of their practice squad safeties to their active roster, but they instead decided to move Jose Ramirez up. The move will prevent other teams from potentially poaching him, but more than that comes as a response to two edges — Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins — not being present at practice on Wednesday. Should one or both of Jones and Hutchins be unavailable against the Jaguars, the 27-year-old Ramirez would be one of just three edges on the active roster ready for the game. He would project as a rotational third option to complement Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas. “He has been a really good practice player for us,” said Mike Vrabel. “I think he has improved since the time he has been here. Multiple times being recognized by taking the reps that we talk about being on the show team and using those to his advantage. So, there will be an opportunity for him to be able to help us this week when we get down to the 48-man roster.” The role Vrabel hinted at might be less of a defensive one, but rather tied to the kicking game. In case Ponder and Jacas are indeed tasked with playing extended snaps on defense, the Patriots could opt to give neither of them any extended special teams snaps versus Jacksonville. Over the first two games, they played a respective 43% and 68% of snaps in the game’s third phase, and Ramirez might help lighten that workload. IR keeps growing After the Patriots moved starting right guard Mike Onwenu to injured reserve on Tuesday, we mentioned eight players being on the list. Now, it has grown to nine, not counting players since released with settlements. Injured reserve (9): RB Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending), WR A.J. Brown (1), WR Jeremiah Webb (29 | season-ending), TE Julian Hill (80 | season-ending), OT Marcus Bryant (52), RG Mike Onwenu (71), LB Khalil Jacobs (59), S Dell Pettus (25), P Bryce Baringer (17) If we were to include those aforementioned settlement players, who are no longer under contract with the team, New England’s injured reserve list would be 15 players deep just two weeks into the season. Window open Brenden Schooler returning to practice does not guarantee he will eventually make the jump from NFI to the active roster. However, it has at least opened a window that will remain open for 21 days. As for a theoretical return, it could therefore come as early as Week 5 against the Raiders. If so, the Patriots would quickly benefit from his presence: Schooler offers some theoretical depth at a safety position that has taken its hits, is one of the best special teamers in the NFL today, and is a respected team leader who was voted a captain in 2025.

Also not participating was defensive tackle DaQuan Jones, a late addition to the injury report. That was […]
full_text: The New England Patriots headed back to practice without four members of the active roster. Outside linebackers Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins as well as safety Craig Woodson all stayed sidelined during Wednesday’s work on the Jacksonville Jaguars. Also not participating was defensive tackle DaQuan Jones, a late addition to the injury report. That was the list of non-participants after guard Mike Onwenu and safety Dell Pettus both landed injured reserve in a span of 24 hours to begin the week. But there were also returns amid the attrition. Here’s the first and updated injury report ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff at EverBank Stadium. DID NOT PARTICIPATE Patriots DT DaQuan Jones (not injury related/personal) LB Dre’Mont Jones (shoulder) LB Quintayvious Hutchins (knee) S Craig Woodson (shoulder) Jaguars No players listed The edges and the secondary were hit last Sunday at Gillette Stadium. Jones exited in the second quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers due to a shoulder injury and was downgraded from questionable to out. Woodson, a fellow starter, also did not finish what became a 20-3 win due to a shoulder injury of his own. And Hutchins, the Boston College product selected with the No. 247 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft, recorded three tackles before a knee injury arose. LIMITED PARTICIPATION Patriots FB Reggie Gilliam (knee) TE Eli Raridon (thigh) OT Morgan Moses (foot) OT Dametrious Crownover (knee) S Brenden Schooler (back — NFI return) Jaguars RB LeQuint Allen Jr. (hip) WR Jakobi Meyers (thumb) OT Cole Van Lanen (knee) C Robert Hainsey (elbow, groin) DT DaVon Hamilton (back) Five Patriots checked in as limited participants on Wednesday, including Raridon. The rookie tight end out of Notre Dame played 11 offensive snaps and hauled in a 30-yard pass last Sunday before suffering a thigh injury. Elsewhere in Foxborough, Schooler saw his 21-day practice window open to begin the week. The 2025 special teams captain spent all of training camp on the non-football injury list and will not be eligible for activation until the initial four games of the regular season reach the rearview. FULL PARTICIPATION Patriots CB Carlton Davis III (neck) Jaguars CB Christian Braswell (knee) New England downgraded Davis to out on the eve of last weekend’s home opener. The veteran cornerback, who started all 17 games last season, carried a questionable designation into the 1 p.m. ET kickoff despite missing three consecutive practices due to a neck injury. He was back as a full participant on Wednesday.

(Photo by Bryan Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brenden Schooler is on schedule in Foxborough. The 2025 New England Patriots captain took part in Wednesday’s practice after sitting out the entirety of training camp . He had remained on the non-football injury list as the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline passed in August. But the 21-day window to return has now been opened in late September. And at the earliest date it could under new league rules. Players on the non-football injury list as well as physically unable to perform list are now eligible to resume practicing after the second week of the regular season. No roster activation can arrive until after the fourth week of the regular season, however, leaving a 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Gillette Stadium versus the Las Vegas Raiders circled in October. Patriots ST Brenden Schooler is back at practice today. He remains on the reserve/non-football injury list through Week 4. Sets the stage for him to potentially return when eligible in Week 5. pic.twitter.com/sgg6Ehu7UK — Brian Hines (@iambrianhines) September 23, 2026 Until then, road matchups against the Jacksonville Jaguars and Buffalo Bills will go on without No. 41, who was a limited participant in his first practice back from a back issue. Schooler, 29, has appeared in 66 games since arriving as part of the organization’s 2022 undrafted class. The 6-foot-2, 210-pound former transfer from Oregon to Texas began his tenure with PFWA All-Rookie honors in the kicking game and has since added Pro Bowl and first-team All-Pro selections. After signing three-year contract extension with the Patriots in 2024, Schooler was named a team captain for the first time last season under special teams coordinator Jeremy Springer. The core safety has seen 1,433 snaps on special teams to go with 93 snaps on defense in a situational role. His career spans 59 combined tackles, two sacks, four fumble recoveries as well as one blocked field goal and punt. Veteran outside linebacker Harold Landry III, a fellow 2025 captain, continues to reside on the PUP list for New England.

summary: The New England Patriots will be without Dell Pettus for a minimum of four games. Pettus, 25, suffered an ankle […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Dell Pettus #24 of the New England Patriots rushes the quarterback during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots will be without Dell Pettus for a minimum of four games. The organization sent the safety to injured reserve on Wednesday morning, as head coach Mike Vrabel announced during his press conference , and promoted outside linebacker Jose Ramirez to the 53-man roster in a corresponding move. Pettus, 25, suffered an ankle injury on special teams in the second quarter of last weekend’s 20-3 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. He was downgraded from questionable to out along with fellow safety Craig Woodson by the end of the home opener at Gillette Stadium. Signed as an undrafted free agent in 2024, Pettus made the initial active roster in Foxborough as a rookie and has appeared in all 36 games since then as well as Super Bowl LX. Making a pair of starts in the secondary, the 5-foot-11, 200-pound Troy alum stands with 471 snaps on defense and 579 snaps on special teams in his NFL career. He has notched 56 tackles, two sacks, one forced fumble and one first down as the personal punt protector. A September signing will take the open spot for New England. Ramirez, 27, joined the practice squad in the days following the league’s cutdown deadline and gets the call-up on the heels of recent Dre’Mont Jones and Quintayvious Hutchins ailments off the edges. Entering the NFL in the sixth round of the 2023 draft at No. 196 overall, the former MAC Defensive Player of the Year by way of Arizona, Riverside City College and Eastern Michigan has appeared in four career games. After setting out with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, with whom he saw 30 snaps on defense and 40 snaps on special teams, Ramirez spent last year with the CFL’s Hamilton Tiger-Cats before circling back to the NFL. The 6-foot-2, 252-pound outside linebacker signed a futures contract with the Philadelphia Eagles in January and was waived at the conclusion of training camp. “Been a really good practice player for us,” Vrabel said of promoting Ramirez. “I think he’s improved since the time he’s been here, multiple times being recognized. He’s taken the reps that we talk about being on the show team and using those to his advantage. So, whether they’ll be an opportunity, we’ll see, for him to be able to help us this week when we get down to the 48-man roster.” Bringing the group of 17 back to capacity, the Patriots announced the addition of outside linebacker Benton Whitley to the practice squad on Wednesday. Whitley, 27, entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with the Los Angeles Rams in 2022 and has appeared in six career games, notching one fumble recovery and one pass defensed. The 6-foot-3, 255-pound Massachusetts native and Holy Cross alum made stops with the Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, Arizona Cardinals as well as Tampa Bay through the 2025 campaign. He spent his most recent training camp with the Cleveland Browns before being waived at the end of August. The Jacksonville Jaguars host next Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff at EverBank Stadium.

full_text: Fresh off their first win of the year, the New England Patriots will travel to Florida in Week 3. The Jacksonville Jaguars, who, like the Patriots, are the owners of a 1-1 record two games in, are the next opponent on their regular season schedule. Let’s learn more about them. Jaguars key stats The Jaguars are the current leaders in the AFC South and their numbers through two games show that balance has been the key for them. Obviously, two games is too small a sample to draw any definitive conclusions, but the early trends are showing a team capable of putting pressure on its opponents on both offense and defense. It also has managed to limit turnovers: besides one Trevor Lawrence interception — albeit a costly one — the team has held onto the ball. The defense, meanwhile, has taken it away three times already. Speaking of the defense, it has performed well but not quite on the same level as the offense so far. Still, the unit very much should present a challenge for a Patriots team whose own offense has yet to find consistency this year. Jaguars 2026 season As noted above, Jacksonville is currently 1-1. The team started its season with a dominant win over the Browns, before falling to the Broncos is a defensive affair. Week 1: 34-10 win vs. Cleveland Browns (1-0) Week 2: 20-13 loss at Denver Broncos (1-1) The Jaguars’ story this year is somewhat similar to the Patriots’; they also could easily be 2-0 had they not squandered a 10-point lead. In Jacksonville’s case, that happened on Sunday in Denver with the aforementioned Trevor Lawrence INT a critical play in turning a 13-3 lead midway through the third quarter into a 20-13 defeat by the final whistle. His traditional stats also look the part: he has completed 35 of 52 pass attempts (67.3%) for 434 yards with four touchdowns and an interception; he also has been sacked three times in 56 dropbacks. Lawrence’s favorite target so far has been Parker Washington, who has seen 18 passes thrown his way. The fourth-year wide receiver has caught 12 of them for 181 yards and a touchdown, making him one of four Jaguars to haul in scoring passes this season. The others are tight end Brenton Strange, old friend Jakobi Meyers, and Josh Cameron, the team’s nominal WR4 behind Washington, Meyers and part-time perimeter starter Brian Thomas Jr. On the ground, Bhayshul Tuten has been the clear main man: he has carried the ball 28 times for 131 yards and a touchdown. The third-year man is quite accurate — 89.7% field goal rate in his career — but his standout trait is his range: he holds the NFL’s all-time record for the longest field goal, a 68-yarder last season. title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Jaguars ahead of Week 3
summary: Old friends will cross paths when the New England Patriots and Jacksonville Jaguars do so at EverBank Stadium. And not just offensive line coach Doug Marrone. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for Sunday have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL careers. Here’s a […]
full_text: Old friends will cross paths when the New England Patriots and Jacksonville Jaguars do so at EverBank Stadium. And not just offensive line coach Doug Marrone. Between the active rosters, practice squads and reserve lists, four players in the fold for Sunday have been members of both locker rooms during their NFL careers. Here’s a glance through the list of former Patriots and former Jaguars leading up to the 1 p.m. ET kickoff. JACKSONVILLE Jakobi Meyers, wide receiver — Entering the NFL as an undrafted rookie out of North Carolina State in 2019, Meyers tallied 235 receptions for 2,758 yards and eight touchdowns across 60 games and 39 starts with the Patriots. The ex-quarterback threw a pair of touchdowns, received the club’s Ed Block Courage Award, and led the offense in receiving yards in back-to-back-to-back seasons. He departed for the Las Vegas Raiders as an unrestricted free agent 2023 and was sent to the AFC South at the trade deadline last November in exchange for the No. 117 and No. 182 overall picks in the 2026 draft class. A three-year, $60 million extension followed for the eventual Jaguars team captain. Since leaving Foxborough, Meyers has caught 236 passes for 2,737 yards and 16 touchdowns across 49 games and 46 starts. The 29-year-old wideout has had a hand in additional three scores as a rusher and passer. Jahlani Tavai, linebacker — After five seasons, the Patriots released Tavai ahead of the new league year. The 29-year-old linebacker had been under contract through 2027 after signing an extension that carried a $16 million base value. First landing in Foxborough as a member of the practice squad in 2021 after being waived by the Detroit Lions, Tavai went on to appear in 76 games, starting 51. The University of Hawaii product logged 350 tackles and 3.5 sacks while intercepting three passes and forcing three fumbles. He saw 2,606 snaps on defense and 1,293 snaps on special teams and was named New England’s recipient Ed Block Courage Award on the way to Super Bowl LX. The No. 43 overall pick in the 2019 NFL draft agreed to terms with the Jaguars amid training camp in August and stands four tackles into his stay on the active roster. NEW ENGLAND Chandler Brayboy, wide receiver — The Patriots added Brayboy to the practice squad following a workout midway through September. The 25-year-old wide receiver made his first NFL stop in Jacksonville. Signed by the Jaguars as an undrafted free agent in 2025, Brayboy spent the duration of his rookie year on the practice squad. After being retained on a futures contract in January, he was waived at the cutdown deadline in August. A former FCS All-American, CAA Special Teams Player of the Year and Elon team captain, Brayboy’s collegiate career spanned 2,660 receiving yards, 245 rushing yards, 1,568 kickoff return yards and 22 all-purpose touchdowns over the course of 55 games dating back to 2019. Greg Van Roten, guard — The Patriots hosted Van Roten on a visit during the first week of August. And after attrition hit New England’s offensive line in the preseason opener, the 36-year-old free agent circled back on a one-year deal to shore up the interior depth. He took over at right guard last week after tenured starter Mike Onwenu was carted off due to a broken ankle. A veteran of 146 games, including 105 starts, Van Roten began his career as an undrafted rookie in 2012. The former All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn has since made stops with nine different NFL clubs. Count the Jaguars among the previous. Van Roten joined Jacksonville during the 2017 offseason on the heels of a CFL run with the Toronto Argonauts, yet was cut amid organized team activities that spring before playing a down. His career now stretches 6,938 offensive downs. Ironman campaigns arrived in 2024 and 2025.

title: A look back at the history between the Saints and Raiders
summary: The New Orleans Saints will finally play their first home game of the 2026 season Sunday when they welcome the Las Vegas Raiders to Caesars Superdome. The two teams first met on Nov. 7, 1971, at Tulane Stadium in New Orleans, where the Saints rallied from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit to end the game in […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - DECEMBER 29: Brock Bowers #89 of the Las Vegas Raiders carries the ball while being tackled by Tyrann Mathieu #32 of the New Orleans Saints during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome on December 29, 2024 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Sean Gardner/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New Orleans Saints will finally play their first home game of the 2026 season Sunday when they welcome the Las Vegas Raiders to Caesars Superdome. The two teams first met on Nov. 7, 1971, at Tulane Stadium in New Orleans, where the Saints rallied from a 14-point fourth-quarter deficit to end the game in a 21-21 tie. The Saints and Raiders have met 16 times in the regular season, with Las Vegas holding an 8-7-1 advantage in the all-time series. The two teams last met Dec. 29, 2024, when the Raiders defeated the Saints 25-10 in New Orleans’ final home game of the season. The Saints took a 7-3 lead in the second quarter when rookie quarterback Spencer Rattler connected with former Raiders tight end Foster Moreau on a 30-yard touchdown pass. However, Las Vegas regained the lead before halftime and shut out New Orleans in the second half to secure the victory. New Orleans returns to the Superdome with momentum after securing its first win of the season, a 24-17 victory over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2. Meanwhile, Las Vegas enters this matchup undefeated at 2-0 under first-year head coach and former Saints offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak. Kickoff is at 3:25 p.m. CT and the game will be broadcast on CBS with Chris Lewis (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (color analyst) and Amanda Balionis (sideline)

(Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images Power rankings already showed some positive movement after the New Orleans Saints’ Week 1 loss, but now that they beat the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2, the rankings could jump. NFL.com – 14 (+7) “The Saints are a sneaky-tough bunch. New Orleans’ defense managed to limit Baltimore’s powerful offense after getting punched in the mouth early on Sunday. Tyler Shough once again showcased his clutch gene, propelling a 21-3 run to close the game, with the second-year signal-caller taking a brutal hit at the goal line on his fourth-down sneak to score the game-winning touchdown. He’s tough as nails and fits perfectly as the face of the upstart Saints.“ Fox Sports – 15 (+4) “OK, I’m a believer. The Saints pushed the Lions to overtime, then beat the Baltimore Ravens on the road. That’s enough to declare them legitimate. I believe QB Tyler Shough is legit, too. I just wonder if this early success is sustainable over the course of the entire season.” Bleacher Report – 13 (+9) “The New Orleans Saints have started slowly in both games, but they know how to rally late. In Week 1, the Saints came up short in overtime, but they completed a comeback on the road against a heavily favored Baltimore Ravens squad in Week 2. Saints’ head coach Kellen Moore’s willingness to run a play on fourth down for the win or a lead shows how much he trusts his team. Despite a subpar ground game, quarterback Tyler Shough has led a solid passing attack that keeps his team in games. If you haven’t bought into the thought of the Saints being NFC South champions, maybe it’s time to consider it. — Moton ” CBS Sports – 18 (+5) “That was a nice comeback on the road in beating the Ravens. Tyler Shough is off to a really nice start. Sports Illustrated – 14 (+6) “The Kelvin Banks news is awful, but I’ll say this: New Orleans is the toughest team I’ve watched on film this year. Everyone is Kevin Costner-movie style gritty, especially Devaughn Vele and Chris Olave. They made some clutch, chain-moving catches in traffic against a good Ravens defense on Sunday to keep the comeback alive. Imagine what this offense looks like with a third star in Jordyn Tyson.”
