title: Is Pete Werner emerging as a key piece of Saints defense?
summary: New Orleans Saints linebacker Pete Werner entered the 2026 season with a bigger role potentially waiting for him. For the first time in his career, Werner is playing without Demario Davis beside him. After spending years alongside one of the most important leaders on the Saints’ defense, Werner now has an opportunity to establish himself […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 20: Mark Andrews #89 of the Baltimore Ravens is tackled by Pete Werner #20 of the New Orleans Saints during the first quarter of the game at M&T Bank Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images New Orleans Saints linebacker Pete Werner entered the 2026 season with a bigger role potentially waiting for him. For the first time in his career, Werner is playing without Demario Davis beside him. After spending years alongside one of the most important leaders on the Saints’ defense, Werner now has an opportunity to establish himself as one of the veteran leaders of the unit alongside Kaden Elliss. Through two games, he is making the most of that opportunity. Werner delivered an impressive performance in Sunday’s 24-17 win over the Baltimore Ravens, finishing with team-high 11 total tackles, including eight solo tackles. He also recorded a sack, three total pressures, a tackle for loss and a defensive stop. His impact as a pass rusher was particularly encouraging, as he earned a 79.6 pass-rush grade from Pro Football Focus. Werner’s performance came at an important time for New Orleans. The Saints trailed 14-3 at one point during the game, but the defense settled down and played a major role in helping complete the comeback. Baltimore managed just three points after halftime as New Orleans flipped the game. Werner was consistently around the football throughout the afternoon. Much like he was in the season opener agains the Detroit Lions. So far, he has shown that he is capable of taking on the increased responsibility. His ability to contribute against the run while also making an impact as a pass rusher gives New Orleans another versatile piece to build around. It is still early, but Werner is off to a strong start in his sixth season and looks to be drifting away from the inconsistency that plagued the early years of his career. The Saints may no longer have his mentor beside him, but Werner is showing that he is ready for breakout season.

title: If Saints win/lose vs. the Raiders
summary: The New Orleans Saints will finally host their home opener when the Las Vegas Raiders visit the Crescent City on Sunday. Here’s what either outcome could mean for the black and gold in Week 3. If the Saints win: A victory on Sunday would be huge for New Orleans and establish them as a team […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore looks on in the second half against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New Orleans Saints will finally host their home opener when the Las Vegas Raiders visit the Crescent City on Sunday. Here’s what either outcome could mean for the black and gold in Week 3. If the Saints win: A victory on Sunday would be huge for New Orleans and establish them as a team to be taken seriously in the playoff picture. Yes, it’s early. But the context is huge here. Both the Saints and the Raiders have gotten off to fast starts. Sunday’s matchup feels like a huge chance for either team to truly prove their worth after three weeks. The black and gold are betting favorites at home after last week’s resounding road victory in Baltimore. Another win here wouldn’t surprise many, but it would further amplify the excitement currently being felt around this team. If the Saints lose: On the flip side, a defeat against an up and coming Vegas squad wouldn’t spell disaster, but it would certainly dampen spirits in the wake of the Ravens win. With the Saints on home turf, a defeat would certainly be a little unexpected. It’s objectively the easiest game of the year so far, as reflected by the betting line. A loss would also put massive emphasis on the Week 4 divisional clash with Atlanta on Monday Night Football. If the Saints were 1-2 going in, that would become almost a must-win game early in the year. Regardless, it feels like the type of game where either outcome will result in a series of overreactions, for better or for worse. Do you think the Saints can take care of business in the Caesars Superdome? Let us know in the comments!

title: NY Giants news: Jaxson Dart surgery, Brian Burns expected to miss time, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as the Giants get set to battle the Tennessee Titans this Sunday. Vaccaro: Jaxson Dart’s Broadway tale staring down a cruel reality | New York Post Jaxson Dart was the one. He was the heir. In this 50th year since Broadway Joe Namath took his […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories as the Giants get set to battle the Tennessee Titans this Sunday. Vaccaro: Jaxson Dart’s Broadway tale staring down a cruel reality | New York Post Jaxson Dart was the one. He was the heir. In this 50th year since Broadway Joe Namath took his talents to Los Angeles for the final forgettable chapter of his career, New York has long sought the successor to the character Namath created and no one else had seen fit to copy: the big-city QB1 who liked the bright lights as much as the lights love him. Tiki: Giants have to consider all options at QB Tiki says the harsh reality is that Jaxson Dart's Giants future is now in question: pic.twitter.com/e8e9iD3HAA — WFAN Sports Radio (@WFAN660) September 23, 2026 Politi: Jaxson Dart’s injury will force Giants to make a crucial QB decision … again | NJ.com A franchise quarterback must prove he can stay on the field, and between this injury and his frequent trips to the blue medical tent as a rookie, there is no evidence that Dart can pass that test. No one is questioning the former Ole Miss passer’s toughness, and sure, Dart might prove to be a stable, 17-game starter with better luck (and decent blocking). The Giants’ braintrust can’t count on that, though, especially not when Dart hasn’t proven that he is the guy in his short career and not when this is a rare draft loaded with top-end quarterback talent. O’Connor: It’s a Dart disaster for Giants. Time for John Harbaugh to earn his $100 million | The Athletic That’s why the 2026 Giants season is already locked in a life-and-death struggle. As one of the best coaches of his generation, John Harbaugh was worth the $100 million investment the Giants made in him. He will earn all of that cash this year if he can somehow keep his team breathing. All Giants eyes on John Harbaugh now, and that’s the way it should be | The Record John Harbaugh raises the floor for an entire franchise and Jaxson Dart raises the ceiling. If you’re the New York Giants today, especially a fan base that has come to expect the worst for a decade-plus, you can’t help but feeling like the ceiling just caved in on the season and so much more. Willie Colon sees a path for the Giants "It's not over" 💪 — @willcolon66 on how the Giants should move forward without Jaxson Dart pic.twitter.com/vcSVOOCZxb — Good Morning Football (@gmfb) September 23, 2026 With Jaxson Dart Out For The Year, Giants Should Ride The Jameis Winston Wave | FOX Sports Which is why it’s Winston-or-bust for this star-crossed team in 2026. The Giants will say that’s not so bad. After all, they liked Winston enough to sign him to a two-year, $13 million contract extension just two weeks ago, making him one of the highest-paid backup QBs in the league. But their faith in him was mostly a short-term proposition. They saw him, according to a team source, as a solid veteran who was smart and talented enough to get them through a short stretch if Dart went down. Their faith gets shakier when it’s a long-term proposition they were hoping to avoid, especially since Winston last started more than seven games in a season seven years ago. With Jaxson Dart out, what’s next for Giants, Jameis Winston? | ESPN.com How does the offense adjust under Winston? It’s going to look different. Winston doesn’t have the same running ability as Dart. That much was obvious against the Rams when Winston rushed for 1 yard in three-plus quarters. That will hurt their traditional running game, too, since they designed an offense around Dart’s athletic skill set. The Jameis experience comes with fire quotes, plenty of chuckles and a wide range of play. It’s not uncommon to see a spectacular tight-window throw down the field followed by a pass that sails 15 yards over a receiver’s head. It will be on this veteran offensive coaching staff, led by coordinator Matt Nagy, to limit the latter. Don’t ask Winston to do too much. Rely on the physical running game to downplay his proclivity for mistakes and interceptions. Exploring quarterback options for Giants to add following Jaxson Dart’s season-ending injury | SNY.tv Among the names being mentioned include FA Jimmy Garoppolo, Bengals Josh Johnson, recently signed by the Jets Will Levis, Vikings J.J. McCarthy, and last year’s starter Russell Wilson. ESPN analysts: Giants should ‘kick the tires’ on this young QB | NJ.com “Joe Milton is a young quarterback that can run,” ESPN’s Jordan Rodgers, a former college QB, said Wednesday on Get Up. “Not that he’s a dynamic runner, but he can do what Dart did in the zone read. He did it in college. He’s a big, physical guy, he could push the ball downfield. I think you kick the tires on Joe Milton, see if he can be traded for a late-round draft pick just so the identity of your offense doesn’t have to completely change with Jameis Winston and you could maybe still compete.” 2026 NFL offensive line rankings | PFF 21. New York Giants (up 1). The Giants struggled more up front in Week 2 than Week 1, with left tackle Andrew Thomas the only starter to muster a PFF grade above 70.0. Rookie right guard Francis Mauigoa had flashes in the run game, receiving a positive grade on 14.3% of run-blocking snaps compared with a 9.5% negatively graded play rate, but he concluded with just an 84.2% PFF pass-block win rate. Resetting expectations for these six NFL teams with injured quarterbacks | CBSSports.com New expectations: Vie for another early draft pick. There is no sugar coating the Giants’ outlook without Dart. What had all the makings of a (finally) exciting year is already down the tubes. That history suggests that so long as Winston is the man under center, New York will stand among the worst teams in the NFL. The silver lining is that the Giants should be able to add more premium young talent to their enticing core in the 2027 draft, but this was supposed to be a season in which that group elevated them out of the early draft pick range and into playoff contention. title: Jaxson Dart injury changes the story of 2026, and perhaps beyond, for the Giants
summary: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The crushing news that quarterback Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the season after sustaining a knee injury Monday night is now official. The impact on the New York Giants will be far-reaching, and for now, we can only speculate about what the future holds. Head coach John Harbaugh, whose […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart | Getty Images EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. — The crushing news that quarterback Jaxson Dart will miss the rest of the season after sustaining a knee injury Monday night is now official . The impact on the New York Giants will be far-reaching, and for now, we can only speculate about what the future holds. Head coach John Harbaugh, whose 64th birthday present turned out to be picking up the pieces after the loss of his talented young starting quarterback, had a message for both Dart and his team with 15 games left in the season. “There’s purpose in this,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll all know what it is at some point in time, but it’s okay to feel bad right now. The sun is going to come up in the morning. The world is going to keep spinning. “He’s [Dart] good. He’s a mature guy. He’s a great guy. He worked so hard, so hard to get to this point and be ready. He was playing at such a high level. It breaks your heart in that sense. If you didn’t feel that way, or you didn’t acknowledge that, you’d be lying. We all feel that way. Yet and still, life goes on. The world keeps spinning.“ As for those 15 remaining games? Don’t tell Harbaugh the season is lost. “We’ve got a challenge in front of us that we’ve got to go take care of,” Harbaugh said. “There’s going to be a story written. There’s a purpose in this whole thing. We’ve got to find what it is. That’s our job. “Go out there and play the best football game we can play this week. Do we have the team this week to go play great football this week? Absolutely we do. That’s what we’re focused on.” The story of the season is certainly not going to be the one anyone expected. Or hoped for. How will it turn out? We’ll see. The future is on hold This was supposed to be the year that things changed for the Giants. To bring him to New York, the organization put a full-court press on Harbaugh, a coach with a Super Bowl title and 194 career victories, the 13th most of all time. With 15 winning seasons and 12 playoff berths in 18 seasons as a head coach, Harbaugh was — and is — supposed to change the trajectory of a franchise that has been heading in the wrong direction. In Dart, they had the quarterback they figured they could build around and go forward with for the foreseeable future. Realistically, 2026 was not expected to produce a team that would win 12 or 13 games and make a run to the NFC Championship Game or beyond. It was, though, supposed to make clear that the three- and four-win seasons that have become too commonplace in the Meadowlands were a thing of the past. Now? That bright future is on hold. A miserable season is certainly a possibility. There is an interesting, perhaps appropriate, parallel between the situation the Giants football team now finds itself in and the massive construction project currently ongoing at the Giants’ 1925 Giants Drive headquarters. The facility is undergoing a massive expansion/renovation project. There is construction everywhere. Players have been relocated to temporary locker room quarters in a group of trailers in what was formerly the media parking lot. The player parking lot is gone, as that space will be used for a building expansion that will eventually connect with the team’s indoor practice facility. There are bulldozers, backhoes, and the constant pounding of construction as pieces of the facility are torn apart while other new pieces are just in the formative stages. The project is not scheduled for completion until before the 2028 season. The result is expected to be a beautiful, updated facility with expanded locker rooms, added office space, a new weight room, expanded rehab and sports medicine space, and more. For now, though, the place is a mess, and everyone is both inconvenienced and doing the best they can to deal with the disruption. It feels like the football team itself is now in a similar state of construction, with tatters pieces all around, and that perhaps the timeline for when the Giants become what they hope Harbaugh can make them has been similarly prolonged. The Giants are in survival mode The mess that the Giants are currently in is certainly a heckuva birthday present for Harbaugh. “There’s a reason why he’s Coach John Harbaugh, right,” safety Jevon Holland said after Wednesday’s light practice. “There’s a reason why he has the pedigree that he does. Because he’s a great coach, to be honest. And I think where he’s best at is in these situations.” Harbaugh is going to have to be. As of today, the Giants really aren’t building for the future or trying to be one of the feel-good stories of the 2026 NFL season. They are trying to survive. They are trying, simply, not to have this season turn into a train wreck. Can Harbaugh guide this team, this organization, that has become so used to failure, and keep it on the track? The Giants have games coming up the next three weeks against the Tennessee Titans and Arizona Cardinals at home, and the likely Jayden Daniels-less Washington Commanders on the road. All are winnable, and could largely tell the story of how well or poorly this season will turn out. They will turn to Jameis Winston as their quarterback for the foreseeable future. They signed Winston to a two-year, $13 million contract extension just a couple of weeks ago, so the idea that they would already be looking for a better option seems ludicrous. As does the idea that teams would be willing to trade a good backup quarterback right now, considering how many starters — and backups — have gone down in the season’s first two weeks. “The team loves Jameis. We voted him captain, so I think that says plenty.” Holland said. “Jameis is going to do a phenomenal job when he steps in there. He’s been leading us in multiple ways already, so it’s not uncommon. It’s not like a new voice or anything like that, so I think it will fit swimmingly.” Bouncing back from a ‘gut punch’ Players referred to losing Dart on the first offensive series Monday as a “gut punch.” It was clear that the loss of the quarterback affected them. Now, though, they have a job to do. The Giants met as a team Wednesday before they began practicing for Sunday’s game against the Titans. Harbaugh said it was a “big” meeting. “A lot of water went under the bridge in the last 30 hours, something like that. We just had to talk about it,” Harbaugh said. “The season’s not over, but it is for him [Dart]. We kind of talked about that, too. That was part of it. That was part of the deal. There’s a certain mourning that takes place. We had the same thing for Calvin [Austin]. You realize how hard it is for the player, really. It’s tough on the team. It’s tough on all of us. “As we said, you wake up, and you feel like it’s the end of the world. Then you wake up, and the world’s not done. The world keeps spinning. The games keep getting played. Nobody feels sorry for you. It’s time to go play the next game. Sunday at 1 o’clock, the ball’s going to get kicked off. We’re going to have to be the best football team we can be. “That’s the thing. It’s not a one-man game. It’s not like tennis. We don’t forfeit. We’re going to have our team out there. The Giants are going to roll out into that field out there and play the football game. We need to be the best Giants we can be.” Fans may believe the season is over, and it is certainly fair to believe the Giants won’t be the team they could have been — or that the upward trajectory of the franchise has now been detoured. “It doesn’t matter what anybody else thinks,” Holland said. “It’s about showing each other and not even showing each other, just continuing to do what we’ve always done, which was always put in extremely hard work. You know, we work to a point where it’s almost mind-boggling if the success isn’t there. “You understand what I’m saying? That’s how much work we have put in, and we’re going to continue to put in. So from my perspective, I personally don’t give a f—- what anybody else has to say outside of the building. Whether they think…

full_text: Brian Burns is helped off the field Monday night vs. the Rams. | Getty Images The New York Giants will be without quarterback Jaxson Dart for the remainder of the season. They could be without some other front-line players on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans, as well. Edge defender Brian Burns , who suffered a low ankle sprain Monday against the Los Angeles Rams, was not seen on the field Wednesday during the brief walk-through period open to media. Per ESPN NFL insider Adam Schefter , Burns “is not expected to need surgery but is likely to miss some time.” Without Burns, who had 16.5 sacks in 2025, Kayvon Thibodeaux will play an increased role. Left tackle Andrew Thomas , who reportedly has a groin/adductor injury, participated in the early portion of practice. Wide receiver Malik Nabers , who played through a shoulder injury on Monday, also participated in the walk-through portion open to media. Cornerback Deonte Banks , who missed Monday’s game with a calf injury, continued to work on the side with a member of the training staff. The Giants have not as of yet added another quarterback to replace Dart. Jameis Winston and Jake Haener were the only quarterbacks at practice on Wednesday. title: Jaxson Dart expected to have season-ending surgery, 6-month recovery
summary: New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to have season-ending surgery, per a report from Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Rapoport reports that Dart’s ACL is intact and he is expected to make a full recovery, however his season is over. He adds that Dart has been seeking second opinions on his injury, […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart leaves the field after being injured. | Getty Images New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart is expected to have season-ending surgery, per a report from Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network. Rapoport reports that Dart’s ACL is intact and he is expected to make a full recovery, however his season is over. He adds that Dart has been seeking second opinions on his injury, however it seems as though surgery is his best path forward. Rapoport later reported on air that Dart suffered a torn meniscus and torn MCL, which the surgery will address. He adds that the Dart faces a six-month recovery time from the surgery, which would likely allow him to take part in the Giants’ full 2027 off-season program. Rapoport also adds that the Giants are exploring all options with respect to the quarterback position going forward, but doesn’t expect a splashy move. ESPN’s Adam Schefter is reporting that while Dart’s ACL is fine, he suffered damage to his MCL, PCL, and meniscus. The primary issue, per Schefter’s report, is the damage to Dart’s meniscus. The meniscus is a rubbery piece of cartilage in the knee that acts as a cushion and shock absorber in the joint. A torn meniscus may be treated through rest and rehab, however more severe injuries need surgery. That said, it’s reassuring that Dart’s prognosis is good despite the need for surgery, as the Giants still expect Dart to be their long-term answer at quarterback. Having clarity on Dart’s prognosis and timeline allows the Giants to come to grips with the fact that they’ll be without their starting quarterback until 2027. Now they’ll need to rally around Jameis Winston and adapt to his skill set.

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 3
summary: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (2nd) 📈 1 spot Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills demolished the Lions on a short week after defeating the Houston Texans on the road. The Bills have the highest offensive EPA/play and the highest dropback EPA. Allen dropped five touchdowns in the first game at Highmark Stadium, and James […]
full_text: Aw Shough! | Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (2nd) 📈 1 spot Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills demolished the Lions on a short week after defeating the Houston Texans on the road. The Bills have the highest offensive EPA/play and the highest dropback EPA. Allen dropped five touchdowns in the first game at Highmark Stadium, and James Cook III rushed for 135 yards on 21 carries ( 6.4 YPC ). I had them ranked second last week, and that was too low. No. 2 — Seattle Seahawks (3rd) 📈 1 spot The Drew Lock-led Seahawks handled their business in the Arizona desert. Lock went 19 of 26 for 235 yards with three touchdowns, as Mike Macdonald’s defense held Jacoby Brissett to 95 yards passing on 28 attempts, and star rookie Jeremiyah Love to just 29 yards on nine carries. Seattle is a force, and they’re winning with a conservative offense and a stout defense, and a whole lot of Jaxon Smith-Njigba, who secured nine catches for 155 yards with three touchdowns on eleven targets. No. 3 — Los Angeles Rams (4th) 📈 1 spot The Rams offense dropped 481 total yards on the Giants and looked like the Super Team that everyone was discussing during the preseason. The injury to Jaxson Dart may have assisted the Rams’ offensive explosion, but Los Angeles was without star receiver Puka Nacua, and they did WHATEVER they wanted against the Giants’ defense. The Rams are back in the top-three! No. 4 — Cincinnati Bengals (5th) 📈1 spot The Bengals went into a hostile environment and defeated a now 0-2 Texans team that does possess a very talented defense. Speaking of talented defenses, the trade for Dexter Lawrence is paying dividends for Cincinnati. He is PFF’s highest-graded interior defensive lineman, and he had a massive fourth-down STOP in the Bengals 20-6 victory in Houston. Also, Ja’Marr Chase may have already had the catch of the season on his 32-yard touchdown grab; he had a pair of touchdowns with his seven catches for 75 yards. No. 5 — San Francisco 49ers (8) 📈 3 spots The 49ers played the Dolphins in Week 2 and cruised to an easy 35-13 home win after defeating the Los Angeles Rams in Australia earlier. Brock Purdy has completed over 80% of his passes for just under 500 yards through two games. The NFC West is STOUT with three teams in the top-five – the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. No. 6 — Kansas City Chiefs (7th) 📈 1 spot The Chiefs narrowly escaped the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday Night Football with a 33-30 overtime victory. Pat Mahomes threw for 371 yards, and the Chiefs’ offense rushed for more than 150 yards, but the Colts battled Steve Spagnuolo’s defense well. Kansas City earned the win, but the game was hard-fought. No. 7 — New England Patriots (11th) 📈 4 spots The Patriots got back on track by beating the Pittsburgh Steelers, 20-3. The Steelers could not do much offensively and New England gained 387 total offensive yards in Drake Maye’s first win of the 2026 season. No. 8 — Baltimore Ravens (1st ) 📉 7 spots The Ravens took a commanding 17-3 lead, but Saints quarterback Tyler Shough, with help from Chris Olave, led a dramatic come-from-behind win, 24-17. Despite averaging 4.9 yards per carry, the Ravens could not defeat the feisty Saints. No. 9 — Philadelphia Eagles (12th) 📈 3 spots The Eagles were almost upset by the Tennessee Titans, but a touchdown pass with nine seconds left in the game from Jalen Hurts gave Philadelphia the 24-20 victory. Hurts did throw a bad interception to Amani Hooker that ended a 15-play drive, and Cam Ward and the Titans scored on the next play; to Philadelphia’s credit, they scored two consecutive touchdowns on their next two possessions. Hurts was far from perfect, but the Eagles remain undefeated. No. 10 — Denver Broncos (14th) 📈 4 spots Denver defeated the Jaguars, 20-13, and Bo Nix threw for 288 yards in the Broncos’ first victory of the season. Jacksonville shut down the rushing attack, but the Broncos’ defense was able to slow down Liam Coen’s high-powered offense. No. 11 — Minnesota Vikings (15th) 📈 4 spots The Vikings defeated the Chicago Bears, 9-3, and now have two divisional wins without Kyler Murray, who is cleared to play in Week 3 against the Buccaneers, who have struggled mightily through their 0-2 start. No. 12 — Chicago Bears (6th) 📉 6 spots The Bears lost their quarterback for the game — luckily it’s not as serious as originally expected — and they played through a low-scoring monsoon, against one of the best defensive coorindators in football ( Brian Flores ). The 9-3 loss is tough, but I expect the Bears offense to bounce back once Caleb is healthy, which seems like it could be as early as a few weeks. No. 13 — Jacksonville Jaguars (9th) 📉 2 spots Jacksonville lost 20-13, and their offense was stifled for much of the game. They had just 268 total yards against Denver’s defense, which looked like the Denver defense under Vance Joseph from last season. Despite the loss, the Jaguars still remain in the top-12, but are tested next week as they host the Patriots. No. 14 — Dallas Cowboys (17th) 📈 3 spots The Cowboys defeated Washington, 37-20, as Dak Prescott tossed four touchdowns against the revamped Washington defense. CeeDee Lamb went for eight catches and 153 yards with two touchdowns, and George Pickens caught six passes for 40 yards. The Cowboys struggled to run the football, but they earned the victory. No. 15 — Detroit Lions (13th) 📉 2 spots The Lions were outclassed by the Buffalo Bills in Week 2, but Josh Allen can do that to a team — especially when he is opening a stadium on Thursday Night Football. The Lions could not do much early against the Bills’ defense, but they scored points in the second half, which made the game look more competitive. The Saints win looks better after their Week 2 upset over Baltimore. No. 16 — New Orleans Saints (22nd) 📈 6 spots The Saints pulled off the epic upset against the Baltimore Ravens. Tyler Shough willed his team to victory, and they’re now in the top half of these rankings. No. 17 — Houston Texans (10th) 📉 7 spots The Texans offense struggled against Dexter Lawrence and the Bengals’ revamped defense. They only scored six points, with the Bengals escaping Houston with a 20-6 victory. Houston started with two home games against quality opponents, and are now 0-2. No. 18 — Green Bay Packers (18th) SAME The Packers escaped MetLife Stadium with a win after some questionable coaching decisions by the New York Jets. It was a defensive struggle, and the Packers were inept on third down; they finished 1-9, but a few big defensive plays allowed them to escape without a catastrophic start to their season. N0. 19 — Carolina Panthers (27th) 📈 8 spots The Falcons did not stand a chance against the Panthers, who beat them badly 34-4. Cooper Rush started for the Falcons again and the Panthers’ defense is still turning the football over. No. 20 — Indianapolis Colts (21st) 📈 1 spot The Colts lost 33-30 in overtime against the Kansas City Chiefs in Kansas City. The injury to Alec Pierce is very unfortunate for the Colts’ offense, but Indianapolis almost pulled off the upset. No. 21 — New York Giants (16th) 📉 5 spots Injuries to Jaxson Dart and Brian Burns dictate where the Giants fall on this list. Still, the 28-6 beatdown against the Rams, where Jameis Winston looked lost and Matt Stafford found plenty of answers, is tough to forget. The Giants were beaten in just about every phase by Sean McVay, but I do think that’s the worst we will see Winston. No. 22 — Pittsburgh Steelers (20th) 📉 2 spots The Steelers offense has been bad for two straight weeks No. 23 — New York Jets (25th) 📈 2 spots The Jets have moved three spots each week. title: Rookie Report: A shaky second game for the NY Giants’ 2026 draft class
summary: The New York Giants had a nightmare of an evening against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2 on Monday Night Football. Just about everything that could go wrong for the Giants, did go wrong. The headline is obviously the knee injury suffered by quarterback Jaxson Dart, but that wasn’t the only storyline from the […]
full_text: New York Giants wide receiver Malachi Fields on the field against the Los Angeles Rams. | Getty Images The New York Giants had a nightmare of an evening against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 2 on Monday Night Football. Just about everything that could go wrong for the Giants, did go wrong. The headline is obviously the knee injury suffered by quarterback Jaxson Dart, but that wasn’t the only storyline from the night. The Giants’ had six rookies playing major roles for them against the Rams, and how the Giants’ 2026 class develops will be one of the most important things to watch as the rest of the season unfolds. The Giants are relying heavily on their young players, and their rookies, this year. In fact, the Giants had the third-most snaps played by rookies of any team in the NFL in Week 2, and perhaps it also isn’t a coincidence that the Los Angeles Rams had the fewest snaps played by rookies. Rookie Snap Count % through Week 2 1. MIA 27.6% 2. CLE 16.4% 3. NYG 15.1% … 30. ARI 2.3% 31. DEN 1.1% 32. LAR 0.7% pic.twitter.com/dA2rPZ8FZV — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 22, 2026 That the Giants are asking so much of their rookies makes the team more prone to mistakes while the players develop. However, it does give them valuable experience to aid in their development. Let’s take a closer look and see how they did in their second game of NFL action. Arvell Reese (LB) ( 59 snaps, 95% ) The Giants’ first pick played almost every snap against the Rams, as well as contributing on special teams. We saw every facet of Reese’s skill set employed by Dennard Wilson against the Rams. Reese played the run, played in coverage as a linebacker, was walked up to the line of scrimmage to show pressure on simulated blitzes, and was asked to rush off the edge. Of those, Reese looked most comfortable playing downhill. He appeared largely disciplined in his run fits and is remarkably strong for a 241-pound linebacker. He is able to take on and stalemate offensive linemen when he engages with good leverage. He also showed off his power with an impressive bull rush off the edge to drive left tackle Alaric Jackson back into the pocket, and he might have been able to disrupt had Blake Corum not delivered a timely chip block. Reese looks less comfortable dropping into space and playing coverage. He typically processes quickly, but doesn’t quite play with a natural feel for coverage. Reese can be a step late to pick up players as they enter his zones, and shows some indecision as well. That said, his speed is absolutely an asset and he simply flies to the ball once he commits. Sisi Mauigoa (RG) ( 58 snaps, 100% ) We saw both the highs and lows of Mauigoa’s game in his play against the Rams. On the plus side, Mauigoa’s power and agility were on full display. At his best, he showed some of what he did against the Cowboys’ interior defensive linemen. Mauigoa was able to displace the Rams’ linemen laterally on zone blocks, vertically when blocking downhill, and move laterally to mirror pass rushers. He has great range as a pulling guard, and was a load for any defender not prepared to block him. On other plays, however, Mauigoa struggled mightily. In particular, he had a tough time with Aaron Donald in his first game back. Sisi struggled to deal with Donald’s technique, leverage, and explosive first step — Donald’s 0.75-second get-off was the third-fastest by a defensive tackle so far this season. There were times when Mauigoa was pushed backward despite the considerable size disparity, as well as times when he struggled to deal with Donald’s speed rushes. The arrow is still pointing up for Mauigoa and his good plays were impressive, but this game definitely made him look like a rookie. Colton Hood (CB) ( 62 snaps, 100% ) Hood got the start in place of the injured Deonte Banks, and it was a long night for the rookie. He played every one of the defensive snaps and was a factor in both run defense and pass coverage. Hood wasn’t always a positive factor, but he did flash the traits that made many consider him a fringe first-round talent. Hood is a tough, physical corner who started the game with a great tackle to limit Kyren Lacy to a 2-yard gain on the Rams’ second play. He doesn’t hesitate to take on bigger blockers or to get his hands dirty. He also has quick feet and fluid hips as a cover corner and flashes the ability to stick in receivers’ hip pockets as a man cover corner. Hood is still a work in progress in off coverages. He has a tendency to overreact to savvy route runners, biting on double-moves or stumbling after a fake. At best that can make him a bit slow to react and at worst he can give up separation that can lead to big plays. Hood flashes the ability to be a good cover cornerback, but isn’t there yet. The upside to playing so many snaps is that he got valuable experience against a great offense. Malachi Fields (WR) ( 47 snaps, 81% ) Fields had an inconsistent day against the Rams, which is to be expected from a rookie. He flashed the upside of what the Giants hope he can be with the diving 14-yard catch from Dart on 1st and 10 early in the first quarter. That play showed off the body control, concentration, and ball skills that the Giants hope will make Fields a weapon on third downs and in the red zone. He generally seemed to run his routes well enough, and did a good job of using his frame to try to create traffic on clear-outs or create natural rubs. The Giants continued to use Fields in condensed formations, frequently starting with him as a slot before motioning a player around him, condensing the offensive formation and leaving Fields him as an outside receiver. That said, Fields also struggled with the Rams’ physical coverage. His size and strength are assets in that regard, however his technique isn’t there yet. Considering he doesn’t have the quick-twitch athleticism to cut with exceptional suddenness, it can be difficult for Fields to generate separation against tight coverage. The Giants can work around that going forward while Fields works on improving his technique to get off physical coverage. The Giants also frequently made use of Fields as a blocker in the run game. He became their primary receiver in 22 or 13-personnel sets after Malik Nabers suffered his shoulder injury, and comported himself well enough. Those were primarily running plays, and Fields is a problem for perimeter defenders as a blocker. There were times where the Giants also used Fields as a pulling tight end or asked him to insert in the box as an extra blocker. He was, predictably, less of an impact player in those situations. However, he was able to lose slowly enough to do his job. Dominic Zvada (PK) and Ben Mann (LS) ( 13 snaps combined ) No slight to specialists, but I think it’s appropriate to lump these two together, as much of the time they’re working as a unit. Fittingly, we’ll start with the long snapper, and Mann was largely solid. His snaps appeared crisp and accurate, arriving on time and well placed for Jordan Stout as a punter and holder for Zvada. Mann did give a fair amount of ground when blocking for Stout on punts, but held up well on both of Zvada’s field goals despite facing the Rams’ starting defensive linemen. For his part, Zvada largely remains a weapon on kickoffs. He had one touchback, but otherwise did a good job of dropping his kicks around the 5-yard line to force a return. Unfortunately, Zvada was the Giants’ lone source of points against the Rams, but we did get to see his strong leg in action. His 52-yard field goal was not only accurate, but appeared as though it would have been good from 62 yards.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Jaxson Dart injury is ‘not an ACL’, but the timeline still isn’t good: Report
summary: There hasn’t been much in the way of good regarding the injury to New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart. At first it was believed that Dart only suffered an MCL strain when he was sandwiched between a pair of Los Angeles Rams defenders and could return inside of a month. It was then revealed Tuesday […]
full_text: ﻿New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart | Getty Images There hasn’t been much in the way of good regarding the injury to New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart. At first it was believed that Dart only suffered an MCL strain when he was sandwiched between a pair of Los Angeles Rams defenders and could return inside of a month. It was then revealed Tuesday morning that an MRI revealed that his injury is worse than initially believed. The reporting hasn’t revealed the exact nature of the injury, but that Dart would be out indefinitely and season-ending surgery is on the table. That catches us up to Wednesday morning, when Mike Garafolo reported that Dart’s injury doesn’t involve his ACL. Garafolo said: “Ian Rapoport and I were both told yesterday, this is not an ACL. But, the MRI did tell a different story from what the Giants were initially expecting. There is more damage than what the evaluations on site showed.“ The Giants’ hesitancy to confirm the nature of the injury makes sense in the light of Garafolo and Rapoport’s reporting. ACL injuries are usually quickly confirmed and the recovery timelines are well understood. A different or complicated injury could be good news, worse news, or just bad news depending on what the continuing tests and opinions show. Garafolo added that Dart’s recovery could follow several different timelines depending on the exact nature of the injury. None of the potential timelines are “very good”, according to Garafolo, and Dart’s season being over remains on the table. “There are a lot of people involved. That means inside doctors [inside the Giants organization], outside doctors, that means Dart, the Giants. Everybody is going to come together and make a collective decision.” Dart, obviously, will lobby to take the quickest route back to the field. Dart is an incredibly competitive young man and even played through a high ankle sprain his final season at Ole Miss. However, that might not be best for his long term health. Garafolo says, “A lot of times when you have a young player, particularly at the quarterback position, these decisions are made with the long term interest of the player in mind.” The Giants had to take Dart’s uniform away from him after he tried to talk his way back onto the field Monday night. With that in mind, the Giants may need to protect Dart from himself as much as deal with his injury. Garafolo ends by saying that we should expect clarity on Dart’s status and timeline in the coming days. We’ll update with more as we get it.
author: Chris Pflum

title: NY Giants-Tennessee Titans storylines: Moving on without Jaxson Dart
summary: Jaxson Dart is likely not going to be under center for any of them, but the New York Giants still have 15 games to play in the 2026 NFL season. How will they do without their young quarterback, who played like a star in an impressive Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys? We begin […]
full_text: Jaxson Dart throwing the ball Monday right before being injured. | Getty Images Jaxson Dart is likely not going to be under center for any of them, but the New York Giants still have 15 games to play in the 2026 NFL season. How will they do without their young quarterback, who played like a star in an impressive Week 1 victory over the Dallas Cowboys? We begin to find out Sunday at MetLife Stadium when the Tennessee Dabolls — er, Titans — come to East Rutherford, N.J. for a 1 p.m. matchup. Below are some of the storylines for the week. Winning without Dart The latest reporting from NFL Network insider Mike Garafolo is that “ there are a few timelines on the table , none of them very good, one of them season-ending” for the Giants quarterback. While we await word on that, it is obvious Dart will not play Sunday against Tennessee. And the Giants will be without him for the foreseeable future. How will the Giants fare without Dart, especially if he is out all season? It is possible that John Harbaugh and his veteran coaching staff squeeze every ounce of juice from this imperfect Giants’ roster and they finish in the neighborhood of .500. It is also possible that a four- or five-win season, the kind of disastrous year the Giants figured was off the table due to Harbaugh’s presence, is back on the table. Beginning with the 0-2 Titans, the Giants have a three-game stretch of games that should be winnable. Tennessee is a young, winless team coming to MetLife Stadium. They did, though, put a Week 2 scare into the Philadelphia Eagles. The 1-1 Arizona Cardinals come to MetLife in Week 4. They are expected to be one of the league’s weaker teams. The Giants visit the 0-2 Washington Commanders in Week 5. The Commanders could be without star quarterback Jayden Daniels, who suffered his second dislocated left elbow in as many seasons on Sunday against the Dallas Cowboys. If the Giants cannot win at least two of those three games, another long, miserable, losing season could follow. Harbaugh, one of the winningest head coaches of all time, is going to be challenged over the next 15 games. The veteran head coach promised on Tuesday that the Giants will “be fighting every step of the way.” “We haven’t even come close – not even close — to playing as well as we’re capable of playing as a football team,” Harbaugh said. “So, that’s really going to be the focus. I mean, it’s going to be something we’re going to have to, you deal with all the different challenges that you face and all the different adversity that you face, for sure. And even the prosperity, you learned that last week, you faced some of the prosperity, and prosperity sometimes can be more dangerous than adversity. “All these challenges to put your best effort out there, play your best football, so you can win a football game. And we’re going to do that. These guys are going to do that. That’s what you get excited about. The prospect of our team playing the best football that they can play. And that’s what we’re working on, working as hard as we can, working like crazy as a football team to do that all together.” The Giants referred to Dart’s injury as an in-game “gut punch.” Harbaugh does not expect that to cause a long-term letdown. “The guys want to go win. They want to go play,” Harbaugh said. “Guys play. They’ll play. They play for each other. They play for themselves. They play for their families. They play because they believe they can win the game. And it’s never one person, never one person that wins or loses a football game. It’s everybody. And the more good players you can have out there, the better chance you’re going to have. There’s no doubt about it. But you still have to be a complete team to win games. “If you get punched in the gut, are you going down? Are you going down? Are you going to crumple to the ground, as Jack Harbaugh would say, like a sack of sour apples and just fall to the ground and just rot away and wither away into the dust. Is that what you’re going to do?” To win games, the Giants are going to have to accomplish several things: They will have to get better play from quarterback Jameis Winston than the miserable 11 of 27 for 11 yards and an interception performance he gave them Monday night. They will have to find some way to get explosive plays from their offense. The longest non-Dart run they have in two games is a 13-yard carry by Cam Skattebo. They have one pass completion of more than 20 yards, a 33-yard grab by Darnell Mooney. The pass rush will have to remember that the regular season has started. They will need to find a way to cover some of the league’s best receivers. They need to hope that injuries to stars Brian Burns, Andrew Thomas, and Malik Nabers aren’t severe. Oh, and that other injuries don’t continue to pile up. We begin to find out how life after Dart will go Sunday against Tennessee. More injuries to worry about Dart suffered the worst and most significant injury on Monday night. Still, the game against the Rams saw several other significant injuries to Giants stars. Edge defender Brian Burns, who had a career-high 16.5 sacks last season, suffered a sprained left ankle. Left tackle Andrew Thomas apparently suffered a groin injury on the Giants’ final offensive possession. Wide receiver Malik Nabers left the game briefly with a shoulder injury. He had just one catch for 1 yard in the game. Cornerback Deonte Banks missed Monday’s game with a calf injury. His status for Week 3 is unclear. The initial injury report of the week comes out Wednesday afternoon. We find out more about the severity of these injuries then. With a short week before playing the Titans, it is fair to wonder just how short-handed the Giants are going to be in a game that not long ago looked like one the Giants should win. Remember the Titans This game has been circled on the calendar for a while simply because of the volume of former Giants — especially key Giants — who are now part of the Titans’ organization. Daboll, fired last season as Giants head coach, is now running the Tennessee offense. Daboll, of course, was instrumental in the Giants’ decision to trade up last season to draft Dart. Robinson is second on the Titans with six receptions for 47 yards, just 7.8 yards per catch. He had the only 1,000-yard season of his career with the Giants last season. Bellinger has just one catch in two games, one of which he started. Schlottmann has started both Tennessee games at center. Through two games, Schlottmann’s Pro Football and Sports Network ‘Impact Score’ is 72.6. For the Giants, starting center John Michael Schmitz is at 73.6. Both scores are slightly below what PFSN considers league average, a score of 75.0. Where’s the pass rush? The Giants’ defense was supposed to be built around what they hoped would be a dominant pass rush. Burns is coming off a career-best season. Abdul Carter was drafted No. 3 overall in hopes he would be a game-wrecking pass rusher. He looked in the summer like he was about to fulfill that promise. Kayvon Thibodeaux has at times been a good, but not great, pass rusher. No. 5 overall pick Arvell Reese is an inside linebacker with pass rush potential. Interior defensive linemen Chauncey Golston and Darius Alexander have pass rush ability. Defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson’s defense used creative schemes to pressure Giants’ quarterbacks throughout training camp. Through two weeks of the regular season, none of that talent, potential, and summer promise has mattered. The pass rush has been non-existent. The Giants have one quarterback sack. Per NextGenStats, their 1.4% sack rate is 31st in the league. Only the woeful Miami Dolphins, who do not have a sack yet, are worse. The Giants’ pressure rate of 26.1, again per NGS, is the worst in the league. The ball is coming out quickly against New York, with the 2.69-second time to throw against the Giants 26th overall. That is .41 seconds faster than league average. Still, the pressure rate isn’t good enough.…

title: Advanced stats for the Giants’ 28-6 loss to the Rams
summary: In John Harbaugh’s first season as head coach of the Baltimore Ravens, he lost a road game to Tony Dungy’s Indianapolis Colts 31-3 in Week 6 to drop the Ravens to 2-3 on the season. A few weeks later his team was manhandled by the Giants 30-10, dropping them to 6-4. That team wound up […]
full_text: Jevon Holland intercepts a pass against the Rams. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images In John Harbaugh’s first season as head coach of the Baltimore Ravens, he lost a road game to Tony Dungy’s Indianapolis Colts 31-3 in Week 6 to drop the Ravens to 2-3 on the season. A few weeks later his team was manhandled by the Giants 30-10, dropping them to 6-4. That team wound up making it to the AFC Championship Game before being eliminated by eventual Super Bowl champion Pittsburgh. Stinkers happen, and Sunday night was certainly one of them for the Giants. The issue is how you react to them. Harbaugh’s 2008 team reeled off four wins in a row in between those losses to the Colts and the Giants. His Giants team now has the chance to do something similar, with the most navigable part of their schedule coming up. For the moment, though, they have to own this stinker of a loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Jaxson Dart’s injury makes it all the more difficult, but that’s why they’re paying Harbaugh the big bucks. As Ed mentioned in The Feed on Tuesday, we’re going to start trying something new after games. We’ll continue to show you Pro Football Focus grades, but say less about them than in the past. In their place, we’ll try to show a number of other advanced stats from various sources to give you a better feel for the team as a whole, and specifically how the quarterback is doing. PFF grades You might guess that few Giants scored well in PFF’s eyes in Monday night’s game. You would be correct. Here are the grades for the offense: Andrew Thomas was the only Giants offensive player to play well, grading 74.5 overall. Thomas gave up a hit and a hurry, but from an “Other than that Mrs. Lincoln, how did you like the play?” perspective, that one QB hit was the one that injured Jaxson Dart’s knee. Similarly, Jermaine Eluemunor was charged with one sack (on the same play) and a hit, the only sack of the night on a Giants QB among 11 total pressures, which is not terrible. Still, we can see the entire Giants interior OL with grades in the 40s and Sisi Mauigoa in particular with an awful 23.3 pass block grade. John Michael Schmitz is down there too, in part because sometimes he decides to block air rather than a pass rusher: As @nickfalato mentioned last night's show — second straight week JMS didn't get a hand on a pass rusher on a screen and killed a big play. So much space ahead. Great play call. One of many bad JMS plays in pass protection from last night. Clock is ticking for him as starter. pic.twitter.com/a9pFtKRhIq — Dan Schneier (@DanSchneierNFL) September 22, 2026 Other than that, there isn’t much positive to say about anyone on the offense. A couple of the receivers (Isaiah Likely, Darnell Mooney) played fairly well, while Theo Johnson (38.0) continues to be a liability. Here are the defensive grades: It’s a very similar story, with one player performing well, a few more in the average category, and a bunch being well below par, even terrible. The most notable was Jevon Holland, who had a spectacular game – an interception (for the second game in a row), 2 forced fumbles, 7 tackles and an assist, no missed tackles, and only one completion for 9 yards. This is reminiscent of his rookie and Year 3 play, which is what got him his big contract. Among starting safeties, Holland is ranked No. 1 after two games, just ahead of the Rams’ Quentin Lake (who also had a great game last night), Julian Love, and Kyle Hamilton. Let’s hope that continues, because his backfield mate Tyler Nubin (29.3 last night) is ranked 64th of 69 safeties. A few other Giants played at least fairly well on defense last night: Dru Phillips (69.5), who only played 30 snaps and wasn’t targeted at all; Brian Burns (67.2), who had a QB hit, a hurry, and a run stop before leaving with an ankle injury; Abdul Carter (67.0), who had the Giants’ only sack of Matthew Stafford; and D.J. Reader (63.8), though both Carter and Reader had two missed tackles. On the other hand, Tremaine Edmunds had an awful game (28.5), with a missed tackle and 3 receptions in 3 targets including a TD. Shelby Harris (40.7) and Josh Tupou (40.2) played poorly as well, and Arvell Reese (50.5) did not distinguish himself either. Advanced metrics Jameis Winston did not have an auspicious season debut, to say the least: Winston was dead last among starting quarterbacks in both expected points added/play and completion % over expected…and it wasn’t particularly close except for the aged Aaron Rodgers being almost as bad in EPA/play. Matthew Stafford was in the upper right quadrant and second overall in EPA/play, which tells you about how effective the Giants’ pass defense was. Not to be outdone, the Giants’ defense said, hold my beer: The Giants were on par overall with the wretched Atlanta Falcons for worst performance of the week, but somewhat surprisingly, six teams were as bad or even worse on defense, including two who actually won their games (Kansas City and Buffalo). Here’s a different perspective on team offense and defense in Week 2, using defense-adjusted value over average ( DVOA ) as the metric: DVOA through Week 2 1. SF (OFF #2, DEF #5, ST #12) 2. BUF (OFF #1, DEF #19, ST #9) 3. BAL (OFF #3, DEF #11, ST #22) 4. KC (OFF #6, DEF #10, ST #20) 5. SEA (OFF #15, DEF #2, ST #15) 6. CIN (OFF #12, DEF #7, ST #10) 7. DAL (OFF #4, DEF #20, ST #4) 8. NYJ (OFF #14, DEF #3, ST #26)… pic.twitter.com/tOtaGWZCij — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 22, 2026 The results are not identical but fairly similar for most teams. The Giants are still in the lower left (bad on both offense and defense) quadrant, but if you’re looking for solace, they have more company than EPA/play gives them, including next week’s opponent Tennessee, which almost beat the Eagles but apparently played poorly while doing so. EPA/play says otherwise. However you slice it, the Giants were bad. In Winston’s defense, his teammates didn’t give him much help. Here is how he ranks in a few Next Gen Stats that are not about him but about the guys he was throwing to and the guys blocking for him: Winston’s receivers had the lowest average separation of any other quarterbacks (2.3 yards). His tight window percentage (TW%) of 33.3% was thus the largest of any QB (the next three – Jared Goff, Daniel Jones, Jordan Love – all lost their games). Winston’s pressure rate of 58.6% (QBP%) also led the NFL, and four of the top five in that category lost their game: If you’re looking for a silver lining, the Giants’ special teams are performing well (the plot below is for two games, not just Week 2): Special Teams EPA through Week 2 1. LV +10.7 2. CIN +10.3 3. NYG +9.9 … 30. HOU -10.1 31. MIA -12.1 32. TEN -13.5 pic.twitter.com/b0tDZbaX3x — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 22, 2026 Fortunately for the Giants, their next three games are against Tennessee, Arizona, and Washington, collectively with one win among them. Last year, when Dart went down with a concussion, Winston kept the Giants competitive against both Detroit and Green Bay. Despite his poor outing Monday night, he’s one of the best backups in the NFL. All three opponents have their own questions at QB, the Commanders being in the same boat as the Giants with their star starting quarterback out due to injury. If John Harbaugh and his staff are as good as the buzz around them was when they were hired, the Giants should still be able to win some games. Let’s see whether the juice was worth the squeeze.

title: New York Jets News: QB Geno Smith Challenged to Take Flight
summary: He isn’t who we thought he was. In 2025, Geno Smith led the league in interceptions (17). Through the first two games of the 2026 season, Smith hasn’t thrown a pick. The Jets have “0 Giveaways in Weeks 1 and 2 – first time that’s happened in 55 years,” Jets senior reporter Eric Allen shared. […]
full_text: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) looks to throw the ball during a game against the Green Bay Packers at MetLife Stadium, Sep 20, 2026, East Rutherford, NJ, USA. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co He isn’t who we thought he was. In 2025, Geno Smith led the league in interceptions (17). Through the first two games of the 2026 season, Smith hasn’t thrown a pick. The Jets have “0 Giveaways in Weeks 1 and 2 – first time that’s happened in 55 years,” Jets senior reporter Eric Allen shared. “QB Geno Smith is hitting on 70.8% of his passes. Since 2011, [the] Jets’ highest completion percentage season was 63.4% in 2024,” Allen revealed on social media. That is all good, but he can be better. The former West Virginia product is only averaging 5.8 air yards per attempt. According to ESPN’s Rich Cimini, Smith is “tied with Daniel Jones for 28th in the league.” It’s a fine line between taking care of the football and displaying a willingness to turn the cap backward to take some deep shots. ESPN’s Rich Cimini challenged Smith to “open up the passing attack to maximize their skill position talent.” That feels like an important factor heading into this Detroit Lions game in Week 3. The Detroit defense stinks, but their offense is loaded with playmakers. This could be a track meet kind of game with a ton of points being thrown around. Smith being at his best and aggressive could go a long way toward increasing the Jets’ chances of winning. J-E-T-S! Take the game-day conversation with you! title: The Jets Need More From Breece Hall
summary: We have had some time as a fanbase to digest the gut-wrenching loss this past Sunday to the Green Bay Packers. As usual, I’ve heard a tremendous amount of blame directed toward head coach Aaron Glenn for some of his decisions that arguably warrant criticism. Again, you’ll also hear some valid criticism for some of […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 20: Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets runs with the ball against the Green Bay Packers during the first half of the game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have had some time as a fanbase to digest the gut-wrenching loss this past Sunday to the Green Bay Packers. As usual, I’ve heard a tremendous amount of blame directed toward head coach Aaron Glenn for some of his decisions that arguably warrant criticism. Again, you’ll also hear some valid criticism for some of the usual suspects: Geno Smith, Arian Smith, Brandon Stephens, Jeremy Ruckert, and, hell, I’ve even noticed plenty of negative commentary about Armand Membou, who had an uncharacteristically disastrous game. But I’ve noticed that the fanbase, as well as the national media, has been shockingly quiet about one underperforming player. And when you compare what the Jets are paying for, I think it’s extremely misplaced not to talk about him. The Jets need more from Breece Hall. Let me preface my overall statement once again by clarifying that I’m talking about Breece Hall’s performance at this moment in time. I fully understand it’s only been two games. I fully understand that Breece Hall is an extremely talented player and that this is an extremely small sample. Things can and likely will change. Hall could run for 200 yards this upcoming Sunday and all will be right for a while, and the sentiment and tone would, and should, be different. But from what I’ve seen so far, I’m disappointed. Hall, unlike some other players on the Jets, should have higher expectations attached to him. After all, he’s one of the laughably few players on this roster who is getting paid like he should perform at a high level. Take a holistic view of the Jets’ financial situation and roster, and you’ll see an obvious signal: the Jets are not paying top dollar pretty much anywhere. If you ignore the fact that Aaron Rodgers and Justin Fields, two guys who aren’t even on the roster, have the highest cap hits, Hall is one of the few Jets players who has actually received a second contract with the team and is getting paid considerable money relative to his position. Hall currently ranks eighth in APY by contract among running backs, and his cap hit this year is the third highest on the team. That’s a long-winded way of saying this: the Jets are paying Breece Hall to be one of the better running backs in the league and one of the best players on their team. So far, based on what I’ve watched, that just hasn’t been the case. Rewatching the game this past week, Hall came across as indecisive in his reads. This wasn’t particularly different in Week 1 where I thought Braelon Allen arguably outplayed him. While the Jets offense has been competent through two weeks, I’m not sure Hall would crack my top 10 names when explaining why that has been the case. Outside of a terrific play after the catch at the end of the third quarter this past Sunday, Hall didn’t really elevate the offense or, to be honest, prove that he should be getting a heavy workload. And if you don’t want to take my word for it, there are plenty of stats that tell a similar story. A few years ago, Next Gen Stats developed a stat called Rushing Yards Over Expected, or RYOE. RYOE is an advanced football metric designed to isolate a running back’s individual skill from the quality of his offensive line blocking. At its core, it asks a pretty simple question: how many yards did a ball carrier gain compared to what an average NFL running back would have gained in the exact same situation? The more yards, the better. If you’re consistently below expectation, you’re probably not playing particularly well. Currently, through two weeks, Hall ranks 48th out of 52 qualified backs in RYOE, producing -16 yards over expectation. Now, this isn’t a perfect stat. No stat is. RYOE can occasionally be driven by a handful of amazing runs that carry a running back’s performance over the course of a season. However, even when you try to account for that statistically, Hall’s numbers aren’t much better. When tracking the percentage of runs that were positive, meaning they gained more yards than expected, Hall ranks 43rd out of 52 backs, with only 28.9% of his runs yielding positive results. Ian Hartitz of RotoWire also tweeted out another interesting stat, which is included in the tweet below. Yards after contact is cool and all BUT it gets skewed by big runs sometimes (like anything). Solution: Percentage of carries to gain 3+ yards after contact. Current leaderboard among all RBs with 15+ carries this season: pic.twitter.com/NVF4ZjulqP — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) September 22, 2026 Even from a yards-after-contact perspective, Hall has ranked poorly, coming in 43rd out of 44 qualified backs. His PFF grade has him 43rd out of 59 backs, and even if you find all of these stats to be too nerdy or advanced, yards per carry tells a similar story. Hall is currently averaging a pedestrian 3.4 yards per carry, which ranks 38th among qualified backs. Again, none of this means Hall is suddenly a bad running back. It’s only two games, and I don’t want to give off the impression that two weeks is enough to completely rewrite our opinion of a player who has already shown us what he’s capable of doing at the NFL level. But when you combine what I’ve seen on the field with what the numbers are telling us, it’s hard to come away from these first two games thinking Hall has played particularly well. I don’t want to sound too harsh. Things can flip quickly in this league, and all it takes is one strong performance for Hall to potentially look great in all of these stats. My main concern is simply that if this team was ever going to outperform expectations this year, or win more games than what their 31st-place ranking in active cap spending would suggest they should, it was going to happen because they got a few great performances from their guys on rookie deals and strong performances from the handful of players they identified as worthy of larger contracts. Hall is one of those players, which is why I think the expectations need to be different for him. This isn’t about demanding that he run for 150 yards every Sunday. It’s about recognizing that the Jets have made a strong financial commitment to Hall and, as a result, they need him to consistently look like one of the better players on their roster. That doesn’t mean I’ve given up on Breece Hall. It doesn’t mean I think the contract was a mistake. It doesn’t mean I think he’s incapable of returning to the player we have seen. It simply means that, through two games, he hasn’t been good enough. History suggests that Jets fans won’t be patient if that continues. Soon enough, they’ll expect more from Breece Hall, and honestly, the Jets should too.

title: Eagles practice squad safety poached by the Rams
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are losing another practice squad player via poaching. One day after the Atlanta Falcons signed cornerback Robert Longerbeam away from Philly, the Los Angeles Rams are adding Eagles undrafted rookie free agent safety Maximus Pulley to their roster. This development notably comes ahead of the Eagles’ Week 4 home game against the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - AUGUST 01: Philadelphia Eagles cornerback Maximus Pulley #36 runs a drill during the Philadelphia Eagles training camp on August 1st, 2026 at Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles are losing another practice squad player via poaching. One day after the Atlanta Falcons signed cornerback Robert Longerbeam away from Philly , the Los Angeles Rams are adding Eagles undrafted rookie free agent safety Maximus Pulley to their roster. This development notably comes ahead of the Eagles’ Week 4 home game against the Rams. The Eagles temporarily elevated Pulley to the roster for their Week 2 game against the Tennessee Titans. He only played on special teams ( six snaps ) but the Eagles presumably called him up to also provide depth at safety. Starter Andrew Mukuba ended up playing but he had been ruled questionable … and Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II were the only other full-time two safeties on the roster. The Eagles still only have three safeties on their roster ahead of Week 3. They did officially add Kenny Moore II to the team on Wednesday but 1) he’s joining the practice squad to start out and 2) as primarily a nickel cornerback, he lacks extensive safety experience. These two poachings come at a time while the Eagles are opting to keep an open roster spot. If they wanted to prevent either Longerbeam or Pulley from leaving, they probably could’ve just convinced them to stay in Philly by promoting them to the roster. Guessing the team wasn’t interested in going that route. In addition to losing Longerbeam and Pulley, the Eagles previously lost four players to waivers after roster cuts: Cameron Latu (New England Patriots), Kapena Gushiken (Indianapolis Colts), Cameron Williams (Atlanta Falcons), and Myles Hinton (Cincinnati Bengals). Latu and Gushiken have already had some flashes with their new teams. Is it the end of the world that the Eagles lost these players? Not necessarily. But while Howie Roseman certainly gets a lot of things right, it is fair to wonder about some of the roster mechanics that have been going on. Did they really need to keep four quarterbacks? Why was Eli Stowers placed on injured reserve prior to Week 1 instead of earlier (with one of their two designated for return spots, if necessary, which instead went to Jakorian Bennett and Grant Calcaterra)? Was E.J. Jenkins over Latu the right call? Did they need to keep vested veterans (who aren’t subject to waivers) like Elijah Moore (who has been a healthy scratch as the team’s seventh WR for two games) and Jonathan Jones on the roster? Even if we assume that the Eagles were justified in making the decisions that they did, it’s not really ideal to be losing six players that the team liked to some extent. title: 6 thoughts on Zach Ertz’s return to the Eagles
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles re-signed Zach Ertz earlier this week! I think it’s a good move. Here are some reasons why. 1) The nostalgia factor. Let me be clear: this signing wasn’t JUST a nostalgia play. But it is hard to deny it’s a nice bonus. Ertz is an Eagles legend. Among many other highlights, he […]
full_text: Oct 14, 2021; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) and tight end Zach Ertz (86) celebrate a touchdown against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-USA TODAY Sports The Philadelphia Eagles re-signed Zach Ertz earlier this week! I think it’s a good move. Here are some reasons why. 1) The nostalgia factor. Let me be clear: this signing wasn’t JUST a nostalgia play. But it is hard to deny it’s a nice bonus. Ertz is an Eagles legend. Among many other highlights, he caught the game-winning touchdown in Super Bowl LII. He’s expressed a lot of love for Philly, which has been reflected through his charity work in the community that continued even after he was traded away. Many an Eagles fan can now break out their old No. 86 jerseys. That’s pretty cool. 2) The Eagles needed tight end help. With Dallas Goedert reportedly expected to miss some time due to a knee injury, the team had no choice but to add to the tight end room. Johnny Mundt averages about five receiving yards per game over the course of his career. E.J. Jenkins has flashed pass-catching ability in practice settings but he has two career targets for one reception that went for seven yards (and a touchdown!). Grant Calcaterra and Eli Stowers can’t be activated from injured reserve until Week 5. It’s hard to feel great about them as major contributors even when they’re ready to return. The Eagles needed to add a more serious pass-catching threat. Ertz is just that. 3) He can still play! At least, there’s reason to be optimistic about his outlook. Ertz had a pretty nice season for the Washington Commanders in 2024, logging 66 receptions for 654 yards, 51 first downs, and seven touchdowns. For context (not comparison), the last time Goedert had 66 receptions was … never. Goedert has also never produced that many first downs in a given season. And the last time Goedert surpassed Ertz’s 2024 yardage total was when he had 702 in 2022. Ertz was the best thing the Commanders had going for them in Washington’s 55 to 23 loss to the Eagles in the NFC Championship Game. His team-high 16 targets produced 11 receptions for 104 yards that day. Ertz looked good again in 2025. His 72 targets produced 50 receptions for 504 yards, 25 first downs, and four touchdowns prior to suffering a torn ACL in early December 2025. Now, I can’t say I know the kind of toll this injury took on him. Maybe it severely impacted Ertz, who turns 36 in November, moving forward. But it’s not like ACL injuries are the death knells they used to be. And it’s not like Ertz’s game was ever predicated on elite athleticism. Ertz has been a really good tight end in the NFL because he knows how to get open. He’s a very smart player who can exploit how defenses try to guard him. This play style has translated well as he’s aged. I expect him to still be able to be effective. 4) He has chemistry with Jalen Hurts. Ertz hasn’t logged catches from Hurts since October 2021. But the two did work together for a time after the Eagles selected Hurts in the 2020 NFL Draft. From 2020-2021, Hurts targeted Ertz 53 times for 28 receptions, 299 yards, 13 first downs, and two touchdowns. Trust is big factor with any quarterback and his targets … but arguably especially so with Hurts. It shouldn’t take too long for the two to get back on the same page. Which is important, because the Eagles will be counting on Ertz to see targets as soon as Week 3 against the Chicago Bears. 5) He could help the Eagles shift their offensive approach. Perhaps this is wishcasting. But the Eagles’ current offensive approach is frustrating. Unable to run the ball efficiently behind a struggling offensive line, they’re wasting early downs by insisting to slam into a brick wall over and over. Look at this first down futility: The Eagles offense is just the second team in the last 27 years to not gain a SINGLE first down on 1st & 10 across their first two games. https://t.co/GXEQfp17L7 pic.twitter.com/nFIuIY9Zz7 — Eagles Eric (@EaglesXsandOs) September 21, 2026 Part of these struggles are due to a lack of actively trying to get a first down on first down. Case in point: it took until midway through the third quarter of their second game for the Eagles to even ATTEMPT A PASS BEYOND THE STICKS while on first down ( this play ). So, how does Ertz factor in here? The Eagles need to be honest with themselves about where their running game is at right now. Maybe it’ll improve down the line. For now, though, their strength is throwing the ball. Hurts looks great. The wide receivers are inspiring confidence. The offense should be leaning into their passing attack. Ertz can be one of the targets to help contribute to this approach. Also, if Nick Sirianni and Sean Mannion are truly as insistent on “staying on schedule” by getting to third-and-manageable as they purport to be, they can sub out ineffective running plays with short targets to Ertz that are likely to be more fruitful. 6) An Eagles franchise record is within reach. No player has logged more receptions for the Eagles than Harold Carmichael, who has 589. Ertz is currently 10 behind him. Assuming he stays healthy, Ertz is very likely going to at least get 11 catches to become the new franchise leader. Other benchmarks of note: Ertz is also only 197 yards away from tying Mike Quick for fourth in Eagles franchise history for receiving yards. He’s 245 away from tying DeSean Jackson. He could feasibly move above those two to only be behind Carmichael at the top and Pete Retzlaff in second place. If Ertz plays in all 15 remaining regular season games, he’ll move to sole possession of the 24th-most games ever played for the Eagles.

title: Jaxson Dart injury: Giants quarterback out for season [UPDATE]
summary: The New York Giants had an exciting Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys! Since then? Not great. The G-Men got blown out by the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night in Week 2 while also sustaining multiple key injuries. One of those was to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, who left the game with a […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Jaxson Dart #6 of the New York Giants walks back to the locker room after being injured in a play against Byron Young #0 of the Los Angeles Rams during the first quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New York Giants had an exciting Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys! Since then? Not great. The G-Men got blown out by the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night in Week 2 while also sustaining multiple key injuries. One of those was to starting quarterback Jaxson Dart, who left the game with a knee injury. After some initial optimism (Giants GM Joe Schoen insisted that he was “going to be OK”) that Dart avoided a major injury, the Giants are getting some bad news. Dart’s injury is “worse than anticipated” and the quarterback is “out an extended period of time, possibly the season,” according to a report from NFL insider Ian Rapoport . [UPDATE: Dart is expected to have season-ending surgery. Brutal.] This news is obviously a brutal blow to the Giants’ outlook. They have an experienced backup in Jameis Winston, who struggled against the Rams but has obviously had some levels of success in the past. The Philadelphia Eagles are set to play the Giants on the road in Week 9 and at home in Week 18. It sounds like Dart will at least miss the November 8 game. And if New York is unable to stay afloat without him, they might not bother bringing him back (assuming he’s even healthy enough to play) very late in the season. Tough break for the Giants, who are now the second team in the NFC East to have a major quarterback injury with Jayden Daniels also getting hurt in Week 2. Check out more coverage of this injury over at Big Blue View . We’re also reacting to the news on the NFC East Mixtape podcast :
