title: Eagles-Titans Film Review: Expected more from this defense
summary: I expected more from the Eagles’ defense against the Titans. There were some outstanding individual plays, and the Titans managed only 20 points (7 of them caused by Hurts’ early INT), but the performance was not what I expected from a Vic Fangio defense. The Eagles gave up 5.7 yards per play, and the Titans’ […]
full_text: Tennessee Titans wide receiver Elic Ayomanor (5) launches over Philadelphia Eagles safety Marcus Epps (29) during the fourth quarter Sept. 20 at Nissan Stadium in Nashville, Tenn. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I expected more from the Eagles’ defense against the Titans. There were some outstanding individual plays, and the Titans managed only 20 points (7 of them caused by Hurts’ early INT), but the performance was not what I expected from a Vic Fangio defense. The Eagles gave up 5.7 yards per play, and the Titans’ offense generated far too many easy yards on the ground and after the catch. The missed tackles and slow reactions were particularly odd because rallying to the football has been such a consistent strength of this group. I think the heat probably contributed. But I don’t want to make fatigue the explanation for everything. Unlike last week, the Eagles’ offense gave the defense real breaks. The defense only faced 51 offensive plays. My feeling watching this was that the Eagles were too easy to attack in situations where they should have been comfortable. Defense Let’s start with the run game. The Titans get movement with duo, and I don’t love the response from either linebacker. Zack Baun and Jihaad Campbell arrive late, and the safeties don’t get downhill with enough conviction to help out. Despite this rep, Campbell had a pretty decent game against the run, but this is a bad rep. He still doesn’t trust his eyes. duo can test linebackers because the double teams create space and the back can choose his crease late. You need decisive second-level fits and help from behind. The Eagles didn’t give themselves enough of either on this rep. I’m not saying every run was a disaster. The Eagles had some very good reps. But this is the kind of rep that sets the tone early on in a game. Eagles' Defense All22 Thread vs. Titans. 1) Slightly strange defensive game. The Eagles had some issues against the run, which they need to work on. The Titans found success with Duo concepts (see below). Both linebackers are slow here, and I wasn't impressed with either safety's… pic.twitter.com/MCgjjvGUlb — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 The biggest challenge the Eagles faced was outside zone runs. On this play, the Eagles slant their defensive line away from the direction of the run. Slanting can disrupt blocking angles and is a tool that Fangio loves to create negative plays, but it carries a risk. If the offense runs the other way, the defense can be displaced from the point of attack. I also wasn’t a fan of these five-man fronts that put Campbell out at edge and left Baun as the lone conventional linebacker. I can see the appeal of getting more bodies on the line, but it asks a lot of Baun if the offensive line wins its blocks. Once again, I wanted the safeties to arrive faster. The Titans had 10 outside-zone attempts for 67 yards, so this wasn’t an isolated run-fit issue. 2) The Eagles struggled against outside zone in this game, too. I didn't love putting Campbell back at edge in some fronts, because it left Baun with a lot to do as a lone LB. The Eagles slant away from the rush direction, which is the risk you take when you slant your defensive… pic.twitter.com/0fACIPRxNe — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 There was plenty to like about Jalyx Hunt, though. On third-and-16, Moro Ojomo and Hunt work the stunt beautifully. Hunt’s rush is the reason the Titans cannot take advantage of what develops behind it. He played with real energy throughout the game, both as a rusher and in pursuit. I was impressed by his athleticism and hustle. But look at the coverage as the rush gets home. Campbell reacts to the short route and leaves too much space over his head. Tariq Wool is shouting at him to get depth, and you can almost see Campbell have the ‘OH NO’ moment when he turns around and sees the receiver. Campbell still has to be more aware of the route developing behind him. Opponents will notice plays like this, and they will keep testing him until he gets better. 3) The Eagles win on 3rd and 16 here, due to Jaylx Hunt's fantastic rush on the stunt with Ojomo. I thought Hunt was excellent and played hard all game. However, watch Woolen and Campbell here. Campbell cannot get sucked up by the short route and let that receiver over his… pic.twitter.com/JbVB4Ith1V — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 However, watch how smoothly Campbell moves to cover the flat here. He has the length and athleticism to make plays in space. My concern in zone is how quickly he recognizes the route combination, gains the right depth, and understands where the next threat is coming from. That should improve with experience, but the Eagles need it to improve relatively quickly. This call caught my eye. Fangio usually majors in weak rotation, moving the safety away from the nickel, and match principles that make routes less predictable for the quarterback. I saw more strong rotation and what looked like conventional spot drops (just think straight-up Cover 3) than I expected outside the obvious third-and-long situations. Fangio has simplified things early in a season before, but I was surprised by how often it showed up here. I have a sort of worry that he could be doing this to protect Campbell and/or Marcus Epps. Does he trust these guys? 4) However, here is why the Eagles will want him to keep developing. Look how long, smooth, and athletic he is covering the flat here. It's not a physical issue in coverage. It's a mental issue. Also, a bit of a weird point, but the Eagles seemed to play quite a lot of standard… pic.twitter.com/SNoH9EJCjN — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 This is a great job collapsing the pocket on 3rd-and-long. Nolan Smith has been particularly good at these cleanup sacks since his rookie year. His athleticism and effort mean that when another rusher forces the quarterback to move, Smith can close the remaining space quickly. It’s not your classic ‘bend the edge’ win, but Smith does find ways to get sacks and make plays. 5) Great job on the rush here by the Eagles. They collapse the pocket, and Nolan Smith is great at getting these clean-up sacks through pure athleticism and hustle. He's been doing this since he was a rookie! pic.twitter.com/nrpW8DTvsM — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 This play bothered me. The Eagles put Michael Carter on the field in dime, a personnel package I was happy to see and I think we probably should see more, and allowed a short completion to become a substantial gain. Ojomo gets after the ball, but the secondary is too slow to respond. For a defense that normally rallies to the football, it looks completely out of character. Too many players in the secondary aren’t hustling to the football, and it happened multiple times. Does the defense lack speed on the back end? It looked like it this week. Plays like this can’t happen. 6) The Eagles did something I haven't seen in years under Fangio, and I'm hoping it was heat-related. They did not rally to the ball well or tackle. That barely ever happens. Watch Ojomo here compared to some in the secondary. They use dime personnel here (which I was quite… pic.twitter.com/SzX0tAjVL0 — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 22, 2026 This is a much better run-defense rep, and Campbell deserves credit. He avoids the blocker and gets to the football. I included this clip to showcase how Campbell gets around offensive linemen, because he prefers to run around them rather than take them on. Ojomo does the hard work by fighting through the combo block, Jordan Davis holds up inside, and Hunt drives the tight end backward. Once the front prevents the Titans from creating their intended gap, Campbell can use his athleticism to finish. That’s the version of this run defense we need to see more often. title: For the Eagles, first down has been the worst down
summary: The new look Eagles offense hasn’t been much fun. There are multiple reasons, but one of them is that on 1st down, they’re terrible. The offense is 28th in EPA/play and 31st in both yards per play and success rate; and have gained a 1st down on 1st down just twice, the fewest in the […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Cam Jurgens #51 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on as he walks off the field against the Washington Commanders following an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The new look Eagles offense hasn’t been much fun. There are multiple reasons, but one of them is that on 1st down, they’re terrible. The offense is 28th in EPA/play and 31st in both yards per play and success rate; and have gained a 1st down on 1st down just twice, the fewest in the league. Oddly, neither were on 1st and 10, Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception in the 4th quarter against the Titans was on 1st and 17 , and then his TD on 1st and goal was from the 3. On 1st down, the Eagles have as many negative plays as they do plays that gained 7+ yards, 9 each. On their 48 1st downs, they have failed to gain yardage on 18 of them. Their average 2nd down needs 8.7 yards to gain a first down, 26th so far this season. They’re bad at everything. Though the Eagles run 65% of the time on 1st down. They stink there. 24th in EPA/play 27th in success rate 28th in yards per carry When the Eagles do throw on 1st down, they’re woefully short. CPOE: 19th EPA per play: 26th Success rate: 31st Air yards per attempt: 31st Yards per attempt: 32nd This is not a Jalen Hurts issue. He had the 5th highest air yards per attempt on 1st down in 2025, and 14th in 2024. Nor is this a lack of AJ Brown issue, he was 48th in air yards per target last season, nor is this a Dontayvion Wicks as his replacement issue, he was 56th. And though it has only been two games, this isn’t a situation where one bad game, the team’s failure to gain a single 1st down on 1st down against the Commanders, is bogging down the numbers. The Eagles converted a 1st down on just 2 of 28 1st downs against the Titans, 7.1%. Given the same rate against the Commanders, the Eagles would still be dead last in 1st conversion rate on 1st down. The next worst team, the Steelers, have converted at 7.4%. This is an offensive line and coaching issue. The Eagles are 19th in sack rate per play, and 28th in pressures per play. Short throws to beat the pressure is a tried and true way of masking offensive line problems, but the Eagles entire first down offense is throwing short passes. They’re not trying to take a shot down the field. Even Darius Cooper’s 23 yard reception on 1st and 17 was caught 5 yards beyond the line of scrimmage, though he wasn’t the first read, that was a good progression by Jalen Hurts. Two games is a small sample size, but the NFL is built out of small sample sizes. Two games is a playoff run. Two games into the season and the Bucs, Chargers, Colts, and Texans are in trouble. Two games into the season and the Eagles offense is in trouble too. Moving Cam Jurgens, who co-leads the league in holding penalties, to guard didn’t improve things. Perhaps more time will result in improved offensive line play, but there’s not a rich history of teams making significant changes to their line in-season and getting great results.

title: Eagles News: “Dontayvion Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal”
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles) has been a pretty good pickup; he’s looking like a real solid WR2 to pair with DeVonta Smith as WR1. Seems to me like Smitty and Makai Lemon missing a lot of time […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Dontayvion Wicks #13 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on against the Washington Commanders during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Dontayvion Wicks (AKA Don Wick AKA Donny Candles) has been a pretty good pickup; he’s looking like a real solid WR2 to pair with DeVonta Smith as WR1. Seems to me like Smitty and Makai Lemon missing a lot of time in training camp really helped Jalen Hurts foster a better connection with Wicks since that was often his top option to throw to. Good job by Howie Roseman to trade for Wicks on the cheap (two Day 3 draft picks) and sign him to an extension to keep him under team control through 2027. Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Cam Jurgens’ fit, Dontayvion Wicks’ emergence, Zach Ertz’s role: Eagles thoughts – The Athletic The passing game has exceeded what I expected, and the wide receivers are quieting any external concerns. Dontayvion Wicks is validating the summer optimism. One point I made frequently this offseason was that the Eagles didn’t need to replace A.J. Brown; DeVonta Smith could handle that No. 1 role. They needed to replace Smith as the No. 2 option. Wicks is showcasing why the Eagles thought he was an under-the-radar steal when they acquired him via trade and signed him to a contract extension. Wicks has caught seven of 10 targets for 147 yards. All seven of his receptions have resulted in first downs or touchdowns. His average depth of target has been 15.7 yards. Three of his receptions have traveled over 20 yards in the air. Four of his five receptions Sunday were on third down, and two were for third-and-12 conversions. Hurts trusts him. Wicks runs precise routes. He makes difficult catches. Wicks and Smith have combined for 20 catches for 317 yards through two games. That’s more yards than in any of the first two games Brown and Smith played together. This doesn’t mean the Eagles have a duo like Brown and Smith, but it’s a formidable combination. Eagles-Titans Film Review: A very good offense is hiding in here – BGN The Eagles won 24-20, and I came away feeling much better about the passing game than I did after Week 1. The Eagles found answers against the Titans’ coverage, attacked the weaknesses I flagged in my preview (which is always great to see), and repeatedly converted third-and-long. However, the offense cannot keep making life this difficult for itself. The Eagles went 11-of-18 on third down, which is an absurd 61.1% conversion rate. That’s why they sustained drives despite averaging only 4.7 yards per play, turning the ball over twice and rushing for 89 yards on 32 attempts. Winning on third down is obviously good. Needing Hurts to repeatedly deliver elite throws on third-and-long isn’t a sustainable offensive identity. The early-down numbers are wild. I mean, come on… Chicago Bears Injury News: Tyson Bagent in concussion protocol – Windy City Gridiron If Williams and Bagent can’t go, look for 38-year-old Case Keenum to get the start. Keenum last played in a regular-season game on Christmas Eve, 2023, when he started for the Houston Texans. He was 11 of 17 for 62 yards and 2 interceptions before giving way to Davis Mills in the fourth quarter. Chicago also has undrafted free agent Miller Moss on the practice squad, who would likely be elevated to back up Keenum. Game Review – PHI 24, TEN 20 – Iggles Blitz All the WRs contributed in this game. Dontayvion Wicks went 5-74, with several catches coming on 3rd or 4th down. He did a good job of getting open and catching the ball when it came his way. He had a drop on the final drive, but it was only going to be for a couple of yards so the team was better off that he didn’t catch that. Darius Cooper was 2-26 and caught the game-winning TD. He had a chance for another good gain, but the pass was just a bit too far out front. Hollywood Brown had 2 runs for 12 yards. Makai Lemon caught 1 pass for 14 yards. He also had 1 run for -5 yards, a pass behind the LOS. Really good game from the WR corps. The Winners and Losers of the NFL Week 2 – The Ringer Every Eagles game becomes a national referendum on how much credit belongs to Hurts and how much belongs to everything surrounding him. But right now, there are real problems for Philadelphia to solve. The offensive line hasn’t played well in the first two weeks. The early-down offense has created far too many difficult third-down situations. Vic Fangio’s defense has struggled throughout both second halves and allowed Cam Ward to play one of the best games of his career on Sunday. But after an offseason spent discussing how much talent the Eagles have assembled around their quarterback, they are 2-0 because of him. He was the one who finished that shit, and he got to tell that to Simmons’s face. Evaluating surprise early-season trends for 32 NFL teams – ESPN The early surprise: The defense has generated zero takeaways. The verdict: Mirage. The Eagles ranked sixth in opponent turnovers (47) over the past two seasons under defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, and they should see their fortunes turn in the near future. They’ll get a boost in the pass-rushing department when their splash offseason acquisition, Jonathan Greenard, returns from his pec injury. “Super, super close,” Greenard said last week. Do-it-all defensive back Cooper DeJean has been dealing with calf and abdomen injuries, as well; the healthier he gets, the more dangerous that back end becomes. Does Zach Ertz still have the juice to contribute to the Eagles? Here’s what the film — and history — says – Inquirer While Ertz still can thrive as a receiver, he does not bring much as a blocker, an area where the Eagles have struggled through two weeks. Much of his time in Washington was spent as a detached slot receiver on run-pass option plays or as a lead blocker on the perimeter for zone-read runs with Jayden Daniels. He has not had an in-line blocking role for the majority of his career, and that is unlikely to change in this reunion. But with Goedert missing time, Ertz’s contributions as a pass catcher seemed to be what the Eagles are seeking in the franchise legend. 10 reasons to be optimistic about the Eagles’ defense – NBCSP Pass defense: Not everything has gone well so far, but the Eagles’ pass defense has been elite. The Eagles have only allowed 166 passing yards per game, 4th-fewest in the league, and they’ve held opposing quarterbacks to 57.4 percent completion percentage, also 4th-lowest in the league. They’ve only allowed two passing touchdowns, tied for 6th-fewest in the league. And they’ve allowed only six total plays of 20 yards or more, 10th-fewest in the league through two games. This is a passing league and the Eagles are built to stop the pass. 2026 NFL offensive line rankings: Falcons rise, Patriots tumble following injury – PFF 4) PHILADELPHIA EAGLES. The injury to Landon Dickerson forced some shuffling on the Eagles’ offensive line, with Cam Jurgens moving from center to left guard and Drew Kendall coming in to replace him in the middle of the offensive line. The results weren’t great for either player, with both earning sub-50.0 PFF grades against the Tennessee Titans. Lane Johnson was the team’s best pass-blocker, producing a 97.7% PFF pass-block win rate. There is clearly still a lot of talent on this offensive line, but how Jurgens and Kendall perform this week will be key. Spadaro: Jalen Hurts, Eagles do what it takes to win – PhiladelphiaEagles.com This has been, as all parties said from the very start, a collaborative project. Sean Mannion was hired as the Eagles’ offensive coordinator and brought with him a new scheme that required everyone to buy in, make progress on a daily basis, and understand the “why” in his…

title: Eagles rookie report card: Titans game
summary: The Eagles beat the heat and the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite scorching conditions down on the field, Philadelphia escaped Nashville on the back of a heroic Jalen Hurts drive. The rookie contribution on Sunday was small, but here’s what we noticed from the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class. Makai Lemon: C- It’s getting kind […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles warms up prior to the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles beat the heat and the Tennessee Titans on Sunday. Despite scorching conditions down on the field, Philadelphia escaped Nashville on the back of a heroic Jalen Hurts drive. The rookie contribution on Sunday was small, but here’s what we noticed from the Eagles’ 2026 NFL Draft class. Makai Lemon: C- It’s getting kind of funny now. In Week 1, Makai Lemon’s peculiar usage landed him with negative five yards receiving. The screens and shuffle passes were not working for the young man. In the Tennessee game, the Eagles decided to get him on another shuffle pass that lost five yards… Luckily for his box score, it was counted as a rushing attempt. Lemon got his first quality target in this game, however, and converted on a really nice 14-yard catch. He broke nicely on a route, Jalen Hurts hit him right in the middle of the field and he caught the pass with bodies around. Those are the kinds of plays the Eagles need from Lemon, especially out of the slot. As the season goes on, I expect Lemon’s usage increases as a middle of the field target as Hurts targets that area of the field more and more. While the Titans game wasn’t a stats bonanza, we got a glimmer of hope from Lemon in this one. Extra credit: Makai Lemon HOOFED it down the field to help tackle Amani Hooker and prevent a pick six. Nice play, rook. Other thoughts on the rookies: Cam Jurgens looked really rough in this game at guard. If the Eagles want to keep Drew Kendall at center, where he played well, Philly might consider benching Jurgens at some point later this season if his bad play persists. Such a move could help Micah Morris up the depth chart behind Willie Lampkin. The Dallas Goedert injury sucks. Even with the Zach Ertz signing, the Eagles tight end situation looks really rough. Eli Stowers needs to contribute at some point this season, even a little bit. He can’t return to the active roster until Week 5 at the earliest.

title: Steelers fans are mad; who is to blame?
summary: Is it already time to panic about the 2026 Steelers? Most football watchers would tell you Week 2 is far too early in the season to overreact. But after a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots last Sunday — a clear blowout by NFL standards — there are definitely some reasons to worry. This […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II and New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft talk before the game at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Is it already time to panic about the 2026 Steelers? Most football watchers would tell you Week 2 is far too early in the season to overreact. But after a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots last Sunday — a clear blowout by NFL standards — there are definitely some reasons to worry. This week, Steelers Read & React attempts to pinpoint what’s really wrong with the Steelers, if it’s fixable, and who is to blame. The Steelers offense is a mess, but is it fixable? RB : The Steelers’ offense, in a three-point effort against the Patriots, was unsurprisingly very bad. Watching the all-22 of this particular performance was essentially a sampler platter of everything you never want to see on offense: mental mistakes, a lack of physicality, questionable play design, looking slow – you name it, there’s a Steelers play from Sunday that exemplifies it. Still, we can distill things down into a few themes: Aaron Rodgers is not the Aaron Rodgers of old. I don’t even mean this in a critical way – he’s 42! It’s hard to hold it against him, but there were some high-level plays left on the table Sunday that a more mobile or accurate-under-pressure passer might’ve made. That said, I would not call Rodgers the main problem in this offense through two weeks. Especially on scramble drills, I’m not sure if Rodgers and his receivers are on the same page much. Rodgers needs a go-to, Davante Adams type, and the Steelers don’t have anyone particularly close. The offensive line, even Zach Frazier, got outmuscled at times on Sunday. When they weren’t getting driven back, the offensive line struggled mightily with the Patriots’ blitzes, simulated pressures and stunts. The Steelers’ line allowed a number of free rushers on Sunday – but without being in the team’s meeting rooms, it’s hard to diagnose which mistakes fall on the quarterback, the pass protectors and/or the coaching staff. On some plays, the Steelers’ pass catchers just weren’t getting open. Some of that falls on play design, but there’s also not a lot of “snap,” for lack of a better word, in the routes. As a caveat to all of the above points, the Patriots defense looked excellent on Sunday. New England has one of the league’s best secondaries, and the front seven has some great players. Similarly to how the Pittsburgh offense looked promising at times following a win over the terrible Atlanta Falcons, it’s important to adjust analysis based on the opponent. Despite how much went wrong on Sunday, Pittsburgh did have some opportunities on offense. The road back to competence is a long one, but it’s not impossible. Let’s take a brief look at the film to illustrate those points: What stood out to me first was just how much the Patriots’ defensive line dominated the Steelers up front. Right tackle Dylan Cook and right guard Spencer Anderson took most of the criticism after the loss, but everyone up front, including highly-regarded center Zach Frazier, put out some bad reps. The 2026 Steelers offense, everyone pic.twitter.com/M3nhu3YSnP — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 23, 2026 The numbers below correlate with the plays in the above clip: Here I’m not sure if it’s weird play design or if Pat Freiermuth should’ve stayed in to block given there’s a free rusher right in Rodgers’ face. Either way, a dump-off to DK Metcalf in motion would’ve been an acceptable outlet here had the receiver not run straight into a bull-rushed Frazier. Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick do a great job climbing to the second level, but the Steelers trust Freiermuth to one-on-one block a defensive end (it doesn’t end well) and Frazier again gets pushed backwards into the play. Not much Rico Dowdle can do here. This time it’s McCormick getting shoved back, and Darnell Washington runs into him trying to get to a split zone block. As a result, Dowdle hits the hole late. A younger Rodgers probably evades this sack, but instead, Spencer Anderson gets driven right into his lap. Failure on multiple fronts on this sack; Anderson gets turned around, the left side of the line fails a stunt pick-up and Frazier gets bull-rushed (and anchors too late), preventing Rodgers from stepping up. That lack of anchor across the board is one of the more worrying cutups. Less worrying, in a weird way, were the reps where a lineman failed to block anyone at all. That feels more like a coaching/communication issue, that should be easier to patch up in-season. I won’t bother giving play-by-play commentary to the below cut-up as it’s fairly obvious. But what bears repeating is that these sim pressures and ambiguous defensive fronts continue to be all the rage in the NFL, and the Steelers continue to struggle against these concepts. Rodgers has long liked to dice up defenses based on pre-snap alignments, but the league has moved past that in many ways. Free rushers were an issue all game against the Patriots pic.twitter.com/qmJA7fW8rh — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 23, 2026 Again, though, I don’t want to over-criticize Rodgers here, who didn’t have a lot going for him all game against a ferocious pass rush and clamping secondary. The "What do we expect Aaron Rodgers to do here?" reel pic.twitter.com/rxXScUFS4t — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 23, 2026 In reference to the clips above: Rodgers does a great job stepping up here, but who is open? Metcalf is not separating at all. Maybe Freiermuth is an option late, but he turns upfield instead of crossing Rodgers’ line of sight. The quick out to Roman Wilson could’ve been an immediate option here, but the play looks like it was supposed to develop further. Rodgers gets flushed right and there’s nothing available, but he does draw a pass interference on a scrambling toss to Freiermuth. Add this to the list of “Should Roman Wilson have not drifted so far upfield?” plays. Freiermuth might’ve been available here cutting inside had he not fallen down when Rodgers looked to throw. This looks like an inaccurate ball from Rodgers, but there’s instant pressure and no one creates any separation at their breaks. Finally, while there were enough horrible plays to lead to dramatic conclusions along the lines of “no one is ever open,” I’d argue that wasn’t always the case. Still, some open receivers at times, but didn't always connect: pressure, drops, etc pic.twitter.com/dbILMNWGOt — Ryland Bickley (@_Ryland_B) September 23, 2026 In reference to the clips above: Even though there’s a safety trying to split the difference between Germie Bernard and Freiermuth here, I think the latter would’ve been open downfield regardless. Pressure forced Rodgers to complete the shorter pass to Bernard, which still went for a solid gain. This is a potential tight-window touchdown to Bernard if the ball is thrown towards the corner of the end zone. Instead, pressure in Rodgers’ face has him completing the shorter pass, which still falls incomplete. Rodgers gets thrown off by interior pressure on what’s clearly supposed to be a quick pass play. Metcalf and Wilson are both open immediately after they turn around, but the rhythm isn’t there and scramble drill afterwards is a mess. While not a part of Rodgers’ initial progression, Metcalf does get a step ahead of the cornerback on a boundary go route. Rodgers tries to throw Bernard open on a fade from the slot, but the rookie turns the opposite way of the ball. This should be a routine pitch and catch for a first down. Same as No. 5. Summing everything up, after a performance so poor against the Patriots, it’s reasonable to expect the Steelers not to have anywhere to go but up. The question is just how much more the team can improve. Theoretically, the communication- and chemistry-related issues should improve with time. But with more changes…

summary: Things have not gotten off to a hot start for the Pittsburgh Steelers and their offense. Despite that, ESPN analyst (and brother of Aaron Rodgers) Jordan Rodgers urges fans and media alike to […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - SEPTEMBER 20: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers walks off the field after 20-3 loss against the New England Patriots of the game at Gillette Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images Things have not gotten off to a hot start for the Pittsburgh Steelers and their offense. After a 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots, the Steelers are 31st in scoring and dead last in offensive success rate. Despite that, ESPN analyst (and brother of Aaron Rodgers) Jordan Rodgers urges fans and media alike to be patient with the Steelers. “I think if you truly watched Week 1, this was a team that was a few drops and a few missed calls away from being absolutely explosive like we haven’t seen out of the Steelers in a really long time,” Rodgers said on First Take . “And Rodgers was actually very accurate down the field. The throws that were not completed because of a non-call or that were dropped down the field were on the money.” Jordan acknowledged that his analysis may come off as biased toward his older brother, but added that Aaron and McCarthy are still figuring things out with a skill group that has been limited thus far. “[I’m] not trying to be a homer,” Rodgers said. “Another aspect that I think is still a feeling out process is Rodgers and McCarthy are like that ex you ended up getting back together with after a long time… I think they’re still trying to feel out who they want to be based on what they both are capable of in this second iteration of their relationship. And I think that’s going to take time. Now, they can’t run the football, which doesn’t help. And no one can catch right now and they don’t have Michael Pittman. So it’s back to what it was last year where no one complements DK, he’s not playing as good as he should right now, and they don’t have other options. So I think they’ll get better. Patience.” Unfortunately for the Steelers, they are quickly running out of time to afford to be patient, as they will host the 2-0 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 3. A loss would send them to 1-2 and a full two games back in the division ahead of a trip to Cleveland on a short week. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: Mike McCarthy expresses faith in DK Metcalf after poor start
summary: DK Metcalf’s slow start to the 2026 season has drawn plenty of attention, but Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is not concerned about his star wide receiver. “DK is a pro, I’m very impressed with his professionalism,” McCarthy said Wednesday. The comments come after a frustrating opening two games for Metcalf, who has yet […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - SEPTEMBER 20: DK Metcalf #4 of the Pittsburgh Steelers lines up during a game between the New England Patriots and the Pittsburgh Steelers on September 20, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images DK Metcalf’s slow start to the 2026 season has drawn plenty of attention, but Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is not concerned about his star wide receiver. “DK is a pro, I’m very impressed with his professionalism,” McCarthy said Wednesday. The comments come after a frustrating opening two games for Metcalf, who has yet to find the explosive production Pittsburgh expected when it acquired him. Metcalf has eight receptions for 67 yards through two games, averaging just 8.4 yards per catch without a touchdown. He caught four passes for 40 yards in the season-opening victory over the Atlanta Falcons before finishing with four catches for 27 yards on nine targets in Sunday’s 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots. The struggles have been particularly noticeable because of Metcalf’s reputation as one of the NFL’s premier big-play threats. In Week 1, he had opportunities to make explosive plays down the field but was unable to consistently capitalize Against New England, the issues continued. Metcalf was targeted nine times but averaged only 6.8 yards per reception, while the Steelers offense struggled to generate explosive plays as a whole. He also dropped two passes. Still, McCarthy’s confidence in Metcalf remains clear. Metcalf’s track record suggests a turnaround remains possible. He has recorded three 1,000-yard seasons during his career and entered 2026 with 54 career receiving touchdowns. For the Steelers, the priority is getting more out of an offense that managed just three points against New England. McCarthy acknowledged after the loss that the offense lacked execution and detail, taking responsibility for the unit’s struggles. Let us know what you think in the comments . Plus a couple other impressive plays. 📈📈📈 #Steelers https://t.co/GsBICkjR5u pic.twitter.com/qq7IGX1ASa — Ross McCorkle (@Ross_McCorkle) September 22, 2026 A 6’2, 205-pound safety who ran a blazing 4.32-second 40-yard dash at the 2026 NFL Combine, Spears-Jennings’ athleticism and effort have made him a productive player when it comes to wrangling NFL returners. That hasn’t gone unnoticed by Steelers special teams coach Danny Crossman. Speaking to the media Monday, Crossman praised the Oklahoma product’s contributions. “I think obviously the scouting department and the coaches did a great job of identifying (Spears-Jennings), and more importantly, he came in with a great mindset,” Crossman said. “He came with the mindset of, whatever his role was going to be, he was going to buy in, and he was going to try to be an exceptional player at whatever we asked him to do.” Crossman highlighted how the rookie’s effort has stood out even though he hasn’t seen much time on defense. “(Spears-Jennings) is finding ways to make plays a lot of ways,” Crossman said. “He’s (at the) point of attack, making plays. title: Mike Macdonald, Graham Bensinger address controversial Sean Payton clip from interview
summary: As a famous fictitious news personality once said, “That escalated quickly.” On Tuesday, Mike Macdonald drew arguably the most attention he’s ever received since becoming Seattle Seahawks head coach. A clip from his nearly two-hour interview with Graham Bensinger went viral on social media after he revealed that Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton accused […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 08: Head coach Sean Payton of the Denver Broncos and head coach Mike Macdonald of the Seattle Seahawks shake hands after the game at Lumen Field on September 08, 2024 in Seattle, Washington. The Seahawks defeated the Broncos 26-20. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images As a famous fictitious news personality once said, “That escalated quickly.” On Tuesday, Mike Macdonald drew arguably the most attention he’s ever received since becoming Seattle Seahawks head coach. A clip from his nearly two-hour interview with Graham Bensinger went viral on social media after he revealed that Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton accused the Seahawks of cheating, when in actuality they prepared for their 2024 opener against Denver by scouting plays filmed by Broncos fans at training camp. Macdonald said that the Seahawks had threatened to sue Payton if he went public with his accusations, and Payton eventually backed down. It’s a sensational story punctuated by Macdonald saying that Payton is “not my biggest fan.” It also should’ve never made it to air, evidently. Coach Macdonald addressed the clip at his weekly Wednesday press conference, confirming that that portion of the interview was not meant to be public record. “It’s something that I didn’t intend for public use,” Macdonald said. “Thought it was the most appropriate thing to reach out to Sean and apologize to him for having that end up be public, where it wasn’t meant to. Something that they have to deal with in real-time that wasn’t on their end, that’s where you’re like, ‘Crap.’ It’s a lesson learned. I have to be better in that moment for understanding like, ‘I’m responsible for what I say, no matter the circumstance.’ Whether you’re mic’d up, whether you’re not. Whether you have a certain type of understanding. I fell short in that moment, so it stings for me, but it’s something that I’m going to learn from. It’s a good example that we have to take responsibility for the things we say.” Macdonald indicated that he thought he was just having normal conversation with Bensinger before he thought the cameras were rolling. As far as whether or not the Bensinger production team reached out to him, he said, “It’s not important on all those details. It got out.” The story, of course, doesn’t end here. According to PFT’s Mike Florio , the Seahawks “didn’t even know that portion of the ‘more off than on”’ the record discussion had been recorded until Tuesday morning,” which is when the clip gained traction. The original full-length interview was about 1 hour and 49 minutes, but later that Tuesday it was pulled from Bensinger’s Patreon and re-uploaded at a length of about 1 hour and 44 minutes, omitting the Macdonald-Payton segment. Bensinger, a longtime journalist who’s interviewed many famous athletes and celebrities, released a statement on Wednesday evening . In effect, Bensinger says he provided the video to the Seahawks Public Relations team last week, while stating that Macdonald reached him about the Payton portion of the interview on Tuesday. Due to ongoing media requests for comment, I want to clarify the timeline surrounding a portion of our recent interview with Mike Macdonald that has received attention this week. The complete Mike Macdonald interview, including the conversation now at issue, was provided to Seahawks PR last Wednesday, September 16 – five days before it was published on YouTube Monday. During that time, no concern was raised about the exchange, and we were never asked to remove it. For the last couple of years, our typical practice with long-form interview releases has been to include some of the pre-interview conversation. Coach Macdonald reached out to me directly yesterday morning expressing concern. I immediately told him we would remove that portion, and we did. Unfortunately, it had already been clipped from our interview by online outlets and circulated elsewhere. I told Coach that, in hindsight, I regretted allowing that exchange to be included and that it was my error in judgment. I have tremendous respect for Coach. We spent significant time together in Seattle, and I came away impressed not only by what he has accomplished in such a short period of time, but by the person he is. The last thing I want is for one exchange to overshadow that story. I also have great respect for Sean Payton, whom I had the opportunity to profile previously. For an interview that, prior to its full release, was considered a fascinating look into Macdonald as a coach and a person, it has unfortunately veered into a considerable controversy within the journalism field. By the way, Payton also had his own comments from his press conference prior to Broncos practice. “[Mike] and I are good,” Payton said. “Lord knows, I’ve been in his position where you’re talking about something … and the story is three years ago. Now, I don’t know Mike at that time really, but I know [John Schneider] really well. And, so, I’m sure my initial call to John wasn’t pleasant, but I would say this, in talking with him, it allowed us to figure out how to handle our training camp relative to just videos. “And I don’t think anything was intentional by fans, you know what I mean? But at first, you’re kind of thinking, ‘Man, how could … ?’ And then we did some research online of what was available, and that’s kind of how we changed our policy. “So obviously, I called shooting before I started looking,” Payton added with a laugh. “And I could only do that with John because, again, he’s someone I’ll have a beer with at the combine. I consider him a good friend.” #Broncos HC Sean Payton says he and #Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald are "good" and that the incident actually taught Denver how to better handle training camp with so many videos being made public by fans. “It helped us to some degree. … The conversation last night was good.” https://t.co/6qiadnwHjZ pic.twitter.com/wwZMTSpwsS — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 23, 2026 Just imagine if all of this had unfolded the same week the Seahawks and Broncos square off in Denver in Week 6…

summary: The Seattle Seahawks will be without their starting right guard for at least the next four games. Bradford will not be eligible to return to the field […]
full_text: The Seattle Seahawks will be without their starting right guard for at least the next four games. On Wednesday, the team placed Anthony Bradford on injured reserve, paving the way for safety Rodney Thomas II to go from the practice squad to the active roster. Bradford will not be eligible to return to the field until Week 7 against the Kansas City Chiefs on Oct. 25. Bradford was initially ruled questionable with knee and hip injuries prior to last Sunday’s win over the Arizona Cardinals. Ominously, however, Bradford was downgraded from a limited participant to a non-participant in Friday’s practice, then he was ultimately ruled out altogether the following day . Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald did reiterate that Bradford’s injuries are not season-ending, so he’ll be IR-designated for return. As far as a timetable, he believes it will be on the “shorter side” as opposed to long-term. In other words, closer to the four-week minimum than anything that keeps him out potentially until December, for example. Christian Haynes and fifth-round rookie Beau Stephens split snaps in Bradford’s absence, with Haynes getting 43 snaps to Stephens’ 27. We’ll see if the rotation continues while Bradford is out, or if Haynes will finally be entrusted to start and play an entire game for the first time in his career. It’s a big opportunity for Haynes given the tough start to his career.

title: Seahawks Week 3 power rankings: Seahawks stay atop the mountain thanks to Drew Lock
summary: Entering Week 2, the national media was very high on the Seattle Seahawks, even despite them losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold to a glute injury. Now, after handily defeating the Arizona Cardinals, one would expect the national media to remain high on Seattle. Or will the victories of other Super Bowl contending teams (like the […]
full_text: Entering Week 2, the national media was very high on the Seattle Seahawks , even despite them losing starting quarterback Sam Darnold to a glute injury. Now, after handily defeating the Arizona Cardinals, one would expect the national media to remain high on Seattle. Or will the victories of other Super Bowl contending teams (like the Buffalo Bills or Los Angeles Rams) potentially knock the Seahawks off a peg? Let’s take a look at five national media sites (NFL.com, CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (BR), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Starting with ESPN, the only site (of these five) who don’t have Seattle ranked at number one. ESPN ranks Seattle the second best team in the NFL , the same ranking as last week. In their ranking ESPN credits Drew Lock as “one of the NFL’s best backup QBs.” ESPN further notes that since stepping in for an injured Darnold, Lock has “completed almost 73% of his passes, with four touchdowns, zero turnovers, and only two sacks.” Additionally, Lock’s total QBR of 86.4 currently ranks fourth best in the league. The only team ranked above the Seahawks for ESPN? The Buffalo Bills. CBS Sports and PFT both also credit Lock’s performance as they keep the Seahawks ranked as the number one team in the NFL. CBS Sports notes that a good team is one that can “go on the road and win with a backup quarterback. ” Just as Seattle did last week in Arizona. PFT meanwhile summed up the Seahawks performance with a simple “ No Darnold? No problem .” NFL.com , who also kept Seattle ranked as first, noted that Lock’s impressive performance should allow Seahawk fans to worry less about the absence of Darnold . B/R, who also have Seattle ranked as the number one team in the NFL, also noted that Lock’s performance should allow the team to not feel rushed to get Darnold back to the field . As you have probably noticed, the power rankings – and the reasoning behind their rankings are all pretty cut and paste from all of the polled national media sites. That can be the case when your team is not only the Super Bowl defending champion, but also one of the favorites to win the next Super Bowl. In these moments, power rankings can become very static. As is the case this week. All five of the above national media sites kept the Seahawks at the same ranking as last week. Entering week two, the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.2. Entering Week 3, the same 1.2 average remains. However, this is still the NFL. And despite being an overwhelming top ranked team by the national media, the Seahawks are only one loss (or even one poor performance) away from slipping down these rankings once again. Their next test comes against the Washington Commanders – quarterbacked by Marcus Mariota .

summary: Everybody’s favorite reporter here, G**** C*** wrote today about the 49ers trading for Daron Payne. I’m not sure I’d want a questionable locker room presence like him, but the resident rabble-rouser has a point: it’s time to start scouring for gettable defensive linemen. I was watching the Giants-Rams game and noticed that Kayvon Thibedoux was […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: President of Football Operations and General Manager John Lynch of the San Francisco 49ers on the sideline during the game against the Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. The 49ers defeated the Rams 27-7. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Everybody’s favorite reporter here, G**** C*** wrote today about the 49ers trading for Daron Payne. I’m not sure I’d want a questionable locker room presence like him, but the resident rabble-rouser has a point: it’s time to start scouring for gettable defensive linemen. I was watching the Giants-Rams game and noticed that Kayvon Thibedoux was hard to notice. I wouldn’t give up Mac Jones or a super premium draft pick to get him. There’s a tier of player that might be worth giving up the best QB insurance policy in the entire NFL, but that tier has to be really selective. Those 48 hours over the preseason where Vita Vea seemed tradeable come to mind… that’s the level of game changer the 49ers need. It’s something I’m paying attention to when watching non-49ers NFL games, alongside looking at 49ers opponents and getting a feel for how they’re playing. 49ers place DT CJ West on IR, sign two D-linemen to roster, practice squad “ The placed defensive tackle CJ West, who started the 49ers’ first two games of the season, on injured reserve with a bone chip in his knee, 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said.” Why had 49ers’ CJ West gone south? Severe knee injury provides context for awful opening (paywall) “He had something in (training) camp,” Shanahan said. “I don’t know if this is the same (injury), or if it was something new. But it was bothering him a lot after the game.” West’s injury, which won’t end his season, Shanahan said, is the latest in the 49ers’ defensive trenches.” 49ers Week 2 Tape Takeaways: Protection questions (paywall) “I really want to focus on one play that I think will be fundamental going forward. It’s about protections. The 49ers lost their last Super Bowl due to protection breakdowns against blitzes. They got throttled by Seattle twice because they (1) didn’t have the physicality to run against an imperious front and defensive unit that doesn’t have to adjust personnel to stop it, and (2) Mike Macdonald manipulates offensive line rules and defeats slides. Macdonald is the master of simulated pressures. He has his own, unique pressure packages… …Brock Purdy and Mike Evans combined for an outrageous, off-schedule play. That’s great. The fact that Purdy had no good answer within the design of the play is a problem. This is simulated pressure with—I believe—Cover-8 behind it. Same thing as Cover-6, except quarters is run to the opposite of the passing strength….. Cover-8 is predicated on a four-man rush, and this rushes four, but uses a simulated pressure to break down protection rules. Macdonald has his own variations, including one that’s functionally similar of the play below, but with Cover-3 behind it. Macdonald will also blitz both corners from either edge drop two interior defenders drop into coverage….. Seattle’s front poses physical, schematic, and even technique-oriented answers to the run game. Their personnel allows them to be multiple without sacrificing size. That’s why I’ve talked about left guard so damn much this offseason. I’m dubious of the 49ers’ ability to create any displacement up front. But the other component is having answers to problems. The Seahawks can be beaten, but they use post-snap rotations, simulated pressures and an abundance of different pressure packages to break protection rules with coverages behind them that often account for tendencies of where offenses look for answers. I’m not yet confident that the 49ers will have enough of those answers. That’s why this is a play that should be front of mind from them. It’s not that one of these plays is going to break them down against every team. But if they don’t proactively answer some of these questions, it could do just that against Seattle.” 49ers poach a veteran defensive tackle off the Vikings’ practice squad “Tom Pelissero tweeted that the 49ers are signing veteran Naquan Jones off the Minnesota Vikings practice squad. Jones, 6’3”, 313 pounds, played 177 snaps in 2025 with the Houston Texans and the Los Angeles Chargers. He spent 2023 and 2024 with the Arizona Cardinals. Jones spent the first three years of his career with the Titans. Per Sumer Sports, Jones had 13 tackles with two misses in 2025. He recorded 13 impact plays across 177 snaps. Don’t expect much as a pass rusher. He had only two pressures, with a 3.3% win rate. His run-stop percentage was a bit better at 4.8%….This move also suggests the 49ers did not want to use Sebastian Valdez, Kevin Givens, or McKinnley Jackson — the defensive tackles from the practice squad — in a game setting.” Kyle Shanahan shares updates ahead of 49ers-Cardinals game “ After the game this week, FB Kyle Juszczyk said that the touchdown to Demarcus Week One was impressive because Robinson was the alert on that play and him and TE George Kittle both liked it because they’re often the alert. How common is it to have the player that’s the alert be the targeted receiver? “It’s pretty common. That’s why I hate when wideouts get judged off of stats. The only way you can force a ball to somebody, to me, is by handing it off to them. Or you can just throw into double coverage and avoid the open people. But I mean, we have that on all our plays and you attack certain coverages and if number one’s covered a certain way, it should take you to number two. If they do a certain thing there, then three should be open. That’s why you like a quarterback who can go through those progressions. You like an O-Line who can give them the time to. And you like receivers who run as hard as they can every play, knowing that just because it says alert on a piece of paper, you get a certain coverage and that alert becomes number one very fast. If you think that it’s always just, ‘Hey, they’re forcing the ball here or there,’ when it’s your time, you won’t be ready. We haven’t thrown that route. We haven’t called that concept versus that coverage yet and didn’t get it much in camp either. That’s a credit to how all our guys are and especially D-Rob on that play. He was running his ass off like he was number one and based off that coverage he was.” Why 49ers’ Brock Purdy looks poised for his best season yet “Purdy’s pursuit of his best season began soon after the last campaign ended, when Shanahan and his staff gave their annual “get better” tape for each player to study over the offseason. Purdy’s tape focused on a few foundational principles: not hanging on to big-play reads for too long so the ball can come out quicker and the offense can stay ahead of the chains; understanding when to better use his legs; and knowing when to take shots down the field without being reckless. All of those things showed up during training camp, whether it was on days when he consistently took checkdowns for easy completions or other days when he pushed the ball downfield for big plays. Warner, who had some serious battles against Purdy and the top offense in camp, said the game now seems to move slowly for Purdy. Warner noted Purdy has evolved in the ways he manipulates defenses with cadence and motion, knows every coverage defenses can throw at him and then has the athletic ability and creativity to make a play when things break down.”
author: Yinon Raviv

title: CJ West suffered a bone chip in his knee and is headed to the Injured Reserve
summary: The San Francisco 49ers officially announced the signing of Naquan Jones off the Vikings’ practice squad. The team did the same with wide receiver Brandin Cooks. Cornerback Jakob Robinson was released from the practice squad after the team signed defensive lineman Viliami Fekhoko Jr. That’s because defensive tackle CJ West was placed on injured reserve. […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers officially announced the signing of Naquan Jones off the Vikings’ practice squad. The team did the same with wide receiver Brandin Cooks . Cornerback Jakob Robinson was released from the practice squad after the team signed defensive lineman Viliami Fekhoko Jr. That’s because defensive tackle CJ West was placed on injured reserve. West suffered a bone chip in his knee. Kyle Shanahan said the injury isn’t season-ending, but West will need surgery. “We hope to get him back sometime.” He appeared out of shape in training camp, and just didn’t have the same kind of power he did as a rookie against the run. If he’s been battling through an injury, that explains it. Shanahan said West was battling an injury during camp, but didn’t know if this injury was the same or something new. He did say that the injury was bothering West a lot after the game. The 49ers’ depth went from thin to non-existent, and that was before James Thompson Jr. sustained a high-ankle sprain . With Thompson and West sidelined, Raheem Morris will rely on players who weren’t on the roster a week ago. San Francisco will likely need to elevate another defensive tackle from the practice squad since they only have three healthy bodies. Here’s Shanahan on the depleted depth at defensive tackle: “Any time you have five defensive tackles make the team, and you’re down to two of them through two games, that’s always a concern for anybody. We were able to sign one new guy, and we’ve got three guys on practice squad that’ll be competing to see who is up. We’ve got guys that are in this building. We’ve got to see how those guys step it up.” The 49ers can only bring back eight players from the injured reserve. Thompson and Demarcus Robinson are candidates to land on the IR. Shanahan said those are “likely” to go on the injured reserve. Here are the current players on the list: CB Nate Hobbs (groin) WR Christian Kirk (calf) LB Nick Martin (hamstring) OL Austen Pleasants (knee) EDGE Sam Okuayinonu (foot) WR De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) DT CJ West (knee) The following players will not practice on Wednesday: WR Mike Evans (hip) DT James Thompson Jr. (ankle) WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) EDGE Romello Height (hand) EDGE Nick Bosa (vet day) LB Dre Greenlaw (vet day) RB Christian McCaffrey (vet day) LT Trent Williams ((vet day) Height is still an option to play this week. Shanahan said, “I heard he came out good. There’s an outside chance he can be available.” Shanahan said that as soon as Brandin Cooks shows he’s one of the five receivers ready to play, he’ll be active. But this is the first day of seeing him, so there are no guarantees. Shanahan mentioned that Cooks has a chance to play at some point over the next couple of weeks. It’s just a matter of how quickly he learns the offense and how he looks during practice.
author: Kyle Posey

title: NFL Week 3 power rankings: National media sees the 49ers as a real contender
summary: The 49ers beat up on the Rams in Week 1, and then dominated the Dolphins in Week 2. The offense ran over Los Angeles but went aerial against Miami. There were some concerns about the run defense at times in both games, but if you score enough points, your opponent knows they need to keep […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers beat up on the Rams in Week 1, and then dominated the Dolphins in Week 2. The offense ran over Los Angeles but went aerial against Miami. There were some concerns about the run defense at times in both games, but if you score enough points, your opponent knows they need to keep up on the scoreboard. They cannot do that by running the ball. Today we’ll use multiple power rankings to see how the national media and pundits view the 49ers. Even with all the injuries, it feels like the Niners are getting the respect that they deserve to begin the season. The Athletic: 1 From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall 1. San Francisco 49ers (2-0) Last week : 1 Sunday : Beat Dolphins 35-13 Rookie spotlight : Kaelon Black The running back out of Indiana has more carries and almost as many rushing yards (90) as Christian McCaffrey (91) through two weeks. Not bad for a third-round pick who didn’t even get an invite to the NFL combine. And it helps make Niners fans feel better about losing promising rookie wide receiver De’Zhaun Stribling for 10 weeks due to an ankle sprain. USA Today: 3 From Nate Davis: 3. San Francisco 49ers (2): Only three NFL players in history have scored 50 touchdowns with two different franchises. Hall of Famers Marshall Faulk and Randy Moss and − now − Christian McCaffrey. End of list. Impressive. Yahoo Sports: 3 Frank Schwab : 3. San Francisco 49ers (2-0, LW: 5) The 49ers got a good runout to start the season. They got the Rams in Australia, when Los Angeles practically blew off that trip by landing the day before the game. Then they got the Dolphins, who have the worst roster in the NFL. They blew out both teams, which shouldn’t be taken for granted in the NFL. Their point differential of +42 is dominant. They have had only two negative plays all season, not counting kneeldowns, the fewest for a team this century through two games, according to Doug Clawson of CBS . Brock Purdy is playing well, keeping the offense afloat despite receiver injuries already piling up, and the defense has given up only one touchdown to the Rams and another TD to the Dolphins when they were leading by 29 points in the final minutes. It has been an impressive start. “Obviously, the scoreboard’s been great the last two weeks, but there are so many things we can always get better at and our standard is going to continue to rise. That’s really what we’re focused on.” NFL.com: 7 (9 last week) From Nick Shook : Folks, Brock Purdy is dealing. Defenses have not been able to stop the 26-year-old in the first two weeks. Purdy is at the peak of his powers and completely comfortable running the show, dicing up the opposition and adding his own flair along the way. Quietly, the 49ers are dunking on the doubters, looking like one of the better teams in the NFL through two games. ESPN: 3 Excerpt from Nick Wagoner : Week 2 ranking: 5 One thing we know about the QB1: Brock Purdy looks poised for his best season. Purdy has been one of the league’s most productive quarterbacks since taking over the starting job in 2022. Now in his fifth season, he’s completely comfortable in coach Kyle Shanahan’s offense and is coming off his best training camp. That hot start has teammates such as linebacker Fred Warner openly wondering whether Purdy can compete for league MVP honors. Through two weeks, Purdy is atop the league in QBR (94.9) despite a supporting cast that has already been thinned by injury. If he stays healthy, there’s reason to believe Purdy will post his best year yet. — Nick Wagoner Sporting News: 3 Vinnie Iyer : 3. San Francisco 49ers 2-0 (5) The 49ers are back to being a well-balanced offensive machine for Kyle Shanahan with the usual big plays from Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey. They also need to be extra pleased about how swarming the defense has been under Raheem Morris. CBS Sports: 3 Pete Prisco: The stars continue to show up for this team, which is why it will be a serious playoff contender. With those guys on the field, and Kyle Shanahan coaching, they will be tough to beat. Sports Illustrated: 4 Connor Orr: Last week’s ranking: No. 6 Last week’s result: beat Dolphins, 35–13 This week: vs. Cardinals Sure, the Rams in Australia and the Dolphins at home to follow. But the clinical dissection of both teams was enough to earn Kyle Shanahan & Co. a major boost this week. I keep thinking about something Shanahan has said that makes the team’s sustained run all the more interesting. Nearly every team in the league runs his offense, so every defense practices against it every day. The fact that the 49ers are still an elite team is more amazing than we think.

title: 49ers in review: Are we ignoring concerning signs defensively?
summary: There was no jet lag for the San Francisco 49ers coming home from Australia. San Francisco was rewarded for their travels with a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, and the 49ers took advantage with a 35-13 blowout win at Levi’s Stadium. Before we look ahead to the 49ers Week 3 meeting with the […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images There was no jet lag for the San Francisco 49ers coming home from Australia. San Francisco was rewarded for their travels with a Week 2 matchup against the Miami Dolphins, and the 49ers took advantage with a 35-13 blowout win at Levi’s Stadium. Before we look ahead to the 49ers Week 3 meeting with the Arizona Cardinals, let’s look in the rearview one last time at the Dolphins. Here is Week 2’s game in review: The players returning from injury came up big… Two of the biggest offseason storylines for the 49ers were how long they would be without the likes of Nick Bosa and George Kittle after both suffered season-ending injuries in 2025. The answer to that question was Week 1, as both returned for San Francisco’s season opener in Australia. Week 2 gave us the answer when we could expect them back to their normal form. If you had to pick a player of the game for both sides of the ball for the 49ers in the Week 2 win, there’s a good argument for Kittle to be that player for the offense and Bosa for the defense. Kittle had the more recent injury, tearing his Achilles back in January, but did he look like the Kittle of old on Sunday? His 80 yards led all pass-catchers, and it only took four receptions to get there. His big catch looked every part of the Kittle we got used to, hauling in the Purdy pass and bouncing off of a few tackles en route to his 40-yard gain. Bosa didn’t have the numbers Kittle had (just three tackles), but his impact was certainly felt. He led the 49ers with five pressures, with at least two directly leading to 49ers sacks. While the pressures against Miami were less than what they had against the Rams, the 49ers were able to sack Malik Willis four times, and Bosa’s presence was a huge part of that. It’s good to see the bigger names on the 49ers perform, but it feels just that much better when they are returning from devastating injuries like Kittle and Bosa. …but the Demarcus Robinson injury might be just as big When the 49ers lost Ricky Pearsall to injury, De’Zhaun Stribling was starting his rise, sliding in as Pearsall’s replacement. When Stribling went down in Australia, the veteran Robinson was the obvious solution to slide into that WR2 spot. But now with Robinson out for a bit with the high ankle sprain, where do the 49ers go from here? Deebo Samuel is the next obvious answer, but we have seen what Samuel looks as a WR2 and it leaves a bit to be desired. Samuel feels better as a luxury to this San Francisco offense, a player you can use out of want instead of need, instead of having a defined role like the second-most important receiver on the team. So where do the 49ers look to replace Robinson for the next few weeks while he recovers? Well, the 49ers added Brandin Cooks to the practice squad, so that’s a veteran presence. But that doesn’t exactly solve the issue. The 49ers will likely enter Week 3 with a receiver depth chart of Mike Evans, Samuel, Jacob Cowing, and Jordan Watkins, leaving a pretty heavy gap between Samuel and Cowing in terms of talent and experience. Wide receiver injuries were a recurring thing in 2025, and it seems to have returned for 2026. Let’s see how the 49ers handle it this season and try to fix the issue by making some sort of addition, or if they try to ride it out. Can I be honest for a second? This is my corner of the internet so I am sure I can overreact to a Week 2 game against the Dolphins without people getting angry about it. But I wasn’t exactly thrilled with what I saw from the 49ers defense on Sunday. I know, I know, they only allowed 13 points and fewer than 300 yards, but it didn’t feel as dominating a performance as it should have been. Now, I will say, they cleaned up in the second half, but the first half certainly had its share of issues; the biggest was not being able to get off the field. The 49ers offense only had two possessions in the first half, and that’s because the defense couldn’t get off the field. Miami’s first-half drives were: 9 plays, 34 yards 17 plays, 63 yards 12 plays, 58 yards Miami converted five-of-seven third- and fourth-down conversions in the first half, including an extra conversion when a Keion White roughing the passer wiped out a Willis incomplete pass on a third down. The subpar Dolphins offense was moving the ball at will against the 49ers, a week removed from San Francisco shutting down the Rams. It wasn’t exactly how you’d want the defense to follow up the Week 1 performance. The two things I will say is that the defense only allowed field goals in the first half and played a much better second half. Maybe it was just an off half for the defense, but it was something to note and something to watch going forward. Rookie of the Week After Kaelon Black would have won the award in Week 1, we will go to the defense to crown Week 2’s winner. And the first official winner of the inaugural Rookie of the Week is defensive tackle, Gracen Halton. The 49ers defensive tackle situation is kind of a black hole, with it led by Osa Odighizuwa, but beyond him, it’s a cluster of prove-it players. Halton got 32 snaps (the most from a 49ers defensive tackle not named Osa Odighizuwa) on Sunday and put together a solid performance. The rookie finished with five tackles (the most by a 49ers defensive lineman on Sunday), with three being solo and another going for a loss. The tackle for a loss came late in the 49ers blowout, but Halton stopped De’Von Achane for a loss of three to force a third down early in the fourth quarter. But Halton was quality in the run game as well. He finished with three run stops, adding an Achane stop for a gain of one yard in the second quarter and holding another Achane run to three yards in addition to the tackle for loss. And the 49ers’ run defense looked better against Miami than it did against Los Angeles (although Miami still rushed for more than 100 yards). With as much help as defensive tackle needs, any positive performance is helpful. Halton was the one to offer that performance on Sunday, and it was a good one to see come from a rookie.
author: Andrew Pasquini

title: Why starting 3-0 matters for the 49ers
summary: Several historical trends favor 2-0 teams that start 3-0. That’s what the San Francisco 49ers are striving for this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. A loss for an undefeated team in Week 2 is hardly a death knell, as those teams have still made the playoffs at nearly a 62% clip over the past 10 […]
full_text: (Photo by Robin Alam/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Several historical trends favor 2-0 teams that start 3-0. That’s what the San Francisco 49ers are striving for this Sunday against the Arizona Cardinals. A loss for an undefeated team in Week 2 is hardly a death knell, as those teams have still made the playoffs at nearly a 62% clip over the past 10 years. But a Week 3 win that takes you to 3-0 puts you in the same group, and those teams have made the playoffs 73.3% of the time, according to a 10-year study . Even better, you have a 44.4% shot at the division and a 20% shot at the Super Bowl. That’s right, a one-in-five chance. History is on the 49ers’ side if they win. It’s a club you want to be a part of. Only 45 teams reached 3-0 in a decade, and three of the last 10 Super Bowl champions were among them. The Seattle Seahawks also fall under this same category. Seattle takes on the Washington Commanders, who are expected to have Marcus Mariota under center. The Niners and Seahawks are headed for a collision course in a couple of weeks where both teams could enter Week 5 undefeated. The odds to win the division if you fall to 2-1 only drop roughly 5%. Interestingly enough, 2-1 teams have been more likely to reach the Divisional Round than 3-0 teams (by 4%), but it’s drastically different once you get into the final two rounds of the playoffs. Those 3-0 teams have a 31.1% chance of making the conference championship, compared to a 17.3% chance with a 2-1 record. The 2018 Patriots are the only Super Bowl champions in the previous ten years to start 1-2. But five of the last six have started 2-1, with the 3-0 Rams as the exception in 2021. What matters for the 49ers is that a Week 3 win, historically, is a fast track to the playoffs.

title: Should the 49ers be active ahead of the trade deadline?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers are turning over every leaf in an effort to keep the roster competitive as they battle attrition. After a slew of injuries […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. The San Francisco 49ers are turning over every leaf in an effort to keep the roster competitive as they battle attrition. After a slew of injuries at wide receiver, the latest move was to add veteran Brandin Cooks, who most recently played for the Buffalo Bills and New Orleans Saints in 2025. Cooks was signed to the practice squad . If Cooks is active while Demarcus Robinson is out, that is probably not a great sign for Jordan Watkins, who was inactive in the first two weeks of the season behind KhaDarel Hodge, a player the team signed in August. Kyle Shanahan is hopeful Christian Kirk can return to practice next week, but there are no guarantees. Until Robinson and Kirk return, the 49ers will likely lean on Hodge, Jacob Cowing, and Cooks. Realistically, that likely means more Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, and Mike Evans. Should the Niners be active at the deadline? Wide receiver isn’t the only position the 49ers are leaky at. Defensive tackle James Thompson Jr. also has a high-ankle sprain . Surprisingly, the 49ers didn’t work out any defensive tackles this week before they return to practice. That means they are going to roll with the bodies they have on the roster. Keion White might need to play more. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris could also lean into more 5-man fronts, where Jaden Dugger sees more snaps. Morris has his work cut out for him for at least a couple of more weeks, until Mykel Williams is eligible to return. Williams will solve quite a few of the Niners’ problems, but it’s unfair to expect him to hit the ground running after a serious season-ending knee injury. Not every athlete will return like they never left, as Nick Bosa has. That led us to our weekly survey question: Do the Niners need to make a move ahead of the deadline to stay competitive? Are you feeling confident in the Niners? Despite the injuries, the 49ers are 2-0 and look like one of the teams to beat to begin the season. What is your confidence level in the team through two weeks? Are you buying, or do we need to pump the brakes and revisit this question in a couple of weeks from now after the Niners run into a couple of playoff defenses?
